author: takashi-matsuyama
body:
## What

A **no-code composer** for the parametric patterns introduced in slice 2a (#30), in the sidebar. This is the visible half of Phase 2: users can now create, edit, save, share, and assign their own per-band visual patterns.

- **Library bar** — new / duplicate / rename / delete, backed by `localStorage` (`spectrum-chisel-patterns`), seeded with starter patterns.
- **Single-layer editor** — primitive (`point/line/polygon/ring`) and layout (`single/radial`) pickers, count/radius/size/sides sliders, and **dropdown-only modulation routing** (source/target/curve + gain). No free-text, no code.
- **Per-band picker** — assign any library pattern to a band, or `(built-in)` to revert to its draw style.
- **Idle preview** — draws the open pattern on a clean canvas for immediate feedback; never wipes accumulated art (skipped once history exists).

### Identity & rewiring

Editing recomputes the content-addressed id and **rewires the bands that referenced the old id**, so the *name* is the stable UX handle while the *id* stays the stable render handle. `loadPreset` re-syncs the composer + per-band pickers **explicitly** (p5 `.value()` fires no change event). Delete asks for confirmation.

### i18n

Structural labels/buttons/alerts are keyed (en/ja); technical param labels (Count, Radius, …) and enum tokens stay English in both locales, per the existing convention.

## Verification

- Gates: `pnpm test` 58/58, `typecheck`, `lint`, `build` (precache 12; composer in the bundle).
- **Composer UI smoke (headless)**: starters seed + persist (localStorage), the per-band picker assigns a custom pattern (`drawCustomPattern` + `patternLibrary` in params), **editing rewires the assigned band** (id `peybb`→`pggs1dz`, band follows), and the assignment renders (idle preview + live).
- **2a round-trip re-checked**: viewer still reconstructs a custom pattern from params alone — no regression.

## Deferred to 2c

`strokeWeight`/`alpha`/`hueShift`/`jitter` targets, `frameCount` source, multi-layer authoring UI, SVG export-size guard, and preset graceful-degrade notices.

Stacked on #30 (now merged); rebased onto main.

body:
## What

Add defense-in-depth `is_unlimited_quota()` guards inside burn-rate and budget-mode functions so they self-protect regardless of caller state.

## Why

When `unlimited_quota: true` is configured, burn-rate warnings and budget-exhaustion pauses could still fire if `_get_budget_mode()` raised an exception — the fallback defaulted to `"session_only"`, bypassing all downstream `_budget_mode == "disabled"` guards. This also supersedes #2003 whose changes are included here.

## How

Three targeted changes in `iteration_manager.py`:

1. `_maybe_warn_burn_rate()` — early return when `is_unlimited_quota()` is True
2. `_downgrade_if_burning_fast()` — early return when `is_unlimited_quota()` is True
3. `_budget_mode` exception fallback — checks `is_unlimited_quota()` before defaulting to `"session_only"`

Each function now independently verifies unlimited quota status rather than relying solely on the caller's `_budget_mode` variable.

## Testing

3 new tests + full suite (14843 passed, 1 pre-existing skip, 1 pre-existing orphan skill failure unrelated).

body:
Closes #1302

### Why  (problem & intent)
`make security` (target `security-agents`) ran the SDK `pip-audit` without the `--ignore-vuln PYSEC-2026-196` flag that CI uses at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:666`, so it exited rc=2 locally on a transient `pip 26.1.1` false positive (uv pulls pip into an ephemeral audit env; zynax-sdk does not ship pip, and the tools image already pins `pip==26.1.2`). CI was green, local was red — pure Makefile↔CI drift, not a shipped vulnerability. This advances EPIC Q (#1172): `make ci` green on a clean checkout.

### What you'll get  (deliverables ↔ what changed)
- `make security` exits 0 on a clean checkout with the current tools image ← `Makefile` (`security-agents` SDK `pip-audit` now `--ignore-vuln PYSEC-2026-196`)
- Makefile and ci.yml share one ignore policy — no further drift ← `Makefile` line matches `ci.yml:666` exactly

### Scope & boundaries
- **In scope:** the single SDK `pip-audit` invocation in `security-agents` (one line in `Makefile`).
- **Out of scope (deferred):** the per-example-agent audits — CI does NOT pass `--ignore-vuln` there (ci.yml:677), so the Makefile loop is intentionally left unchanged. N/A otherwise.

### Test plan & acceptance

| Acceptance criterion | How verified (command) | Result |
|----------------------|------------------------|--------|
| `make security` exits 0 on a clean checkout with the current tools image | `make security` | ✅ rc=0 — `No known vulnerabilities found, 1 ignored` (SDK pip-audit) |
| Makefile and ci.yml use the same ignore/pin policy (no drift) | diff of `Makefile:327` vs `ci.yml:666` | ✅ both `uv run pip-audit --ignore-vuln PYSEC-2026-196` |

**Local gates:** `make security` ✅

### Evidence
- **CI:** all required checks green (see this PR's run).
- **Local output:** `make security` → `rc=0`; SDK audit prints `No known vulnerabilities found, 1 ignored` (PYSEC-2026-196 ignored, matching CI).
- **Artifacts / images:** none — no service source changed; `Makefile` only.
- **Post-merge digest sync → main:** N/A — no image rebuild.

### Risk & rollback
Low — single-line change to a developer-facing make target; no behaviour change to CI or any shipped artifact. Rollback = revert this PR.

### Review aids
One file, one line: `Makefile` `security-agents` target. The change makes the local SDK audit match `ci.yml:666` verbatim. Note the per-example-agent loop is deliberately unchanged to mirror CI's per-agent audits, which do not ignore.

author: proestimateio
body:
## Drive sync — Phase 5 (document routing) + Phase 7 (migrations)

Builds on [#152](https://github.com/coen-gpt/coenconstruction.com/pull/152). **Additive, flag-gated / dry-run-default** — zero production behavior change until `drive_sync_enabled` is on and an admin explicitly runs a migration.

### Phase 5 — App → Drive document routing
- **`driveFileDocument`** — files a record's stored document into the correct job subfolder per the routing table (`slotForSource`). Idempotent (dedupes by a source-hash in `appProperties`, kept within Drive's 124-byte value limit). Fetches Base44 `file_url` bytes **or** accepts inline base64; provisions the folder tree on demand; optionally writes `drive_file_url` back to the source record. `gated:true` respects the master flag.
- **`fileDocumentsSafe()`** (`src/lib/driveFileClient.js`) wired into the in-app document manager (`ProjectDocuments`) — uploaded job docs mirror to Drive, fire-and-forget, can't break the upload.

### Phase 7 — migrations (`dryRun:true` by **default**, admin-only, never delete)
- **`migrateStandardizeSubfolders`** — adds any missing of the 8 subfolders to existing job folders. Chunked + time-bounded.
- **`migrateNormalizeCities`** — merges duplicate/case/trailing-space city folders into the canonical (moves children), fixes names, sweeps stray root files to `_UNSORTED`. (Uses the tested `planCityMerges`.)
- **`migrateBackfillProjects`** — links existing Drive job folders to matching `ContractorProject`s (city + street/name). Unmatched folders are **queued for review** (reported), only auto-created with an explicit `create_unmatched:true`; test/system folders are flagged, never created.

### Verification
363 unit tests green, eslint clean, all Drive functions esbuild-syntax-OK, `vite build` passes.

### Recommended sequence (why not merge-and-forget)
This phase is real Drive I/O that **can't be exercised until Drive is connected**. Suggested order:
1. Merge #152's deploy → **Connect Google Drive → Self-test** (proves the Drive client against your Shared Drive).
2. Merge this PR + enable `drive.config`.
3. Run each migration **`dryRun` first**, review the JSON report, then `dryRun:false`. Recommend active jobs before historical.

> Deliberate follow-up: per-finalize-point hooks for the **ephemeral** proposal/contract PDFs (`emailEstimateToCustomer` / `processApproval`) — they're never stored, so they must be captured at PDF-generation time. Best done once the live foundation is verified.

## Intent

Complete the derived decode-step slice for middle reserved binary layouts. A codec with `derive decode` can now use the generated schema decode-step helper for the already-supported visible `UIntN`, middle `ReservedBits`, visible `UIntN` storage-unit shape.

## Consequences

The derived codec boundary now preserves the generated helper behavior for successful decode, short-input readiness, and reserved-bit mismatch diagnostics. The completed slice is promoted into the current specification and executable specification catalog, while the proposal text is narrowed so it no longer describes this behavior as future work.

## Risks

The main compatibility risk is diagnostic projection through the JVM runtime for source-visible `DecodeError` values. The new executable specification covers the reserved field path and byte offset to keep that behavior pinned.

author: mavenrain
body:
## Challenge 16: Verify the safety of `core::iter` adapters

Towards challenge #16 (tracking issue #280).  Adds Kani harnesses for the unsafe
methods and safe abstractions in `library/core/src/iter/adapters/`.

This revision answers the 2026-08-15 review (feliperodri: CHANGES_REQUESTED,
blockers F-B1 unbounded and F-B2 generic `T`, plus notes F-N1..F-N5; Copilot:
the same points inline, plus the enumerate.rs doc comment).  Section "Response
to review" below goes item by item.  Section "std code changes" lists every
line changed outside the `#[cfg(kani)] mod verify` modules.  Section "Harness
inventory" lists every harness with its bound and element types.  Section
"Known upstream findings" lists the two defects the harnesses found in the
current upstream code and how the harness domains exclude them.

### Unsafe methods (proven free of UB)

| adapter | unsafe methods |
|---|---|
| `cloned` | `__iterator_get_unchecked`, `next_unchecked` |
| `copied` | `__iterator_get_unchecked` |
| `enumerate` | `__iterator_get_unchecked` |
| `fuse` | `__iterator_get_unchecked` |
| `map` | `__iterator_get_unchecked`, `next_unchecked` |
| `skip` | `__iterator_get_unchecked` (plain source, and a `MAY_HAVE_SIDE_EFFECT = true` source) |
| `zip` | `__iterator_get_unchecked`, and `ZipImpl::get_unchecked` directly over arbitrary valid `Zip` state |

The `__iterator_get_unchecked` harnesses read at a symbolic in-bounds index
(`kani::any_where(|i| i < size_hint().0)`) over a `kani::any()` backing array;
the `next_unchecked` harnesses establish the non-empty precondition by
construction.

### Safe abstractions (proven free of UB)

`array_chunks::next_back_remainder` and `array_chunks::fold`,
`copied::spec_next_chunk`, `filter::next_chunk_dropless`,
`filter_map::next_chunk`, the `map_windows` `Buffer` operations (`as_array_ref`,
`as_uninit_array_mut`, `push`, `drop`), `step_by::original_step`,
`take::spec_fold` and `take::spec_for_each`, and `zip::next` / `next_back` /
`nth` / `fold` / `spec_fold`.

### Approach

- Harnesses live in a `#[cfg(kani)] mod verify` at the end of each adapter file.
- Because Kani cannot attach a `proof_for_contract` to a generic trait method
  (kani#1997), each generic method is instantiated at representative concrete
  element types via macros, with the caller precondition established by
  construction rather than as a `#[requires]`.
- The representative element types are unit (ZST), `u8` (1-byte), `char` (4-byte,
  validity-constrained), compound tuples with padding such as `(char, u8)` and
  `(u32, i16)`, and, where a code path is gated on `needs_drop`, a `DropToken`
  type with a real destructor; `zip` harnesses pair two of them.
- The per-element loops in the production code that the harnesses drive carry
  `#[safety::loop_invariant(...)]` (the repo's loop-contract spelling, already
  used on plain `for` loops in `slice/mod.rs`, `str/pattern.rs`,
  `num/dec2flt/decimal_seq.rs`), so the iterating harnesses have no
  `#[kani::unwind]` for those loops and the slice length is symbolic instead of
  unrolled.  The invariants bound only the loop counter, because the loop
  frame Kani infers (or, for `array_chunks`, the frame stated with
  `kani::loop_modifies`) writes only the counter and the accumulator, so every
  size relation the body needs survives as an entry value.  Where a loop
  cannot take a contract (it calls `next` on a generic inner iterator, or it
  lives in the generic `Iterator::try_fold` default), the harness stays
  bounded and the code comment says why.
- No loop changed shape.  Every production hunk is an added attribute, an
  added `#[cfg(kani)]` import, or an added comment.

### Response to review

#### F-B1: unbounded verification

Status: the production loops that the harnesses drive now carry
`#[safety::loop_invariant]`, and the corresponding harnesses have no
`#[kani::unwind]` for those loops (an unwind attribute is kept only where a
sibling construct with a length-independent trip count needs one, stated per
row).  23 loop-contract harnesses (`take` 8, `array_chunks` 4, `zip` 11:
`fold` x4, `nth` x4, `nth` side-effect x3) run with a symbolic slice length
and no unrolling depth on the contracted loop.
Two adapters (`filter`, `filter_map`) and four narrow
`array_chunks`/`zip`/`skip` paths stay bounded, for the reasons below.  Local
run status is in "Verification status".

Now verified by a loop invariant on the production loop:

| production loop | invariant | harnesses (unwind attribute) |
|---|---|---|
| `take.rs` `SpecTake::spec_fold` (TrustedRandomAccess impl), `for i in 0..end` | `kani::index <= end` | `check_take_spec_fold_unit`, `check_take_spec_fold_u8`, `check_take_spec_fold_char`, `check_take_spec_fold_tup` (none) |
| `take.rs` `SpecTake::spec_for_each` (TrustedRandomAccess impl), `for i in 0..end` | `kani::index <= end` | `check_take_spec_for_each_unit`, `check_take_spec_for_each_u8`, `check_take_spec_for_each_char`, `check_take_spec_for_each_tup` (none) |
| `array_chunks.rs` `SpecFold::fold` (TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce impl), `while inner_len - i >= N` | `i <= inner_len`, with `#[cfg_attr(kani, kani::loop_modifies(&accum, &i))]` | `check_array_chunks_fold_unit`, `check_array_chunks_fold_u8`, `check_array_chunks_fold_char`, `check_array_chunks_fold_tup` (none) |
| `zip.rs` `ZipImpl::fold` (TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce impl), `for i in 0..len` | `kani::index <= len` | `check_zip_fold_unit`, `check_zip_fold_u8`, `check_zip_fold_char_u8`, `check_zip_fold_tup` (none) |
| `zip.rs` `ZipImpl::nth` (TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce impl), `while self.index < end` | `self.index <= end` | `check_zip_nth_unit`, `check_zip_nth_u8` (`unwind(3)`), `check_zip_nth_char_u8`, `check_zip_nth_tup` (`unwind(12)`), `check_zip_nth_side_effect_a`, `check_zip_nth_side_effect_b`, `check_zip_nth_side_effect_both` (`unwind(3)`).  The unwind attribute covers only `super_nth`, which runs at most one iteration after the contracted loop has consumed `min(n, len - index)` items, and (for `char` and the tuple) the element-wise `kani::any` construction of the `MAX_LEN` backing arrays; neither count depends on the slice length. |

Why the invariants only bound the counter.  The loop frame that Kani's loop
contract machinery infers for these loops is `{acc, i}` (or `{accum, i}`, or
`{self.index}` for `zip::nth`): `end`, `len`, `self.iter`, `self.a`, `self.b`
are not havoced, so `end <= self.iter.size()` and
`end <= self.len <= min(a.size(), b.size())` stay available to the body as
entry values and do not need restating.  A method call on the captured `self`
inside the invariant (for example `self.iter.size() == ...`) is not something
the current Kani/CBMC pipeline evaluates (it becomes a nondeterministic
value), so the counter-only form is both sufficient and the only form that
proves.  For `array_chunks::fold` the frame is stated explicitly with
`kani::loop_modifies(&accum, &i)` (precedent: `slice/mod.rs`), because the
`from_fn` closure borrows `self` mutably and the inferred frame would
otherwise havoc the whole adapter, `remainder` included.  Each production
comment says this.

What "unbounded" means here, stated precisely: the loop is verified by
invariant (CBMC havocs the loop frame and checks the invariant inductively),
so no unrolling depth truncates the number of iterations.  The slice length is
still a symbolic value in `0..=MAX_LEN` where `MAX_LEN` is the size of the
`kani::any()` backing array.  For the loop-contract harnesses `MAX_LEN` is
`isize::MAX` for the ZST (every length a Rust slice can have; 50 for the
`zip` pair, whose two arrays are separate allocations), `u32::MAX` for `u8`,
and 10 for `char` and the padded tuples.  The 10 is a solver-time choice, not
a proof-structure one: the loop is the same monomorphic code at every
`MAX_LEN`, and the cost that scales with `MAX_LEN` for the wide types is the
element-wise `kani::any` construction of the backing array under the
loop-contract (DFCC) transformation, not the loop.  The ZST and `u8`
ins

author: vivekmaru
body:
🚨 **Severity:** CRITICAL
💡 **Vulnerability:** A Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability was present in the proxy endpoint. The target upstream URL was constructed using raw string concatenation without stripping leading slashes or user-info markers from the requested path. This allowed an attacker to shift the URL authority (e.g. using `//malicious.com` or `@malicious.com`) bypassing origin mismatch checks and forcing the backend to proxy arbitrary requests to unauthorized servers.
🎯 **Impact:** If exploited, this could allow an attacker to make arbitrary backend HTTP requests, potentially accessing internal endpoints, scanning internal networks, or bypassing network restrictions.
🔧 **Fix:** Changed the proxy route URL construction to explicitly strip any leading forward slashes from the incoming tail path before joining it with a single `/` to the base URL. This ensures the parsed origin strictly remains the intended upstream origin.
✅ **Verification:** Verified that `app.all("/proxy/*")` correctly parses and enforces the origin constraint, and all `pnpm test` cases pass.

## Phase 13, unit 5b — LLM provider + model REST CRUD

The operator-facing admin surface under `/api` to manage providers, their weighted keys, and model aliases (the Console wires to these next). The stores were already wired into `Deps` by 5a; this adds handlers + routes + tests + smoke.

### What's here
- **`handlers_llm_providers.go`** — `/api/llm/providers` CRUD + `/{name}/keys` add/list/delete. Key ids auto-mint a ULID.
- **`handlers_llm_models.go`** — `/api/llm/models` CRUD (alias → provider+model).
- **`router.go`** — routes gated on `d.LLMProviders` / `d.LLMModels`. Reads require auth; **writes require the admin umbrella scope**.
- DTOs marshal `config`/`default_params` (object) ↔ JSON string, `model_allowlist`/`capabilities` (array) ↔ JSON string.
- **Tests** — provider+key+model CRUD round-trips, admin-required (403), invalid-JSON (400), missing-fields (400), not-found (404), under `-race`, with functional map-backed fakes (no sqlite import, §13).
- **`scripts/smoke/phase-13.sh`** — 8 new live checks (provider create→round-trip, model create→round-trip).

### Note: orchestrator-built
The autonomous loop wedged on this unit hitting the documented **write-truncation** failure mode — NIM (a verbose reasoning model) emitted a single `write` for the whole large handler file, the tool-call JSON was cut off mid-string, and it spun ~32 min producing nothing. author: borisbat
body:
Followup to #3175 — final item of the 64-bit container sweep.

## Problem

The byte-buffer `Stream` API truncated 64-bit sizes/counts at the boundary, even though the pipe internals (`deque<vector<uint8_t>>`) are already `size_t`:
- `Stream::push(const uint8_t*, uint32_t size)` — a single buffer > 4 GB truncates.
- `Stream::pushBatch(const uint8_t* const*, const uint32_t* sizes, int count)` — a per-item size > 4 GB truncates; > INT_MAX items truncates.
- `streamPushBatch` built a `vector<uint32_t> sizes` and passed `(int)data.size`.
- `invoke_stream_block(..., uint32_t size, ...)` (pop side) + the 3 `(uint32_t)item.size()` casts.

## Fix (widen the Stream API to 64-bit)

- `Stream::push` size → `uint64_t`.
- `Stream::pushBatch` sizes → `const uint64_t*`, count → `int64_t` (loop counter `int64_t`).
- `invoke_stream_block` size → `uint64_t`; dropped the `(uint32_t)` casts on `item.size()` (`size_t` → `uint64_t`).
- `streamPushBatch`: `vector<uint64_t> sizes`, `uint64_t` loop counter, `int64_t(data.size)`.
- `aot_builtin_jobque.h` `Stream` declarations updated to match.

The das-bound functions (`streamPush` / `streamPushBatch` / `streamPop`) are **unchanged** — they take `TArray` and call the internal `Stream` methods — so there's no das-API or AOT-prototype change (das2rst produced no doc churn).

## Test

A true >4 GB-buffer / >2 G-batch repro isn't CI-feasible, so no new test (same as the foreach/fio PRs). Validated normal behavior: `tests/jobque/test_jobque_stream.das` (20/20), `test_jobque_channels.das` (19/19), and the full suite (10291, 0 failed).

## Scope notes (follow-ups)

Two adjacent int-bounded jobque APIs left out (separate decisions):
- `Stream::total()` returns `(int)pipe.size()` — a das-facing queue-depth count accessor (category-1).
- `Channel::push` / `Channel::pushBatch` — the typed-message path, takes `int count`.

body:
Stacked on **#8** (`ramiro/paid-media-optimizer`) — base this PR's diff against that branch.

## What
Adds data-calibrated **per-portfolio objectives** to the budget optimizer engine.
Each portfolio declares an objective — `purchase | app_install | signup | lead |
traffic | awareness` — and the engine resolves the matching calibrated profile.

## Additive by design
With no objective set, `DEFAULT_CONFIG` reproduces the Excel behaviour exactly — the
fidelity tests are unchanged. A profile only activates the generalized path.

## Changes
- **types / objectives.ts** — optional KPI fields (`leads, appInstalls, signups,
  landingPageViews, reach`) + `OptimizationObjective`; `OBJECTIVE_PROFILES` (kpiField,
  per-trajectory weights, gamma, asymmetric velocity caps, significance gate, EWMA).
- **config** — `applyObjectiveProfile` + `resolveConfig` folds the profile *before* the
  explicit override (precedence: profile → portfolio → review).
- **scoring** — window score generalized to `events / spend` on the profile KPI
  (awareness ≈ impressions/$); significance gate counts KPI events; EWMA smoothing of
  the composite across cycles.
- **engine** — asymmetric velocity caps; learning phase keeps the −8% down-cap as an
  additional floor. `classify` / `triggers` / scale-mode target count the objective KPI
  (default purchases), so non-purchase portfolios aren't mis-classified or false-paused.
- **ingest.ts** — Meta export/API field → `WindowMetrics` mapping.
- **schemas** — new optional window fields + `OptimizationObjectiveSchema`.
- **FE plumbing** — typed `objective`, threaded through `runPortfolioCycle` + the API
  route, objective-aware CPI, `OBJECTIVE_LABELS` for display, sample data normalised.

## Tests
20 pass (12 existing + 8 new): per-KPI scoring, asymmetric caps + learning floor,
significance gate, EWMA blend, conservation across all six objectives, ingest mapping.
`bun run build` passes.

author: gmankey
body:
Documentation-only. Lands three ADR records onto canonical `staging`. No code, no contract changes.

## ADR-0037 — V4/V4.1 cadence-drift defect (new)
Skipped/empty rounds reopen at `now + roundDurationSec` (24h) instead of the next fixed calendar slot, violating ADR-0001/0010's calendar-anchored, self-healing schedule. Surfaced when V4.1-B burned 4 empty rounds in 4 days. Inherited verbatim from V2; the real root cause is a false claim in ADR-0004. Immutable in the deployed contracts → accepted as a documented defect for V4/V4.1, and a **hard calendar-anchored gate for V5** (ADR-0036), with a drift-simulation test required before V5 mainnet.

## ADR-0004 — retraction
Removes the incorrect "confirms ADR-0001's fixed schedule self-heals skips" line. The skip path rolls the schedule forward 24h; it does not re-anchor. Points to ADR-0037.

## ADR-0038 — V5 plain-MON denomination (new)
V5 retired tickets (ADR-0036) without pinning the replacement display unit. Decision: **denominate everything users see in MON** (the on-chain principal is already MON-denominated; no contract change). No ticket/credit abstraction, no raw shMON share counts, and — per operator — **no proactive shMON "your token count went down" disclaimers**; customer support owns that question. Includes a "do not re-add disclaimers" note for future sessions.

Branched from `origin/staging`; diff is exactly these three files (ADR-0036 untouched).

author: bobmatnyc
body:
# trusty-review hardening batch (0.3.12 → 0.3.13)

One coordinated PR bundling five independent fixes, all touching `trusty-review`,
sharing a single version bump (0.3.12 → 0.3.13). Each fix is its own commit.

Closes #1241, #1233, #1312, #1234. Fixes the #1343 runtime residual.

---

## FIX 1 (lead) — #1343 runtime residual in `verify.rs::rederive_verdict`

**Symptom:** a real PR review returned inner review_body APPROVE/A- but outer
structured APPROVE*/C+.

**Root cause:** `rederive_verdict` path (a2) hard-coded the baseline to
`Verdict::ApproveWithReservations` (APPROVE*) whenever ANY non-High finding was
CONFIRMED — including a low-effort `praise` finding. Then
`derive_verdict(APPROVE*, survivors)=APPROVE*` and
`clamp_grade_to_verdict(A-, APPROVE*)=C+`, bypassing the source-of-truth
reconciliation in `grade.rs::derive_verdict` (the #1343 fix).

**Fix:** path (a2) now takes the **severity-min** of `(primary_verdict, APPROVE*)`
via a new `verdict_min` helper.
- primary REQUEST_CHANGES/BLOCK still caps **down** to APPROVE* (#1015 behavior preserved);
- primary clean APPROVE **stays** APPROVE — a confirmed praise/low-effort finding
  can neither harden the verdict nor downgrade the grade. This mirrors the
  source-of-truth reconciliation `grade.rs` already applies.
- A confirmed **High-effort** finding still escalates via path (a).

`verify.rs`: `rederive_verdict`, new `verdict_min` / `verdict_ord`.
Tests: `rederive_confirmed_praise_keeps_clean_approve` (exact runtime case:
APPROVE/A- + confirmed confidence=1.0 praise → stays APPROVE, grade stays A-),
`rederive_confirmed_high_effort_still_escalates_from_approve` (guard: High still escalates).

## FIX 2 — #1241 safety: fail-CLOSED (UNKNOWN) on parse failure / truncation

**PM decision (ticket > spec precedence):** #1241 **supersedes** spec REV-130's
fail-OPEN APPROVE. A silent APPROVE on unparseable/truncated output posts a green
GitHub check for a review that never happened — a safety hole. Fail CLOSED to UNKNOWN.

- **2a** `parser.rs`: `ParsedReview::fail_safe` now sets `Verdict::Unknown`;
  unrecognised verdict tokens inside otherwise-valid JSON also resolve to UNKNOWN.
  Verified UNKNOWN flow: GitHub posting always uses the `COMMENT` event (never an
  API-level APPROVE), so UNKNOWN posts an advisory "could not review" comment and
  **no green check**. UNKNOWN already short-circuits verification and is preserved
  by `derive_verdict` — no downstream change needed.
- **2b** `runner.rs`: LLM-error path fails closed to UNKNOWN; new `is_truncated`
  guard converts a completion at ≥95% of the output-token ceiling to UNKNOWN
  **before** trusting the (likely incomplete) parse. `max_tokens` is threaded out
  of the request for the comparison.
- **2c** `prompt.rs`: `max_tokens_for_model` raises the Gemini ceiling to 8192 so
  its verbose structured JSON isn't truncated.
- **2d** `openrouter.rs`: `cost_per_million` now matches the `google/gemini-*`
  family by substring (Pro/Flash/Flash-Lite tiers) so versioned slugs get a
  non-zero, clearly-flagged **best-effort** cost estimate.
- **2e** SPEC UPDATE: **REV-130 lives ONLY as inline code comments, not in
  `docs/specs/`.** The inline comments in `parser.rs`, `prompt.rs`, and
  `models/mod.rs` are updated in place to mark REV-130 superseded by #1241 →
  fail-closed UNKNOWN, with rationale.

Tests updated to assert UNKNOWN: `parse_fail_safe_unknown_on_empty_response`,
`parse_fail_safe_unknown_on_malformed_json`, `parse_fail_safe_unknown_on_unparseable_verdict`,
`run_review_fail_safe_on_llm_error`. New: `parse_truncated_json_object_is_unknown`,
`run_review_truncated_output_is_unknown`, `is_truncated_*`, `max_tokens_gemini_is_raised`,
`max_tokens_default_for_non_gemini`, `cost_estimate_gemini_{pro,flash,flash_lite}_*`.

## FIX 3 — #1233: MCP `reviewer_model` override must switch provider

`mcp/tools.rs::deps_from_state` ignored the override and always cloned
`state.llm` (the startup provider), so an `openrouter/...` / `bedrock/...` override
hit the wrong backend. It now resolves the override's provider via
`llm::resolve_provider_and_model`; when it differs from the startup provider it
builds a fresh provider via `llm::build_provider` (async), falling back to the
startup provider with a `warn!` on build error. Same-provider overrides still
cheaply clone (no allocation).

Tests: `deps_from_state_openrouter_override_switches_provider` (openrouter/
override vs bedrock-startup → `name() == "openrouter"`),
`deps_from_state_no_override_reuses_startup_provider`.

## FIX 4 — #1312: flaky auth-strategy test env race

`strategy.rs::select_garbage_override_falls_through_to_mode` was missing
`#[serial]` (all sibling `select_*` tests have it) and raced on `AUTH_MODE_ENV`.
Added `#[serial]` + a `remove_var(AUTH_MODE_ENV)` guard.

## FIX 5 — #1234: verify-only (no code change)

`integrations/context/github_issues.rs` already caps queries at 256 chars.
`cargo test -p trusty-review -- query_capped` → **2 passed**
(`query_capped_at_256_chars`, `query_capped_at_word_boundary`). Ready to close #1234.

---

## Version

`trusty-review` **0.3.12 → 0.3.13** + root `[workspace.dependencies]` pin + `Cargo.lock`.

- `cargo check` — OK
- `cargo test -p trusty-review` — 834 lib + 19 bin passed, 0 failed (3 pre-existing ignored)
- `cargo clippy -p trusty-review --all-targets -- -D warnings` — 0 trusty-review warnings

author: os-zhuang
body:
Closes #1978. Foundation slice of [ADR-0053 Phase 2](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/framework/pull/1975).

## What

Adds `ExecutionContext.timezone` (optional IANA zone) and resolves it **once per request** in `resolveExecutionContext`, with precedence **user preference → org default → `UTC`**:

- **User override** — `sys_user_preference` row `(user_id, key='timezone')`.
- **Org default** — the tenant-scoped `sys_setting` `(namespace='localization', key='timezone', scope='tenant')`. One org per physical tenant (ADR-0002), so the row needs no `tenant_id` filter.
- An invalid IANA zone is ignored and resolution falls through. Every read goes through the existing defensive `tryFind`, so timezone resolution **never blocks auth**.

## Why it's safe (pure plumbing, zero behavior change)

Nothing reads `ctx.timezone` yet, and an absent value resolves to `'UTC'` — exactly today's behavior. This is the keystone the rest of Phase 2 consumes:

- #1980 — tz-aware `today()`/`daysFromNow()`/`daysAgo()`
- #1981 — datetime rendering in the reference zone
- #1982 — tz-aware analytics bucketing

(Those slices depend on this one for the `timezone` value.)

## Notes

- A discoverable `localization` settings **manifest** for the org default is a small follow-up — the resolver already reads the row if present, so this lands without it.
- Resolution adds at most two cheap reads per authenticated request, consistent with the resolver's existing `sys_member` / permission-set lookups. A caching pass can come later if needed.

## Testing

- New: user preference wins over org default; tenant-scoped org default used when no user pref; `UTC` when neither; an invalid zone falls through; anonymous requests leave it unset.
- Full `@objectstack/runtime` suite green — **387 tests**; `@objectstack/spec` kernel green — **682**; DTS build + typecheck clean.
- Changeset: `minor` (new optional `ExecutionContext` field + resolver).

author: theolong
body:
## What

A **Redaction** toggle (System tab → Actions) that masks PII so the dashboard can be screenshotted or screen-shared safely. Redaction is enforced **server-side** — masked data never reaches the browser, so it can't be recovered from the console, network tab, or page source.

When ON:
- **Server masks every JSON response** (after-request hook) — case/receipt numbers, applicant + representative names, and receipt numbers embedded in URLs/log text — across `/api/cases`, `/api/updates`, `/api/system-log`, `/api/history`, etc.
- **Data exports return 403** (`/api/export`, `/api/system-log/export`).
- **Pull rows are locked**: their steps (auth/MFA/case-fetch — the most PII) are never rendered into the DOM and the expander is disabled.
- **Client masking treatment**: redaction bars on receipt/name fields, grayed "Download full history" + "Copy this snapshot", across Cases / Updates / System.

It's a **global, server-side switch** persisted in `config.json` (`redaction_enabled`), toggled via `/api/redaction-mode` (mirrors the Debug toggle). The pill syncs the flag on boot before first paint and re-fetches on toggle.

## Architecture

- **`src/redaction.py`** — `REDACT_KEYS`, `scrub_text()` (USCIS receipt + email patterns), `redact_obj()` (deep, pure). Mirrored by the same-named client helpers in `app.js` for the local masking treatment.
- **`server.py`** — `/api/redaction-mode` GET/POST + atomic config write; `@app.after_request` JSON redactor; 403 guards on the two export endpoints.
- **`app.js`** — server-backed pill (`loadRedactionState` + POST toggle), pull-row lock, redaction-bar styling, disabled exports.

## Testing

- **Python**: redaction module (purity, nesting, embedded-receipt scrub) + route tests (toggle persistence, after-request masking with a realistic 10-digit receipt, export blocking).
- **Node (vm-sandboxed `app.js`)**: deep redactor, `scrub_text`, `redactDetailValue`, the `_detailKvHtml` system-log chokepoint, and the server-backed toggle flow.
- **Static markup/CSS**: pill as ARIA switch, popover copy (server-side wording), redaction-bar + disabled-button + locked-pull CSS.
- Full suite: **544 passed**.
- **E2E via cloakbrowser** (through Cloudflare + the gate), redaction ON:
  - Raw API responses (`/api/cases`, `/api/history`, `/api/system-log`) contain **no receipt** — verified by `fetch()` inside the page.
  - `/api/export` → **403**.
  - Pull row **locked** (`syslog-nested-locked`), **0 step rows in the DOM**.
  - Cases/Updates/System: no receipt in visible text *or* DOM attributes; raw JSON masked; download/copy disabled.
  - Persists across reload; toggling off restores everything.

body:
## What

`--compilation_level ADVANCED` was a **literal no-op** — it returned the source verbatim. This wires it through the **same degrade-safe typed optimization pipeline as `SIMPLE`** (parse → bridge → `run_simple_pipeline` → emit, falling back to `whitespace_only` on any error).

ADVANCED is specified to be **at least as aggressive** as SIMPLE, so reusing the already-tested SIMPLE pipeline is a correct, zero-risk first step. Advanced-only passes (aggressive property/global renaming, cross-module tree-shaking) layer on as they are implemented.

## Changes

- `run.rs`: `CompilationLevel::Simple | CompilationLevel::Advanced` now share the typed pipeline arm; `Bundle | TranspileOnly` remain identity passthrough.
- Correlation-vector trace: ADVANCED reports `advanced_v1` (same shape as `simple_v2`) instead of `identity`.
- New fixture `tests/diff/advanced-optimizes/` + integration harness; unit tests `advanced_optimizes_like_simple` / `advanced_matches_simple_output` pin ADVANCED ≡ SIMPLE output today.
- Bump `0.143.0 → 0.144.0`; CHANGELOG, README, `cli.spec.json`, help-markdown fixture updated.

## Verification

- Full `cargo test` for closurec: **0 failures**.
- Empirically: `function f(longName){return longName+1} f(5);` under `--compilation_level ADVANCED` → `function f(a){return a + 1};f(5);` (previously returned verbatim).
- Security review (inline diff): **PASSED** — no new panic/overflow/error-handling/injection surface; the pipeline body is unchanged and already degrade-safe.

author: tokuhirom
body:
## Summary

Closure-generated infinite sequences (`1, 1, * + * ... *`, `0, 1, *+* ... *`) were eagerly materialized to a ~32-element prefix and frozen as a plain cached list, so indexing past the prefix returned `Nil` (e.g. `fib[100]` → `Nil`). This makes them **truly lazy**: elements past the eager prefix are produced on demand by re-invoking the generator closure.

```raku
my $s = (1, 1, * + * ... *);
say $s[100];          # before: Nil   after: 573147844013817084101

constant fib := 0, 1, *+* ... *;
say fib[100];         # before: Nil   after: 354224848179261915075

my @a = (2, 4, 6 ... *).lazy;
say @a[100];          # before: Nil   after: 202
```

## How

- New `LazyList.closure_seq` (`ClosureSeqState`) keeps the generator closure, its captured env, and the pre-compiled fast-path body. `Interpreter::extend_closure_sequence` extends the cache on demand over the growing element history (promoting to BigInt naturally, since the closure's `+` does).
- Extracted the per-element generator invocation into a shared `sequence_closure_step`, used by both the initial generation loop and the on-demand extension.
- Routed `sequence_spec` / `closure_seq` lazy lists through the bounded incremental-pull index path (previously only gather/lazy-pipe did) — this also fixes `(2,4,6 ... *)[100]`.
- Fixed a latent env-corruption bug: the generator's captured env could leak a stale shadow of an outer variable (notably the very `$s` the sequence is bound to) back through the env overlay, clobbering it on the second pull. Now only captures the body **genuinely mutated** (e.g. `++$i`, `++$sunk`) propagate back to the caller.

## Scope

Unblocks `S04-declarations/constant.t` test 46 (`fib[100]`); the file's only remaining failure is the unrelated `G::c` constant-aliased-enum dispatch (test 44).

Lazy **arrays** (`my @a = 1..*`) remain eager: Array mutation ops (clone / unshift / shift / `:delete` / element-assign) have no reify-on-demand path yet, and preserving laziness there regresses `S32-array/{create,delete-adverb}.t`. Left as a follow-up.

## Tests

- New `t/lazy-closure-seq.t` (16 subtests: scalar/`.lazy`/`constant` indexing, side-effecting & named-sub generators, `last`-terminated finite sequences, BigInt promotion).
- `make test` green; targeted roast sample (134 sequence/lazy/range/list/array tests) all pass; clippy + fmt clean.

author: nao1215
body:
## Summary

Two byte-oriented applets decoded input as UTF-8 text and then operated on runes, diverging from GNU on binary or invalid-UTF-8 input (issue #953):

- `tr` decoded its whole input with `string(data)`/`[]rune`, so invalid UTF-8 bytes were normalized to U+FFFD. `tr '\377' X` corrupted a lone `0xFF` byte into the replacement character instead of translating it, and `tr A Z` rewrote unrelated non-UTF-8 bytes while translating valid ones.
- `wc` counted a lone NUL or control byte as a word, because it treated every non-space rune as a word start.

## Changes

- `tr` now decodes input into cells that preserve invalid bytes verbatim (a cell is either a valid rune or a raw byte). Set membership, translation, deletion, and squeezing operate per cell, and untranslated raw bytes are written back unchanged. This matches GNU `tr`'s byte-oriented behavior on binary input while keeping multi-byte UTF-8 text behavior for valid input.
- `wc` (`textproc.CountReader`) now starts a word only at a printable, non-space character; control bytes and invalid UTF-8 bytes are transparent — they neither start nor end a word. So `a\x01b` is one word and a lone NUL/control/invalid byte is zero words, matching GNU `wc`.

## Design Decisions

`tr` keeps a `raw` flag per symbol so a translated binary byte is emitted as a single byte rather than multi-byte UTF-8, and an octal escape like `\377` matches input byte `0xFF`. `wc` uses `unicode.IsPrint` plus an explicit invalid-byte check (`RuneError` with size 1) to mirror glibc `iswprint`/`iswspace`. Verified byte-for-byte against GNU `tr` and `wc` for every reproduction in the issue. The applets listed in the issue as "worth auditing next" (rev, fold, fmt, cut) are left for a separate follow-up as the issue notes they are not yet catalogued.

Closes #953

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * `tr` command now properly preserves binary and invalid UTF-8 data without corruption
  * Word-counting logic updated to align with GNU `wc` behavior for control bytes and word boundaries

* **Tests**
  * Added coverage for binary data handling and word counting edge cases

author: raccioly
body:
🚨 **Severity:** CRITICAL
💡 **Vulnerability:** Unsanitized variables inside shell execution calls using `execSync`. If a directory name or path string contains shell metacharacters (`&`, `;`, `||`), an attacker could easily inject arbitrary code and spawn unauthorized processes.
🎯 **Impact:** Arbitrary remote code execution (RCE) / command injection. By replacing the shell execution, we bypass the OS shell entirely and pass arguments safely and directly to the binaries.
🔧 **Fix:** Refactored vulnerable invocations across `cli/commands/setup.mjs`, `cli/commands/score.mjs`, `cli/ensure-skills.mjs`, `cli/validators/freshness.mjs`, and `cli/shared-git.mjs` to use `execFileSync`. Removed shell features like pipes (`| wc -l`) and redirections (`2>/dev/null`), replacing them natively with JavaScript string splitting and native stdio ignores (`['pipe', 'pipe', 'ignore']`). Cleaned up unused `execSync` imports from surrounding files.
✅ **Verification:** Ran test suite (`node --test tests/*.test.mjs`) to verify git integrations and CLI initializations operate identically without regressions.

author: crgasparoto-br
body:
## Problema

A tela de relatórios estava dividida entre `ReportsPage` e `ReportsGoalsPage`, o que vinha causando confusão sobre qual implementação era chamada pelo menu lateral e onde aplicar as melhorias recentes. Além disso, a tela Profissional havia regredido: perdeu o cabeçalho original de acompanhamento profissional e parte das abas internas da análise da pessoa acompanhada.

## Solução

- Ajusta a rota `/reports` para importar `@/pages/ReportsPage` diretamente.
- Mantém `ReportsPage` como fonte única da tela Reports, preservando os blocos já esperados pela suíte de testes.
- Remove `client/src/pages/ReportsGoalsPage.tsx`, eliminando a página duplicada.
- Renomeia o teste de peso para `ReportsPage.weight.test.tsx`, removendo a referência ao nome antigo.
- Recupera na tela Reports as análises mais fortes da antiga `ReportsGoalsPage`: aderência à meta calórica ajustada, gráfico consumido vs meta base/ajustada, evolução de peso com leitura de tendência, qualidade alimentar agregada e água/exercícios como apoio.
- Restaura o cabeçalho inicial da tela Profissional como `Profissional / Acompanhamento profissional`, com o texto de gerenciamento de vínculos autorizados.
- Mantém as abas principais da tela Profissional: `Vínculos de acompanhamento` e `Análise por pessoa acompanhada`.
- Restaura as abas internas da análise profissional: `Resumo`, `Hoje`, `Relatórios`, `Metas` e `Comentários`.
- Preserva os ajustes recentes de relatórios, incluindo aderência, água, exercícios, evolução de peso e g/kg/dia planejado/realizado.
- Mantém o botão `Analisar` nos vínculos levando para a aba de análise e preserva o ponto de renderização das sugestões de exceções de meta dentro de `Metas`.

## Validação

- GitHub Actions `Agent-first gate` passou completo no commit `182bcf87202389c106ab441c9e8d212fe9ed0196`.
- Etapas verdes: TypeScript check, Tests, Architecture check, Documentation check, Build e Agent check.
- Vercel segue bloqueado por limite de build da conta (`build-rate-limit`), não por falha de código.

## Risco

Médio. A tela Profissional combina navegação visual, dados de paciente autorizado e relatórios agregados; a implementação preserva as consultas atuais e recompõe a navegação anterior em abas, mas ainda recomenda validação visual manual no fluxo `/professional`.

author: mfoulds
body:
## Summary

- Replace the release tag-phase `git pull --ff-only origin main` with explicit fetch plus `merge --ff-only` against `origin/main`.
- When resuming a release from `phase=merged`, tag the stored release PR merge commit instead of whatever commit `main` currently points at.
- Verify the target commit's `pyproject.toml` version before creating or validating the release tag.

## Why

The 0.7.11 and 0.7.12 release publishes both merged the release PR, then failed before tag creation with `fatal: Cannot fast-forward to multiple branches.` The release script should not depend on `git pull` or mutable `FETCH_HEAD` state during the tag phase.

## Validation

- `bash -n new_release.sh`
- `git diff --check`

## What

`tanglebrain.__version__` now derives from the installed distribution metadata (`importlib.metadata.version("tanglebrain")`) instead of a hardcoded literal. Also refreshes the C1-era module docstring to describe the current frontier-first + paid-tier design.

author: mbryantms
body:
## What & why

Fixing one typo'd field meant opening the full **30-field edit sheet**. This adds click-to-edit popovers on the issue **Details** grid so an admin can PATCH a single scalar field in place (audit **B12**).

## How

- **New `InlineIssueFieldEdit`** (client): renders the field's value; for admins it adds a pencil → popover with a **type-aware input** (text / textarea / number / enum) that PATCHes just `{ [field]: value }` via the existing `useUpdateIssue`, then `router.refresh()`es the RSC so the new value re-renders. The issue PATCH is `RequireAdmin`, so **non-admins see the value only** (no pencil). A field→config map owns the kind + enum option sets, mirrored from the bulk `EditMetadataDialog` so inline and bulk edits offer the same choices.
- **Pure `buildFieldPatch` helper**: empty → `null` (clear the field), number → parsed int or null, else trimmed string — matching the server's `Option<Option<T>>` PATCH semantics. Unit-tested.
- **Wired into the Details grid** (`page.tsx`) for the scalar fields: publisher, imprint, alternate series, story arc (+ number), volume, language, age rating, format. The popover only mounts where a value **already exists**, so the grid stays compact and *adding* a missing field still uses the sheet.

## Scope (per decision)

Scalars only — **credits / cast / genres / tags / covers keep the full sheet** (they need multi-value editors / the audited junction-writer path). Web-only: no server or codegen change (reuses the existing `PATCH /series/{slug}/issues/{slug}`).

## Verification

- Unit: `buildFieldPatch` (trim, clear-on-empty, number parse/clear, enum passthrough).
- `typecheck` / `eslint` / `prettier` clean.
- **Live-verified** as admin on `/series/a-force/issues/1` → Details: opened the Publisher pencil (pre-filled "Marvel", Save disabled until changed), edited to "Marvel Comics", saved → value re-rendered after refresh, popover closed, "Issue updated" toast, 0 console errors (reverted back to "Marvel").

author: tokuhirom
body:
## Summary

In Raku, `.sort`, `.reverse` and the `sort(...)`/`reverse(...)` sub forms all return a **`Seq`**, but mutsu returned a `List`/`Array`:

```
(1,2,3).sort.^name      # raku: Seq   mutsu(before): List
(1,2,3).reverse.^name   # raku: Seq   mutsu(before): List
reverse(1,2,3).^name    # raku: Seq   mutsu(before): List
```

mutsu's `Seq` is an eager `Arc<Vec<Value>>` (the same shape as a materialized list), so only the **result type tag** was wrong — `.sort` even returned an `Array` kind. The fast-path list dispatch (`dispatch_core_list.rs`), the `reverse` native function (`functions.rs`), and the `reverse` slow-path (`builtins_collection.rs`) all now produce `Value::Seq`.

`.^name` now reports `Seq`, matching Rakudo; indexing, assignment to `@a`, and stringification are unaffected since `Seq` already round-trips as a list everywhere.

## Test

- `make test` PASS
- roast `S32-list/{sort,reverse,seq}.t`, `S03-metaops/reverse.t`, `S02-types/{list,lists}.t`, `S02-lists/indexing.t` all PASS

author: tiana-code
body:
## What

Adds `ConcurrentPostersIT`, a Testcontainers PostgreSQL 17 concurrency test that proves the ledger's no-lost-update invariant under real contention. 100 virtual-thread posters, released together by a `CountDownLatch` start-gate, each commit a distinct balanced `DEBIT +100.00 / CREDIT -100.00` transaction to one shared account pair through the idempotency-wrapped path (`idempotencyService.execute { transactionService.post(...) }`), the only path where the bounded optimistic-retry absorbs the `@Version` conflicts on the shared `account_balances` rows.

## Asserted contract (non-flaky, S = observed success count)

- Final balance of each account equals the algebraic sum of the committed postings (`balance == 100.00 * S` via `compareTo`).
- Every poster resolves to exactly one outcome: committed success or a typed `ConcurrencyConflictException`; any other throwable (including a raw `OptimisticLockingFailureException` or a pool-timeout) is captured first and fails the test loudly.
- Transaction rows == S; entry rows == 2 * S; vacuous-run guard (balance != 0 when S >= 1).

All assertions are phrased over the observed S, so the test passes on every CI run regardless of how the scheduler resolves 100-way contention (default `max-attempts=3`, no backoff, means many posters legitimately resolve to a typed 503; that is correct and asserted).

## Notes

- Test-only slice, **zero production change**.
- `@DataJpaTest` + `@Transactional(NOT_SUPPORTED)` so worker threads commit and the read-back sees committed cross-thread state; mirrors the `AuditRetryTopologyIT` harness.
- Hikari pool sized (`maximum-pool-size=16`, explicit `connection-timeout`) to keep real parallelism while staying within the shared-container budget; `@AfterEach outboxRepository.deleteAll()` keeps sibling global-count ITs green.
- Runs on CI only (Testcontainers; no in-memory fallback).

Closes #56

author: sumleo
body:
The Responses API request body is encoded with a bare `JSONEncoder()` that doesn't set `.sortedKeys`. The tools array serializes Swift dictionaries (`JSONSchema.properties: [String: Property]` and `rawJSONStorage: [String: AnyCodable]`), and dictionary iteration order is randomized per process. So the same tool list can serialize with its keys in a different order from one run to the next.

OpenAI prompt caching keys on a byte-exact prefix match, and the tools live in that cached prefix. Reordered keys change the bytes without changing the meaning, so the cache_read path silently stops firing and every request pays full price.

The fix is to set `outputFormatting = [.sortedKeys]` on that encoder, mirroring what's already done on the Anthropic path in `CompletionsAnthropic.swift`, which has a comment explaining the same caching concern. The wire shape is unchanged; only key order becomes deterministic.

I couldn't build or run this locally since it needs Xcode, so I've kept the change minimal and am relying on CI to verify it compiles. Two edits only: the encoder change in `ResponsesAPIRequest.swift` and a one-line release-notes entry.

body:
## Summary

`list_tables` / `list_views` filtered the in-memory `SchemaContext` by the requested schema and returned the matches. A schema **outside the introspected source set** yielded the same empty array as a schema that genuinely has no tables/views — the caller (an AI agent) could not tell "nothing here" from "I'm not looking there".

Both tools now also return, alongside the existing list:

- **`sourceSchemas`** — the configured source schemas (`SchemaContext.meta.sourceSchemas`), so the scope is visible without guessing;
- **`outOfScope`** — `true` when the requested schema is not one of `sourceSchemas`, so an empty `tables`/`views` then reads as "not looking there" rather than "in scope but empty".

The output is **additive**; nothing changes for an in-scope schema's existing fields.

## `includeSystem`

The advertised `includeSystem` input on `list_tables` was described as "currently ignored" and never read by the handler. The introspected schema set is fixed when the `SchemaContext` is built, so it can never be honored at call time. It is therefore **dropped from the MCP tool definition** (the agent-facing advertised input). To avoid a source-compatibility break for the exported `ListTablesInput` type, it is **kept as a deprecated, ignored optional field** on the zod input schema, and zod still accepts it.

## Scope semantics (note)

`sourceSchemas` is the **configured source set** — `introspect()` deliberately returns the requested schemas (a configured-but-absent schema is warned and skipped at introspect time but still listed; `introspect.test.ts` locks this). `outOfScope` therefore means "not among the configured source schemas," which matches the issue's definition of "never introspected (outside the configured source schemas)". This is documented in the handler comments.

## Tests

- `schemas.test`: updated for the new required output fields (`sourceSchemas`, `outOfScope`) and the deprecated-but-accepted `includeSystem` input.
- New `list-scope.test` (no DB): proves an in-scope-empty schema reports `outOfScope: false` while an out-of-scope schema reports `outOfScope: true`, for both tools.

`pnpm -r typecheck`, `eslint`, and the `@kozou/mcp` suite (105 tests) pass.

## Review

Adversarially reviewed to convergence. Findings surfaced and addressed: (1) the `includeSystem` removal would have broken the exported TS input type — kept as a deprecated field, removed only from the advertised tool definition; (2) confirmed `outOfScope` correctly uses the established `sourceSchemas` = configured-source-set contract (changing `introspect()` to "successfully introspected" would break a deliberate, test-locked contract, so it was documented rather than changed).

Closes #178

- Support digital leader signatures stored in the same storage mechanism, include a QR validation link, and ensure the printed date uses the system `ApprovedAt` timestamp in `pt-BR` format. 
- Provide programmatic access to download the PDF and a public validation endpoint so downstream consumers can verify issued letters.

### Description
- Domain: added `LetterStatus`, enriched `PreachingLetter` (number, `ApprovedByUserId`, `ApprovedAt`, `PdfStoragePath`, `QrCodeValue`, `DestinationChurchId`, status/timestamps), `LeaderSignature`, and church/user metadata fields such as address, city, state and `ChurchJoinedAt` in `User` (files: `src/CadastroIgreja.Domain/Requests.cs`, `src/CadastroIgreja.Domain/Church.cs`, `src/CadastroIgreja.Domain/User.cs`).

body:
When you open the chat drawer, you'll now see the most recent messages right away instead of having to wait for them to load, and each message shows what time it was sent. This makes the chat feel more natural and responsive, like other messaging apps.

The in-game global chat already exists and works. This PR fixes two polish gaps in the existing feature:

- **Message timestamps:** Each message now displays a small, muted `HH:MM` local time (derived from `created_at`) so players can gauge how recent the conversation is.

## How to test

1. Open the app and enter the building world, then press **Enter** (or click the 💬 button, lower-right) to open the chat drawer.
2. You should see the seeded messages — including **"Chat messages appear here in real time."** from *Staging demo* — listed oldest-to-newest, with the most recent at the bottom.
3. Each message now shows a small, muted **HH:MM** time after the text (e.g. the time it was sent in your local timezone).

author: mikelwl
body:
## What
The non-Windows `onnxruntime` was unpinned, so a fresh virtualenv could resolve a newer release than the OCR ground-truth goldens reproduce and than the shipped backend runs. The Windows build caps at DirectML 1.24.4 (the `onnxruntime-directml` line never advanced past it), and the Rust `ort` binding loads `api-24` (load-dynamic), so 1.24.4 is the runtime both backend arms ship. The OCR equivalence panels are ONNX-version-sensitive, so an unpinned non-Windows install drifting to a newer release would fail them in a fresh checkout.

This pins the plain CPU `onnxruntime` to 1.24.4 on every platform (collapsing the prior Windows-only pin plus the unpinned non-Windows line into one unconditional pin), so a fresh install resolves the version the goldens and the shipped runtime already use.

## Test plan
- OCR equivalence full suite at 1.24.4: `pytest backend/tests/e2e/test_ocr_equivalence.py -m full` -> 5 passed.
- Cross-language equivalence at 1.24.4: `just test-equivalence` -> Rust legs green plus 54 Python conformance tests passed.
- Full backend suite at 1.24.4: `just test-backend` -> 2337 passed, 2 skipped.

author: clates
body:
## Summary

Fixes all 8 bugs identified by automated codebase analysis (issues #77–#84). Also updates `AGENTS.md` to enforce PR-only workflow going forward.

- **#77 / #78 / #79** — NULL `progress_blob` / `plan_rules_blob` caused `TypeError` crashes for new students in `logic.py`, `main.py`, and `agent.py`. Fixed with `or "{}"` null guards.
- **#80** — `generate_weekly_plan` used `datetime.now()` (local time) instead of UTC, producing wrong `week_of` dates on non-UTC servers. Fixed to `datetime.now(UTC)`.
- **#81** — `_get_grade_level` fell back to `0` when a student had no packets, causing plan generation to fail with "no standards found". Now falls back to the grade level in the student's metadata blob.
- **#82** — Repeated apply/reverse quantity feedback cycles accumulated floating-point drift in `activity_bias`. Fixed by rounding to 6 decimal places after each update.
- **#83** — Concurrent plan saves for the same student could create duplicate packet rows. Replaced `DELETE` + `INSERT` with atomic `INSERT OR REPLACE`.
- **#84** — Deleting a student left orphaned `packet_feedback` rows. `delete_student()` now deletes the student's `weekly_packets` first, which cascades to all packet-related data.

Also adds section 7 to `AGENTS.md` documenting the correct automated analysis → issue → PR workflow to prevent future direct-to-main commits.

- [ ] Create a new student (NULL blobs) and verify plan generation and `/progress-map` no longer return 500
- [ ] Verify student deletion removes associated packets and feedback from the DB
- [ ] Submit feedback multiple times and confirm `activity_bias` doesn't drift
- [ ] Confirm `week_of` in generated plans is always a Monday in UTC

Closes #77, #78, #79, #80, #81, #82, #83, #84

body:
## Summary
- Switch ffmpeg from `homebrew/core` to the **`homebrew-ffmpeg/ffmpeg`** tap build (libass, drawtext/libfreetype, many extra filters) in developer + cloud-engineer. Default bottled build : **fdk-aac is intentionally omitted** (it needs `args: ["with-fdk-aac"]`, a from-source build that recompiles on every ffmpeg update). Brewfiles carry a note on how to re-add it.
- **Fix tap-trust ordering**: Homebrew's tap-trust enforcement now blocks installing/updating from an untrusted tap, but bootstrap trusted taps *after* `brew bundle`. A fresh install would fail on the new tap (and on `hashicorp/tap`). Now tap + trust declared taps *before* bundling.
- **Idempotent migration**: a pre-bundle step replaces a core ffmpeg with the tap build only when needed, detected via the keg's `INSTALL_RECEIPT.json` source tap (jq-free, since jq may not be installed yet). No-op if already the tap build.

## Why
The tap build's filters (drawtext/libass) are needed for the recording/encoding workflow; core ffmpeg lacks them.

## Test plan
- `bash -n install/bootstrap.sh` + shellcheck clean.
- Brewfiles: tap line present, `brew "homebrew-ffmpeg/ffmpeg/ffmpeg"`, no bare `brew "ffmpeg"`.
- On a machine already running the tap build, the receipt detection takes the no-op path (verified).
- Filters confirmed present on the installed tap build: `drawtext` (libfreetype), `ass` (libass).

## Note
fdk-aac trade-off captured in the Brewfile comment; tracking issue to follow.

author: austinkregel
body:
## Summary

- **Root cause of powerwash (third iteration):** ChromeOS's `PasswordInputScraper` is gated by `getSAMLFlag`, which queries `isSamlPage_` at `document_start`. In Chromium's architecture, `document_start` content scripts run **before** `loadcommit` fires for the same page — so `isSamlPage_` always reflects the *previous* page's `loadcommit`, not the current page's `pendingIsSamlPage_`. With a server-side 302 (`/embedded/setup → /login`), `/embedded/setup` has no `loadcommit` of its own, so `isSamlPage_` is `false` when `/login`'s `document_start` fires. The scraper never initializes, `password_` stays null, ChromeOS arms `kSilentPowerwash`.
- **Fix:** when an unauthenticated webview hits `/embedded/setup`, return a 200 HTML page with `google-accounts-saml: start` that `window.location.replace()`-redirects to `/login`. This gives ChromeOS a `loadcommit` for `/embedded/setup` (`isSamlPage_ = true`). When `/login` subsequently loads, its `document_start` fires before `/login`'s own `loadcommit` — but `isSamlPage_` is now `true` from `/embedded/setup`'s loadcommit, so the scraper initializes and captures the typed password.
- **No impact on normal logins:** the intermediate HTML page only fires for `routeIs('gaia.embedded-setup') && $response->isRedirect()`. Normal `/login` visits (no GAIA session) are unaffected. The `google-accounts-saml` header is a ChromeOS-internal concept; non-ChromeOS browsers silently ignore it.
- This mirrors how real enterprise SAML works: GAIA (`accounts.google.com`) emits the header on its own HTML page (not a 302), gets its own `loadcommit`, and the actual IdP's `document_start` then sees `isSamlPage_ = true` from GAIA's prior loadcommit. Previous attempts (v1.6.4: `gaia_saml_api` injection, v1.6.5: header on `/login` only) both failed because they didn't address this timing constraint.

## Code references (openFyde r132 Chromium tree)

- `saml_handler.js:572` — `isSamlPage_ = pendingIsSamlPage_` (only at loadcommit)
- `saml_handler.js:1026` — `onGetSAMLFlag_` returns `this.isSamlPage_` (not `pendingIsSamlPage_`)
- `saml_injected.js:214` — `getSAMLFlag` sent at `document_start` (before loadcommit)
- `saml_handler.js:990` — `onUpdatePassword_` only stores if `this.isSamlPage_`

## Test plan

- [ ] Deploy to device; complete OOBE sign-in; reboot — device should NOT powerwash
- [ ] Normal browser login to `aut.hair/login` (no GAIA flow) — no `google-accounts-saml` header, no JS redirect
- [ ] CI: `GaiaSamlModeTest` — `/embedded/setup` unauthenticated returns 200 with SAML header + `window.location.replace`; `/login` returns 200 with SAML header; completion page has no SAML header

body:
## Problem

Editing a taste (编辑) still showed a large empty band above the 取消/编辑/保存 header — even after PR #135. The previous fix only adjusted the content `paddingTop` (36→20) *below* the header, which was never the real gap.

## Root cause — the top safe-area inset was applied twice (edit mode)

| layer | inset added |
|---|---|
| route `app/taste/[id].tsx` | `paddingTop: insets.top` |
| `EditActionHeader` (inside DetailView, edit mode) | `padTop = insets.top + 12` |

→ `2 × insets.top + 12` of dead space **above** the header text (~106px on a notched phone). Read mode looked fine (no header; single route inset). The reference screen **AddModal** never doubles: its route (`add.tsx`) is `absoluteFill` with no inset, so its `EditActionHeader` applies the inset exactly once.

## Fix — move inset ownership into DetailView (mirror AddModal)

- Route `taste/[id].tsx` no longer pads `insets.top`.
- Read mode applies `insets.top` once on an **outer non-positioned wrapper**, so the inner `position:relative` block (hero photo + absolute back button / verdict stamp / play overlay) shifts down uniformly — pixel-identical to the old route padding, with no Yoga absolute-vs-padding ambiguity.
- Edit mode gets the inset exactly once via `EditActionHeader`.

## Tests (both two-directional)

- `TasteDetailRoute.test.tsx` (new): mounts the real route with `DetailView` stubbed + `insets.top=47`, asserts the route container has **no** `paddingTop` — pins the route as non-owner of the inset, independent of DetailView internals.
- `DetailViewEdit.test.tsx`: read-mode outer wrapper carries `insets.top`; edit mode does not. `StyleSheet.flatten` for array-safe style reads.

## Verification

- ✅ `pnpm --filter @yon/mobile test` — **639 pass, 103 suites, 0 act-warnings**
- ✅ mobile `tsc --noEmit` clean
- ✅ Cross-provider Codex review (gpt-5.5, 2 rounds): 1 HIGH (absolute-children inset) + 1 MED (test didn't pin source) raised and fixed; second pass **RESOLVED**

author: dvaerum
body:
## Summary

Adds a curl-only Path A regression guard to both nixosTest scaffolds (`vm-single-tenant`, `vm-multi-tenant`) that would have caught the PR #165 bug at the hermetic test layer instead of leaking out to a browser click-through.

PR #165 fixed an asset-prefix sentinel substitution gap: Next.js's static export emits RSC (React Server Components) flight payloads as `<page>.txt` alongside each page; the router's `.txt` → `text/plain` MIME mapping was correct, but `text/plain` was missing from `_SUBSTITUTABLE_CTYPE_PREFIXES`, so the literal `__AGENT_MCP_ASSET_PREFIX__` reached the browser in RSC payloads. On every client-side route transition the browser then tried to load `/agent-mcp/app/<name>/__AGENT_MCP_ASSET_PREFIX__/_next/static/css/<hash>.css`, and the SPA fallback served `index.html` (text/html), tripping Firefox's strict-stylesheet MIME check.

The pre-PR-#165 hermetic tests curled the dashboard HTML and grepped for the sentinel, but they did **not** curl the dynamically-loaded chunks (JS/CSS) or the RSC `.txt` flight payloads — so the bug got through to a manual Firefox-MCP click-through on 2026-06-17.

## What this PR adds

Step #6 in each `testScript`:

1. Curls the per-project dashboard HTML root (`/agent-mcp/app/<name>/`).
2. Extracts every `/agent-mcp/assets/<rest>` reference from the served HTML via regex (matches both `src=` and `href=` attribute values).
3. Enumerates every `.txt` RSC flight payload the static export ships, mapping each to its app-relative serve URL (`/agent-mcp/app/<name>/<rest>.txt`).
4. Curls every extracted URL + every RSC `.txt` URL and asserts the response body contains zero `__AGENT_MCP_ASSET_PREFIX__` occurrences.
5. Names the offending URL(s) in the failure message so the operator can grep the dashboard build to find the file the substitution missed.

Both nixosTests now include the assertion (single-tenant + multi-tenant).

## Verification — the guard actually catches PR #165's bug

Reverted PR #165's fix (removed `text/plain` from `_SUBSTITUTABLE_CTYPE_PREFIXES` in `agent_mcp/router/asset_prefix.py`) and re-ran both nixosTests:

**Before (PR #165 fix removed → guard fires):**

```
vm-test-run-agent-mcp-single-tenant> AssertionError: PR #165 regression: the asset-prefix sentinel leaked into one or more dynamically-loaded chunks served from the dashboard (single-tenant). This is the exact failure mode PR #165 fixed — `.txt` RSC payloads served as text/plain must be substituted before bytes go on the wire, otherwise client-side route transitions construct broken CSS URLs and the browser strict-MIME check fails. Offending URLs: ['/agent-mcp/app/only-project/index.txt']

vm-test-run-agent-mcp-multi-tenant> AssertionError: PR #165 regression: the asset-prefix sentinel leaked into one or more dynamically-loaded chunks served from the dashboard (multi-tenant). This is the exact failure mode PR #165 fixed — `.txt` RSC payloads served as text/plain must be substituted before bytes go on the wire, otherwise client-side route transitions construct broken CSS URLs and the browser strict-MIME check fails. Offending URLs: ['/agent-mcp/app/alpha/index.txt']
```

**After (PR #165 fix restored → both tests pass):**

```
vm-test-run-agent-mcp-single-tenant> (finished: run the VM test script, in 13.05 seconds)
vm-test-run-agent-mcp-single-tenant> test script finished in 13.13s

vm-test-run-agent-mcp-multi-tenant> (finished: run the VM test script, in 13.28 seconds)
vm-test-run-agent-mcp-multi-tenant> test script finished in 13.34s
```

This proves the guard would have surfaced PR #165's exact regression class before merge.

## Stale URL cleanup (incidental)

Both `nix/tests/{single,multi}-tenant.nix` referenced the pre-PR-B dashboard URL shape (`/agent-mcp/__dashboard/<name>/`), which has 404'd since the Shape-3 rename to `/agent-mcp/app/<name>/`. The existing tests therefore fail on `origin/main` (the upstream CI workflow doesn't run `nix flake check`, so this rot didn't surface). Updated to the current shape so the new guard's HTML pre-condition has something to curl, and the existing `200`/`302`/W1-redirect assertions actually exercise the live URLs.

## Test plan

- [x] `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.vm-single-tenant -L` → green
- [x] `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.vm-multi-tenant -L` → green
- [x] Break-the-fix experiment (revert PR #165 → guard fires; restore PR #165 → guard passes) on both nixosTests
- [x] `pytest -n auto` → 1122 passed
- [x] `ruff check tests/` → clean
- [x] `npm run build` in `agent_mcp/dashboard/` → clean

author: ishaan-berri
body:
## Relevant issues

Proof of concept for moving LiteLLM's inference path to Rust, starting with one low-risk route (OCR) and a pattern we can reuse for other routes

## Linear ticket

N/A

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] My PR passes all unit tests
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] I have requested a Greptile review

## Type

🆕 New Feature

## Changes

This ports Mistral OCR to a native Rust engine while keeping auth, logging, spend and FastAPI serving in Python. It is the first route in a strangler-style migration; the goal is to prove the pattern once and reuse it (embeddings, chat, etc.) later.

New crate `litellm-rust/` whose module tree mirrors `litellm/llms/` exactly. It carries the real transform types: a `BaseOcrConfig` trait in `llms/base_llm/ocr/transformation.rs` and a `MistralOcrConfig` impl in `llms/mistral/ocr/transformation.rs`. The transforms are pure (no I/O), so the same core feeds two consumers:

- a PyO3 extension module `litellm_rust` exposing a single sync `ocr(...)` that does provider routing, request/response translation and the upstream HTTP call
- a standalone axum server binary `litellm-rust-server` that serves `POST /v1/ocr` by reusing the exact same transforms, which answers the "can we have a Rust server hit this endpoint" question directly

On the Python side, `litellm/ocr/main.py` routes the Mistral provider through `litellm_rust` instead of the old `MistralOCRConfig` + `BaseLLMHTTPHandler` path. The `@client` decorator still wraps `ocr`/`aocr`, so auth and spend tracking are unchanged. The async path already runs `ocr()` inside `run_in_executor`, so the blocking Rust call lands off the event loop and the engine releases the GIL during the request anyway.

The Python `MistralOCRConfig` is deleted. Azure AI and Vertex AI OCR configs used to subclass it, so the shared (standard-format) transforms moved up into `BaseOCRConfig` and both were reparented onto it; their behavior is unchanged.

No feature flag: Mistral OCR runs through Rust by default. If the wheel is not built, the Mistral path raises a clear ImportError telling you to run `maturin develop`.

Engineering notes: every Rust file is under 500 LOC, and a new `rust_lint` CI job runs `cargo fmt --check` plus clippy on a pinned `cimg/rust` image.

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Build the engine into the venv:

```
cd litellm-rust && maturin develop --features python
```

Standalone Rust server serving the OCR endpoint (upstream pointed at a local Mistral stand-in here because the `MISTRAL_API_KEY` in my env returns 401; the engine targets `https://api.mistral.ai/v1/ocr` by default):

```
$ PORT=8088 ./target/debug/litellm-rust-server &
$ curl -s localhost:8088/health
{"status":"ok"}

$ curl -s -X POST localhost:8088/v1/ocr -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
```

author: jscott3201
body:
## What

Turns the **SingleHopFactual** per-class dense-relevance floor from OFF (the P0 plumbing default) to **0.60**. An off-topic factual query now returns empty rather than surfacing a confident-but-unrelated hit. Other classes stay OFF pending their own calibration; the dense-weight-zero `Quote` class stays exempt (a dense floor is meaningless where the dense signal is off).

## Why 0.60 (calibration)

`0.60` is the center of the clean separation window measured on the `aionforge-eval` off-topic-rejection harness against the production **gemini-3072** embedder:

- Across an everyday corpus **and** a harder project/domain-adjacent corpus, off-topic queries peaked at **~0.55** dense similarity while on-topic gold bottomed at **~0.64**.
- A floor at the midpoint rejected **100% of off-topic queries at zero false-rejection** (recall@5 held at **1.0**).
- The midpoint maximizes the margin on both sides, so it is robust to embedder drift.

Embedder comparison (gemini at 768/1536/3072, codestral, qwen) confirmed gemini separates best at every size; the value is gemini-cosine-calibrated. Re-measure with `cargo test -p aionforge-eval --test floor_sweep -- --ignored` after any embedder/dimension change. **No model calls run in CI** — the eval harness is `#[ignore]` and key-gated; the key stays local.

## Embedder-down guard (product fix)

The default floor gates on dense similarity, so with **no** dense signal it would drop every (now lexical-only) hit and empty the recall — the opposite of the intended graceful degradation to lexical recall during an embedder outage (03 §8.1). The default floor is now **skipped when the embedder is unavailable**; an explicit per-query `RecallOptions::min_relevance` is the caller's deliberate choice and is still honored.

## ⚠️ Design tension (flagged for owner / follow-up)

The floor gates on **dense** similarity, so it also drops **low-dense hits surfaced by non-dense paths**:

- entity-set-algebra / high-precision composition,
- lexical anchoring,
- the cooling re-rank.

Each can surface a genuinely relevant hit that carries no qualifying dense score, and the floor drops it. Isolation tests for those mechanisms (`cooling_rerank`, `lexical_anchor`, `trust_rerank`, `precision`, `project_corpus`, and the engine `forget_acceptance` acceptance test) opt out with `min_relevance: Some(0.0)`; the floor's own behavior is pinned by `min_relevance_floor.rs`. Exact-identifier / entity queries route to the exempt `Quote`/`Entity` classes, so they are unaffected.

**Recommended follow-up:** measure exact-match / entity-linked recall under the floor before flipping more classes on.

## Tests

- Rewrote `tests/router.rs` and `tests/min_relevance_floor.rs` to pin factual=0.60 / others=0.0 and reproduce the off-topic admission (P4) with the floor off vs. its rejection with the class default.
- Full `aionforge-retrieval` + workspace suites green; fmt, clippy (`--workspace --all-targets`), and rustdoc `-D warnings` clean locally.

author: mtereshchenko-veeam
body:
## What

`clutel.Inherit` (and therefore `clues.Inherit`) does not propagate the OTEL trace context from `from` to `to`. Its trace block:

```go
details := map[string]string{}
ReceiveTrace(from, details)
InjectTrace(to, details)
```

has two defects:

1. **Reversed order** — it extracts *out of* the empty `details` carrier (`ReceiveTrace(from, …)`) and then serializes `to`'s span *into* the carrier (`InjectTrace(to, …)`). The span on `from` is never written into the carrier.
2. **Discarded return values** — `ReceiveTrace` returns the context carrying the extracted trace, but the result is thrown away, so `to` never gains it.

Net effect: detaching a fire-and-forget goroutine via `Inherit(ctx, context.Background(), …)` silently loses the originating `trace.id` (and baggage), breaking log/trace correlation for async work.

## Fix

Serialize `from` into the carrier, then capture the context returned by extracting into `to`:

```go
details := map[string]string{}
InjectTrace(from, details)
to = ReceiveTrace(to, details)
```

Because `clutel.Init` registers a composite `TraceContext{} + Baggage{}` propagator, this restores both the trace context and baggage.

## Tests

The existing `TestInherit` asserts only the inherited OTEL client (`n.OTEL.ServiceName`) and never inspects the span, so this was uncovered. Adds `TestInherit_PropagatesTraceContext`, which detaches onto `context.Background()` and asserts the originating `trace.id` and baggage survive. Verified it fails on the old order and passes on the fix.

author: antoniovfranco
body:
Fixes #8115

### Problem
`PregelLoop.put_writes()` modifies `self.checkpoint_pending_writes` without synchronization. Because this method is called concurrently by background threads, the current read-filter-assign-extend pattern is not atomic and can cause silent data loss in checkpoints during parallel execution (e.g., when using `Send`).

### Fix
Protected the critical section in `put_writes()` using a `threading.Lock` (`_pending_writes_lock`), initialized in `PregelLoop.__init__`.

### Testing & Impact
- Existing regression tests pass.
- Verified with concurrent stress tests (8 threads): zero write loss.
- No API changes; `SyncPregelLoop` and `AsyncPregelLoop` inherit the protection automatically via `super()`.
