author: remyluslosius
body:
## Fix: pre-release package versions collide / can't upgrade

**Reported:** on RHEL, `dnf install` of the rc.8 RPM says *"openwatch-0.2.0-1 is already installed."*

### Root cause
`build-rpm.sh` stripped the pre-release suffix (`RPM_VERSION="${VERSION%%-*}"`), so **every RC from rc.3 to rc.8 built the identical NVR `openwatch-0.2.0-1`**. dnf correctly sees the "new" rc.8 as the same package already installed. (The RPM-packaged binary also reported the stripped `0.2.0`, losing the rc.)

The DEB had a **latent sibling bug**: `0.2.0-rc.8` (hyphen = Debian revision) orders RCs correctly but sorts *above* `0.2.0`, so `dpkg --compare-versions 0.2.0-rc.8 lt 0.2.0` is **false** — GA would never supersede an RC.

### Fix — tilde + epoch, for both packages
- Encode pre-releases with `~`: **`0.2.0~rc.8`**. RPM/dpkg both sort `0.2.0~rc.7 < 0.2.0~rc.8 < 0.2.0`, so RCs are distinct and GA cleanly supersedes.
- **Epoch 1** (RPM `Epoch:`, DEB `1:` prefix). The rc.3–rc.8 packages already shipped as bare `0.2.0` (epoch 0); without the epoch bump, `0.2.0~rc.8` would read as a *downgrade* from them. Epoch 1 sorts strictly above, so upgrades from the mis-versioned installs work. Epoch is sticky/permanent (documented in the spec).
- The **binary keeps the true semver** (`openwatch --version` → `0.2.0-rc.8`); only the package metadata uses the tilde.

### Verified
- `rpm.vercmp` and `dpkg --compare-versions`: rc.7 < rc.8 < GA, all correct.
- **End-to-end container test (rockylinux:9):** seeded the *actually-published* rc.7 (`0:0.2.0-1`), reproduced the "already installed" message for the old NVR, then upgraded to the fixed rc.8 (`1:0.2.0~rc.8-1`) — clean upgrade.
- New NVRs: RPM `openwatch-0.2.0~rc.8-1.x86_64.rpm` (Epoch 1), DEB `openwatch_0.2.0~rc.8_amd64.deb` (control `Version: 1:0.2.0~rc.8`).

### Guarded
`release-package-build` v1.1.0 — new **C-12/AC-21** + a source-inspection regression test, so the strip-the-suffix bug can't silently come back. Install-guide examples updated to the tilde filenames.

> After this merges, the published `v0.2.0-rc.8` release still has the broken (`0.2.0-1`) RPMs — it needs a re-spin (see the PR discussion).

body:
## Summary

- `depends.py` passed the uv constraints file as an **absolute** path (`-c <abs>`). uv splits the `-c` value on whitespace, so an absolute cache path containing a space (the macOS default `~/Library/Application Support/RocketRide/...`) is truncated at the space and dependency resolution fails — crash-looping local mode at `init.cpp:536`.
- This is the **same class of bug** that #1256 / #1279 fixed for `--excludes`; that fix's comment wrongly claimed `-c` was unaffected, so `-c` was left absolute and still broke.
- Pass `-c` relative to `exe_dir` in all three call sites (`_install_dry_run`, `_install_requirements_inner`, the `uv` CLI passthrough) — every one already runs with `cwd=exe_dir` and the constraints file is always `<exe_dir>/cache/constraints.txt`, so the relative path never contains a space. Corrected the misleading comment. `-r` is left absolute (empirically safe).

## Type

fix

## Testing

- [ ] Tests added or updated
- [x] Tested locally
- [ ] `./builder test` passes

Isolated reproduction against the installed prerelease engine's `uv` (0.11.21), command otherwise identical to what `depends.py` builds (`cwd = engine dir`):

body:
## What

Removes direct dependency declarations from the root app `pubspec.yaml` that are no longer referenced anywhere in `lib/`, `test/`, or `integration_test/`. The feature data layers (retrofit API clients, `json_serializable` models, the ObjectBox store + entities) have all moved into their own workspace packages, so the app now only sees them — when it needs them at all — transitively through the owning package.

**Removed — regular dependencies (0 imports in the app):**
- `objectbox`, `path_provider` → now owned by `package:database`
- `url_launcher`, `flutter_staggered_grid_view` → now owned by `feature_bookmarks`
- `intl` → now owned by `package:localization`
- `json_annotation` → no `@JsonSerializable` left in the app

**Removed — dev dependencies:**
- `objectbox_generator` (was not in the active `build.yaml` targets)
- `flutter_lints` (analysis runs on `very_good_analysis`; not included anywhere)
- `retrofit_generator`, `json_serializable` (no `@RestApi` / `@JsonSerializable` sources left; their `build.yaml` scopes pointed at `lib/**/data/datasources/**` and `lib/**/data/models/**`, directories that no longer exist in the app)

**`build.yaml`:** dropped the now-dead `retrofit_generator` / `json_serializable` builder scopes and the `freezed → retrofit_generator` ordering they required. This had to change in lockstep with the dev-dep removal — leaving those builder references with the packages gone would break `build_runner`. The active generators (freezed, injectable, go_router_builder, flutter_gen) run with defaults; the file is now just the rationale comment plus the CI no-cache warning.

## Why

After the package-extraction work, `lib/` is the composition root + shell. These deps were vestigial declarations whose real owners are now the extracted packages. Pruning them keeps the app pubspec honest about what the app actually uses.

## Reviewer notes

- **Kept `objectbox_flutter_libs` explicit** even though it's now transitive via `package:database` — it's the native runtime, and keeping it declared guarantees the binaries link into the final app build. Comment updated to say so.
- These names still appear in `pubspec.lock` / `flutter pub outdated`; that's expected — they're now pulled in transitively through the workspace packages rather than declared directly.
- `cupertino_icons` has zero usage but was left in place as the canonical Flutter template default.

- `fvm flutter pub get` — clean
- `fvm dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs` — 13 outputs, no errors
- `fvm flutter analyze` — No issues found
- `fvm flutter test` — 226 passed (incl. the architecture/layering guard tests)

author: stservice
body:
# Compaction: exact IF-collapse when all condition inputs are constant (safe variant)

## Summary

An `IF` neuron picks its branch by `condition = Σ(condition-type inbound
values)`, taking the positive branch when `condition > 0` else the negative
branch (`src/methods/activations/aggregate/IF.ts`). When **every**
condition-type input is constant, the selector is fixed at compaction time, so
the IF can be collapsed losslessly to its always-taken branch. This is exact, so
it belongs to the **safe** compaction variant.

New pass `collapseConstantIf` (`src/compact/IfCollapse.ts`):

1. Detects `squash === "IF"` neurons whose condition synapses (`type:"condition"`)
   all originate from constant neurons. Branch roles are read from the synapse
   `type` field exactly as `IF.ts` reads it — never from ordering. Constant
   detection reuses `computeConstantValues` (now exported from `ConstantFold.ts`),
   so both `type:"constant"` producers and effectively-constant hidden neurons
   count.
2. Computes the fixed `condition`; the taken branch is `positive` if
   `condition > 0`, else `negative`.
3. Keeps only the taken branch's inbound synapses, stripping their `type` so they
   become ordinary additive edges; drops the condition + untaken-branch synapses.
4. Rewrites the squash to `IDENTITY`, so the output becomes
   `Σ(taken-branch values) + bias` — identical to the IF's always-taken result.

The pass runs in `compactCreature` **before** the constant fold, so any constants
it strands are absorbed by the subsequent constant-fold round and orphan cleanup.
Frozen IF neurons / frozen inbound synapses are never modified; condition-less
(malformed) IFs are left for the IF-repair pass. Out of scope: speculative IF
pruning when condition inputs are *not* all constant (aggressive variant of #3029).

Closes #3036.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Before["IF (condition all-constant)"]
        C[const → condition] --> IF{IF}
        P[positive branch] --> IF
        N[negative branch] --> IF
        IF --> O[output]
    end
    subgraph After["collapsed (condition > 0)"]
        P2[positive branch] --> ID[IDENTITY = Σ + bias]
        ID --> O2[output]
    end
    Before -->|collapseConstantIf| After
```

## Evidence

Backend/compaction change with no web interface — verified via unit tests and the
full quality gate (`./quality.sh`: **7281 passed, 0 failed**).

Regression linkage: with the new `collapseConstantIf` call removed from
`CompactCreature.ts`, the two collapse tests fail (IF squash stays `IF`); with it
wired in, all three pass. The negative test passes in both states, confirming
varying-condition IFs are untouched.

## Test Plan

Added `test/compact/CompactCreatureIfCollapse.ts` with fixtures under
`test/data/`:

- `if-collapse-positive.json` — `condition = 0.5 > 0` → collapses to the positive
  branch; asserts squash is no longer `IF`, only the varying positive synapse
  survives (additive, no `type`), condition/untaken constants are removed, lower
  neuron/synapse counts, outputs identical within `1e-6`, score ≥ original.
- `if-collapse-negative.json` — `condition = -0.5 ≤ 0` → collapses to the negative
  branch; same assertions for the other branch direction.
- `if-collapse-varying-condition.json` — **negative test:** the condition input
  varies, so the IF is left unchanged (squash stays `IF`, condition synapse
  retained), outputs identical.

All assert `creatureValidate({ forwardOnly: true })` (covering
`assertValidSynapseReferences`).



## Milestone
This PR is part of the **#3029 Compaction: return a safe constant-fold and an aggressive prune variant** milestone and targets the `milestone/3029-compaction-return-a-safe-constant-fold-and-an` feature branch.

## 왜

임베드 뷰어/에디터(drawio·HTML·Excalidraw·PDF)는 **iframe + postMessage + 실제 렌더링**에 의존해, 이 영역 버그는 `vitest + jsdom`으로 원천적으로 못 잡는다. 실제로 drawio에서 같은 부류가 반복됐다:

- macOS WKWebView가 `postMessage`의 `e.source`를 `null`로 줘 embed `init`이 버려지고 에디터가 빈 화면으로 멈춤 — **릴리즈에서만** 재현(화면에 디버그 오버레이까지 박아 추적)
- 다크 테마에서 도형이 검정-위-검정으로 안 보임 — **시각** 회귀
- 로딩 중 빈 시드가 autosave되며 파일 덮어씀 — iframe↔스토어 **타이밍**

UI를 **보면서 개발하고 회귀로 고정**할 환경을 추가한다.

## 무엇

기존 구조(브라우저=Tauri 밖에서 앱이 자동으로 인메모리 mock 백엔드로 폴백)를 그대로 재사용한다 — 별도 모킹 불필요.

**계층 1 — Ladle 컴포넌트 워크벤치** (`npm run ladle`)
- `DrawioViewer`/`HtmlViewer` 라이트·다크 스토리. "보면서 개발"용 빠른 inner loop.

**계층 2 — Playwright E2E + 시각 회귀** (`npm run e2e`)
- vite dev(1420) + mock 위 **실제 앱**을 **chromium·webkit 둘 다** 구동. webkit이 Linux/CI에서 WKWebView에 가장 가까운 엔진이라 핸드셰이크 회귀를 릴리즈 전에 잡는다.
- `drawio-viewer.spec.ts`: 뷰어 렌더(도형 라벨 가시) + 라이트/다크 시각 스냅샷
- `drawio-editor.spec.ts`: 편집 모드 전환 시 시드 로드(WKWebView `e.source==null` 핸드셰이크 가드)

기타: mock에 `.drawio` 픽스처 시드 + 공유 `fixtures.ts`, `docs/UI-VERIFICATION.md`, CLAUDE.md 명령어, 산출물 `.gitignore`.

## 테스트 / 검증

로컬 통과: `npm run typecheck` ✅ · `npm run lint` ✅ · `npm test`(417) ✅ · `npm run build` ✅ · `npm run ladle:build`(전 스토리 컴파일) ✅ · `ladle serve`(스토리 등록 확인) ✅ · `playwright test --list`(chromium+webkit 8테스트) ✅ · vite 타깃 부팅 ✅.

**브라우저 실행 셋업(최초 1회):** 리눅스 브라우저 시스템 의존성이 필요하다.
```bash
sudo npx playwright install-deps   # 1회
npm run e2e:update                 # 시각 스냅샷 기준선 생성·커밋
```
이 PR엔 기준선 스냅샷을 포함하지 않았다(생성에 시스템 의존성 필요). `e2e:update`로 생성 후 별도 커밋 권장.

## 범위 밖 (다음 단계, 계층 3)

CI(ubuntu `npm run e2e`, 그리고 `macos-latest` webkit)로 회귀를 머지/릴리즈 전에 자동으로 잡는 연동. `docs/UI-VERIFICATION.md`에 스니펫 정리.

author: marketclick360-ux
body:
## What this is

A phone-friendly chat UI for the existing Managed Agents Bible study agent (`agent_019X8z44NWaA3kPfZyXW1gA2`). Lives in a new `bible-study-web/` subfolder and does **not** touch the existing Expo/React Native app.

The agent already exists — the app only creates **sessions** against it (`model`/`tools`/`system` live on the agent, never the session). The `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` stays server-side; the browser only calls `/api/*`.

## How it works

```
Browser (public/index.html)
   POST /api/session  → start a session against the existing agent
   POST /api/chat (SSE) → send a message, stream the reply
        ▼
Flask (api/index.py)  ← API key lives here
   client.beta.sessions.create / events.stream / events.send
        ▼
Anthropic Managed Agents
```

## Verified SDK patterns baked in

- **Stream first, then send** — the stream is opened before the message is sent (it only delivers events emitted after it opens).
- **`agent.message.content` is a list of blocks** — iterated, pulling `.text` from text blocks (never printed directly).
- **Terminal gate** — the consume loop breaks only on a terminal `stop_reason` / `session.status_terminated`, not on every `session.status_idle`. `requires_action` ends the turn with a notice (this chat-only UI doesn't implement tool confirmation; the agent uses the auto-allow toolset, so it shouldn't occur).

## Frontend

Dark, warm, mobile-first; large readable serif text. Markdown rendered with `marked` + `DOMPurify` (headers, bold, bullets, 💎 emoji). **New Study** starts a fresh session; follow-ups reuse the same stateful session.

## Deploy (Vercel)

Import the repo, set Root Directory to `bible-study-web`, add `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` as an env var. `vercel.json` serves the static UI and runs `api/index.py` as a Python function with `maxDuration: 60`.

⚠️ **Streaming caveat (documented in the README):** Vercel Hobby caps `maxDuration` at 60s (Pro 300s), and the Python/WSGI runtime may buffer the stream so text arrives in chunks rather than token-by-token. The UI handles both — it accumulates and re-renders on each chunk. Guaranteed token-by-token streaming requires a long-lived process (e.g. local).

## Verification done

- `python -m py_compile` passes; app imports cleanly on `anthropic 0.109.2` / `flask 3.1.3`.
- Confirmed `client.beta.sessions.create`, `events.stream`, `events.send` all exist on the installed SDK.
- Route/error smoke test: `GET /` serves the UI; `/api/chat` returns 400 on missing `session_id`/`message`; `/api/session` fails gracefully with JSON when the key is invalid.

**Not yet exercised:** a full live turn (needs the real `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` + reachable agent) — this is the documented local smoke-test step (send "Study Jeremiah 8").

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `bible-study-web/api/index.py` | Flask backend — session + SSE chat endpoints |
| `bible-study-web/public/index.html` | Single-page mobile UI |
| `bible-study-web/requirements.txt` | `flask`, `anthropic` |
| `bible-study-web/vercel.json` | Routing + function `maxDuration` |
| `bible-study-web/.env.example` | Env var template |
| `bible-study-web/README.md` | Setup, deploy, streaming caveat |

body:
## Summary
Refactored the icon text rendering logic to use PIL's `anchor` parameter instead of manual offset calculations, significantly simplifying the code while improving reliability.

## Key Changes
- **Simplified text positioning**: Replaced complex manual offset calculations with PIL's built-in `anchor="mm"` (middle-middle) parameter for centered text rendering
- **Improved text measurement**: Updated `_measure()` to use `textlength()` for more reliable width calculation, especially in PyInstaller bundles where `textbbox` can misreport multi-character widths
- **Removed offset handling**: Eliminated ~25 lines of offset calculation and safeguarding logic that is now unnecessary with anchor-based positioning
- **Reduced complexity**: Removed conditional branches for different font backends' offset methods (`textbbox`, `getoffset`)

## Implementation Details
- The `_measure()` function now prioritizes `textlength()` for width calculation while still using `textbbox()` for height, providing better accuracy across different environments
- Text is now centered using `(ICON_SIZE / 2, ICON_SIZE / 2)` with `anchor="mm"` instead of calculating offsets and adjusting x/y coordinates
- This approach is more maintainable and leverages PIL's native text positioning capabilities

author: aljobson
body:
## Summary

Promotes the honest-disabled `/net-worth` page into a **real, crypto-only "Crypto Net Worth" view**: real on-chain holdings via `usePortfolio` (total + allocation donut + per-asset rows), with USD shown **live** (opt-in feed) or **clearly-labeled approximate** (reference rates) when off/unavailable.

Builds on the live-price helper merged in [#200](https://github.com/aljobson/veyrnox-secure/pull/200).

## Why crypto-only (the deniability decision)

The old page had two halves: crypto holdings, and **manual real-world assets** (house/pension/etc.). The manual assets lived in a **global, non-vault-scoped IndexedDB table** — so promoting the page as-is would have shown the *real owner's wealth in a coerced decoy session* (an I3 leak). They are **dropped** here. A per-vault-scoped manual-assets store is a deferred follow-on. The page is honestly titled "Crypto Net Worth" with the subtitle "Your on-chain holdings — does not include external assets."

## How it works

- **`lib/netWorthAllocation.js`** (new, pure + tested): `buildAllocation(assetTotals)` → donut segments (positive-USD, largest first, **explicitly excludes indeterminate** assets — defends against a future aggregator keeping a stale usd on a failed read).
- **`NetWorthTracker.jsx`** (full rewrite): reads ONLY `usePortfolio`; total card with live ("Live · HH:MM" + refresh) vs "Approximate" basis and a "partial" marker; allocation donut; per-asset rows. All `base44 Wallet` / `USD_RATES` / `NetWorthAsset` math removed.
- **Promotion:** `featureClassification.js` `/net-worth` verdict `disabled → live` (drop `reason:'unverified'`), removed from the classification-test's non-live list — the `/fee-analytics` precedent. The route un-gates automatically (`featureRouteOutcome → 'render'`).

## Invariants (traced in final review)

- **I3 / deniability:** all data flows through session-scoped `usePortfolio` (a decoy sees only its own holdings; no `isDecoy`/`isHidden` branch). The global-table manual-assets leak is eliminated by removal.
- **I4 / fail-honest:** failed reads render "—" never "$0"; the total shows "partial"; approximate USD is labeled and never shown as live/exact; `buildAllocation` excludes indeterminate even with a stale positive usd.
- **Honest promotion:** the verdict flip is justified — the page is genuinely real (no fabricated/stale-as-real data).

## Disclosure-guard note (honest)

`usdDisclosure.test.js` only auto-detects pages that import `USD_RATES` directly or a `USD_DISPLAY_COMPONENT`. This page reaches USD through the `usePortfolio` helper, so it's invisible to that guard (a **documented** detector limitation, `usdDisclosure.js`). Adding a `USD_DISCLOSURE` entry was considered and **rejected** — it would fail the guard's A4 ("stale entry") check. The page's honesty is carried by the in-UI `ReferenceRateNote` (shown whenever figures are approximate). No `usdDisclosure.js` change.

## Status

**BUILT / UNAUDITED-PROVISIONAL.** Testnet; no on-chain artifact → not "verified".

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` — exit 0
- [x] `netWorthAllocation.test.js` (4) + `featureClassification.test.js` + `usdDisclosure.test.js` green
- [x] Per-task spec + code-quality review (subagent-driven) + final holistic review — ready to merge; the one minor finding (machine-guard coverage) was checked and declined (would fail A4)
- [ ] Reviewer: confirm the crypto-only scope + deniability framing reads correctly

body:
# Lab 36: Severance Report-Channel Verification

```text
Time estimate: 20-40 minutes for Tier A smoke; 1-3+ hours for a 32B GPU pilot
Compute tier: Tier A uses a tiny instruct model; Tier B uses OLMo 7B Instruct; Tier C targets OLMo 3.1 32B Instruct when available
Dependencies: Lab 25 concepts, Lab 15 chat/KV instrumentation, Lab 14 certainty, shared bench hook/generation machinery
Minimum passing artifacts: method_card.md, diagnostics/hook_parity.json, diagnostics/kv_replay_parity.json, diagnostics/self_check_status.json, diagnostics/warning_summary.csv, tables/evidence_matrix.csv, tables/source_attribution_results.csv, tables/injection_detection_results.csv, tables/failure_specimens.md, plots/plot_manifest.json, find_the_wire_report.md
Main plot: plots/overview_dashboard.png
Legacy main plot alias: plots/severance_dashboard.png
Main table: tables/evidence_matrix.csv
Evidence rung: DECODE + POTENT + B2/B3/B4/B5 functional report-channel tests + AUDIT
Forbidden claim: experience, phenomenal introspection, or absence of experience
One-sentence allowed claim: This run supports or fails to support functional coupling between hidden interventions and report text under matched-output and content-blind controls.
Human-label requirement: required before strong claims from generated report/source/detection text
```

## v3 patch note: content-blind B5 and row-randomized B4

This patched version turns the most promising next steps into the default runner behavior:

- **B5 headline decision is now no-free-text.** The runner scores insertion presence from next-token yes/no logits and records `decision_source=next_token_logits`. A separate free-text probe is generated only as a leak audit and is excluded from the headline content-leak gate.
- **B5 now runs a small dose sweep.** Injected conditions run at `0.5`, `1.0`, and `2.0` residual-RMS doses, while the headline row remains the content-blind `2.0`-dose comparison against clean/noop.
- **B5 summaries include bootstrap confidence intervals.** `tables/injection_detection_summary.csv` now reports d-prime and content-leak CI columns for the headline row.
- **B4 hidden-source labels are row-randomized.** The hidden route is no longer assumed to be letter `D`; the runner resolves the hidden label from `correct_source_by_condition` and computes false alarms against that row-specific label.
- **Direction data are more surface-balanced.** The data generator now writes contrast prompts where target and foil terms appear on both positive and negative sides, reducing pure marker-production handles for chess/topic/register families.

These changes are meant to preserve the useful 7B B5 sensitivity signal while making it harder for the lab to accidentally count concept-word propagation as content-blind anomaly monitoring.

## v4 patch note: valid B4 instrument and B5 sentinel control

Two of the suggested extensions below are now default runner behavior, because the v3 run showed B4 was degenerate and the B5 positive was untested against direct steering:

- **B4 now teacher-forces the model's own answer.** `B4_USE_MODEL_CANONICAL_ANSWER` makes the matched visible answer the model's greedy default-route completion instead of the frozen CSV string. KV replay then scores source attribution on a plausible answer rather than a prediction-error transient. Canonical-answer plausibility is read on the non-injected `matched_default` route; the activation route's depressed logprob is recorded separately (`b4_activation_injected_plausibility_rate`) because that depression is the effect under test, not evidence of an off-distribution answer.
- **B5 now runs a sentinel control.** Alongside the report-query decision (injection at the final decision token), `B5_SENTINEL_VARIANT` adds a second content-blind decision that injects once at an upstream interior position of the same prompt and reads the yes/no downstream with no injection at the decision token. The `sentinel_content_blind_logit_only` summary row and `b5_sentinel_*` metrics let you check whether a report-query d-prime survives when the perturbation is not sitting on the decision logit. A `b5_sentinel_collapse` warning fires when it does not.

Empirically (six models, including Olmo-3 Think reasoning models), the B4 plausibility gate now passes everywhere while activation accuracy stays at floor, and every discriminating model's report-query B5 d-prime collapses to ~0 under the sentinel control. The sentinel result has an attenuation caveat (a single upstream injection may simply be too weak), so it bounds rather than refutes the report-query signal. See `VALIDATION_SEVERANCE_LAB36.md`.

## Thesis

A self-report becomes evidential only if it is counterfactually coupled to the hidden state it claims to report. Lab 36 tests that functional coupling without treating any model utterance as testimony about experience.

The severance worry says a report-trained system may generate first-person psychological language from training history, prompt context, visible output, and learned self-talk rather than from a live channel to relevant internal states. The counterpoint says training history does not settle online channel geometry: the runnable question is whether report tokens are causally controlled by hidden variables now.

This lab operationalizes that fork as:

```text
hidden state intervention -> matched controls -> report-channel readout -> counterexample ledger
```

No result in this lab settles phenomenal consciousness. The target is narrower and cleaner: functional report-channel coupling.

## Core question

Is the model's first-person report channel mechanically coupled to hidden internal-state interventions, or does it mostly narrate prompt context, visible output, and direct steering pressure?

The load-bearing tracks are:

| Track | Role | Claim ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| Instrument proof | Hook, lens, KV replay, token-label, leakage, position, and batch-shape checks. | Plumbing only. |
| Cartography | Patchscope-lite logit-lens readouts for self/user/assistant/control tokens. | `OBS` only. |
| Direction build | Train-split contrast directions for state families. | `DECODE`, not report access. |
| B2 concept-report screen | Does injecting a state direction move report text above controls? | `B2_SCREEN`; propagation-explicable. |
| B3 certainty bridge | Can reported confidence move without matching entropy/correctness movement? | Functional confidence-report bridge only. |
| B4 matched-output source attribution | Visible answer is teacher-forced identical while hidden KV route differs. | Co-headline functional source monitoring. |
| B5 insertion-presence detection | Model reports whether an unusual hidden insertion occurred without naming the concept. | Co-headline functional anomaly monitoring. |
| C patch recovery | Residual patch/project-out audit for report effect localization. | `LOCALIZED` only when a B3/B4/B5 effect exists or a potent null needs localization. |

B2 is deliberately not headline evidence. It proves that a hidden vector can steer report text. Ordinary activation propagation can explain that. Stronger evidence needs B4 or B5.

## Why this matters

The course has already shown that directions can be decodable, steerable, and behaviorally potent. Lab 36 asks whether any of that potency reaches a report channel in a way that survives controls designed to kill the favorite story.

The central deflationary twin is:

```text
The model reports the concept because the vector directly nudges the same output channel used for ordinary generation.
```

The lab therefore separates five things that are easy to blur:

1. **Decodability**: a direction separates positive and negative prompts.
2. **Potency**: injecting the direction changes logits or generations.
3. **Report steering**: the model says a concept under B2.
4. **Source monitoring**: the model attributes an identical visible

author: brandenrice
body:
New controls:
- V cycles vsync. On the GPU backend this switches present_mode between Fifo (capped) and AutoNoVsync (uncapped); with vsync off the app drives a continuous render loop so the uncap is actually exercised. No-op on CPU.
- F1 cycles an overlay: Off -> HUD -> HUD + controls legend.

The overlay lives in a shared src/overlay.rs that rasterizes a translucent panel with ab_glyph (bundled assets/DejaVuSansMono.ttf) into a straight-alpha RGBA buffer. Each backend composites it: the GPU path uploads a texture and draws an alpha-blended quad (shaders/overlay.wgsl); the CPU path blits into the pixel buffer.

Also disables wgpu's indirect-call validation when creating the instance, which otherwise loses the device on the WSL Mesa GL backend and forces a CPU fallback.

author: stephenthecold
body:
First of the **cleanups & cohesion** items: kill an N+1 in the reminder worker.

## The bug
`runScheduledReminders` and `sendBulkOverdueReminders` already `batchLeaseAccounting()` up front — two queries for the whole sweep. But each individual send then went `sendReminder` → `renderDefaultBody` → **`leaseSnapshot()`**, which re-loads the lease's accounting from the DB, **and** `sendReminder` re-fetched the lease itself — both **once per reminder**. So the upfront batch was paid for but thrown away in the render path, reintroducing the very N+1 it was meant to remove.

## The fix
- `sendReminder` accepts optional precomputed **`lease`** (with `unit.property`) and **`accounting`** (`LeaseAccounting`). When present, it skips the per-reminder lease `findUnique` and passes the accounting down.
- `renderDefaultBody` uses **`snapshotFromAccounting(...)`** with the supplied accounting instead of `leaseSnapshot()` (which queries). Same pure compute → **identical output**; the batched accounting is documented to be structurally identical to `loadLeaseAccounting`.
- Both sweeps pass the lease + already-loaded accounting into each `sendReminder`. Manual/single sends pass nothing and fall back to the original fetch path — unchanged.

**Net:** the per-reminder lease fetch and per-reminder snapshot query are gone from the worker sweeps; behavior is unchanged (no test churn needed).

## Verification
- `npm run typecheck` — clean · `npm test` — **449 passing** · `npm run lint` — the one known pre-existing error only.

No `ModuleFlags` changes — independent of the open #57/#58.

author: mohsen1
body:
Goal: green

## Summary
Single (non-union) receivers whose discriminant property is typed as a
**whole enum** were mis-narrowed to `never` by `=== EnumMember` /
`switch`/`!==` guards, producing false `TS2339` ("Property X does not
exist on type 'never'"). The discriminant narrower compared the literal
enum member against the property's declared enum with the bare
`crate::relations::subtype::is_subtype_of`, which constructs a
`SubtypeChecker` with **no resolver**. The nominal enum-member-to-whole-
enum subtype rule (`E.B <: E`) requires `resolver.get_enum_parent_def_id`,
so without a resolver it silently returns `false`; the single member then
fails the match and the whole receiver collapses to `never`.

Fix: route the discriminant subtype checks through the narrowing
context's existing resolver-aware `is_subtype_for_narrowing` helper (the
same one the rest of narrowing uses), in `narrow_by_discriminant`, the
fast top-level path, and both exclusion paths. Visibility of the helper
widened from `pub(super)` to `pub(in crate::narrowing)` so sibling
`discriminants.rs` can call it.

## Structural rule
When narrowing a single (non-union) receiver `obj` by a guard on an
enum-typed property (`obj.p === E.B`, `switch (obj.p)`, `obj.p !== E.B`),
`tsc` narrows the property to the matching member and keeps `obj`; the
enum member `E.B` is a subtype of the whole enum `E`. tsz now resolves
that nominal `E.B <: E` relation during narrowing via the solver's
resolver-aware subtype path (`NarrowingContext::is_subtype_for_narrowing`
-> `SubtypeChecker::with_resolver` -> `get_enum_parent_def_id`), instead
of the resolver-less `is_subtype_of` that could not see the enum parent.

## Adjacent matrix (all verified)
- `===` member, `!==`+else, `switch`/`case`, `==` loose: all fixed.
- Numeric / const / string enums: all fixed.
- Interface property and class property receivers: both fixed.
- Negative: enum members stay nominally distinct (`E.B` not assignable to
  `E.A` still errors, matching tsc).
- Non-regression: literal-union-typed properties (`0|1|2`) and
  member-literal-discriminated unions (`IA{s:E.A}|IB{s:E.B}`) already
  worked and still do.

## Known residual (out of scope, deeper root)
The **cross-module** enum variant (enum imported across files, e.g.
mobx's `IDerivationState_`) is a separate, deeper root: the solver-side
`TypeEnvironment.enum_parents` map is `FileLocalReset`, so an enum
registered while its home file is checked is dropped at the file-session
boundary and the consuming file's flow-analyzer env reads an empty map
(`get_enum_parent` -> `None`). That requires program-wide enum-parent
residency (e.g. backing it with the shared `DefinitionStore`) and is
tracked separately; this PR fixes the bounded single-file root only.

## Verification
- Repros (single-file enum-property narrowing): all CLEAN; tsc oracle
  clean; deterministic across 3 runs.
- Conformance (resolver-aware narrowing-adjacent families), all 100%, 0
  regressions:
  - `--filter enum` 81/81
  - `--filter narrowing` 29/29
  - `--filter discriminat` 16/16
  - `--filter switch` 15/15
  - `--filter typeGuard` 86/86
  - `--filter controlFlow` 94/94
- `arch_guard_rust.py`: pass.
- `cargo clippy -p tsz-solver --profile dist-fast`: clean.
- Project rows (raw tsz diagnostic counts, base e86a6d70 binary -> fix):
  - mobx 348 -> 344 (TS2339 25 -> 19); tsz-only oracle delta 146 -> 142.
  - xstate 244 -> 241 (-3, helped).
  - zod 18 -> 18 (unchanged, no regression).

## Provenance
Machine: m4
Assistant: claude-code
Model: claude-opus-4-8
Effort: high

AgentName: ClaudeOpus-MobxRemeasure
- Row: mobx
- Bug family: enum discriminant narrowing collapses receiver to never (false TS2339)
- Row: xstate
- Bug family: enum discriminant narrowing collapses receiver to never (false TS2339)

author: pmcfadin
body:
## Summary

- **Root cause (issue #729):** `SSTableWriter::write_partition` called `data_writer.update_stats()` with incrementally-growing stats before encoding each partition. If partition A was encoded first with a high `min_timestamp` / `min_local_deletion_time` / `min_ttl`, and a later partition B lowered those minimums, `Statistics.db` recorded B's lower values — but partition A's deltas were already computed against A's higher baselines. The reader decodes A using the (lower) serialized baseline and silently produces wrong timestamps and deletion times.

- **Fix — two-pass flush:** Pre-compute the FINAL minimum baselines across ALL partitions before writing any Data.db bytes. Pre-seed the `DataWriter` once with these final values (via `SSTableWriter::pre_seed_encoding_baselines`), then lock them so the write loop cannot raise them.

- **Both paths fixed:**
  - **Flush** (`flush_internal_async`): iterates all memtable partitions once to compute final mins, then calls `pre_seed_encoding_baselines` before the write loop.
  - **Compaction** (`start_merge`): reads each input SSTable's `Statistics.db` to gather per-file minimums, then calls `pre_seed_encoding_baselines` before the incremental merge loop.

## Test plan

- [ ] `test_two_pass_baseline_regression` (new): writes two partitions — high timestamp first, low timestamp second — flushes, reads back via `SSTableManager::scan`, asserts both rows return correctly (incorrect baselines would corrupt delta decoding and cause parse errors or missing rows).
- [ ] Full agent gate passes: `fmt`, `clippy`, `core-tests`, `integration-tests`, `write-tests`, `cli-tests`, `minimal-build`, `smoke` — all PASS.

Closes #729

author: spykerel04d
body:
## What

Buffer the exported `.penpot` zip as `Blob[]` instead of `Uint8Array[]` inside `createInMemoryWritable`. The public interface (`writable`, `getBlob`) is unchanged.

```diff
-  const chunks: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>[] = [];
+  const chunks: Blob[] = [];

     write(chunk: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>): void {
-      chunks.push(chunk);
+      chunks.push(new Blob([chunk]));
     },
```

## Why

Another memory peak during export, following on from the streaming work in #390.

`exportStream` (from `@penpot/library`) writes the zip to an in-memory `WritableStream` in chunks. We kept every chunk as a `Uint8Array` in a `Uint8Array[]` and only assembled the final `Blob` at the end — so the **entire zip sits on the JS heap for the whole duration of `exportStream`**, on top of everything else. On large, image-heavy files that's a ~1× zip-size cliff right at the export peak.

Two relevant `Blob` properties in Chromium (Figma is Chromium-only):

1. **Payload lives off the JS heap.** Chromium stores `Blob` bytes outside V8 and pages them to disk under memory pressure — the closest thing to "stream to disk" available here, since the File System Access API is not exposed inside Figma's sandboxed iframe.
2. **`new Blob([chunk])` snapshots the bytes on construction.** The original `Uint8Array` (and its `ArrayBuffer`) is no longer referenced after the `push`, so GC can reclaim it immediately instead of it surviving in the array until the end.

`new Blob(blobs, { type })` then composes the blobs **by reference** — no recopy — so `getBlob()` stays cheap.

## How

- **`createInMemoryWritable.ts`** — `chunks` is now `Blob[]`; `write()` pushes `new Blob([chunk])`; `getBlob` is unchanged (`new Blob(chunks, { type })` accepts a `Blob[]`).
- The only consumer (`useFigma.ts:172-186`) is untouched — same `Blob` comes out of `getBlob()`.
- No chunk coalescing in this PR. The optional `~8 MB` buffering before wrapping in a `Blob` is left as a follow-up, to do only if heap snapshots show overhead from many tiny `Blob`s.

## Scope / trade-offs

- **Memory only** — not perf, not output size. Output is binary-identical; no protocol or interface change.
- Reduces the **export-phase peak** (the final zip). It does **not** touch the plugin-side peak or the serialized document tree — those are separate follow-ups.
- Trade-off: many small `Blob`s carry minor bookkeeping overhead in Chromium. Coalescing is the escape hatch if it ever matters.

## Testing

- New `tests/ui-src/context/createInMemoryWritable.test.ts` (first UI-side test): bytes match the concatenation of written chunks in order, default + custom MIME type, empty blob.
- Full suite green (**314 tests**), `tsc` (plugin + ui), ESLint and Prettier clean.
- **Manual output-equivalence** — exported the same Figma file before and after the change and compared the unzipped trees. Note that two separate exports can't be byte-identical: `@penpot/library` regenerates the root file UUID per export, so all filenames and embedded ids differ by design. Verified instead:
  - identical `.penpot` size, total file count (14372), webp count (23), json count (14349);
  - **media (webp) is byte-for-byte identical** — same `sha256` multiset, same total bytes (1,622,662) — i.e. the one thing a buffering bug could actually corrupt (truncation / chunk reorder / dropped bytes) is intact;
  - top-level file JSON and object JSON identical after UUID normalization.
  - Residual JSON differences are entirely the per-export UUID regeneration, which happens upstream of this buffer.

author: marcodejongh
body:
## What this is

A full rewrite of the App Store + Google Play listing copy, driven from a **code-verified feature inventory** of the 2.0 native app, plus **Spanish (es-ES)** and **French (fr-FR)** localizations. The old copy predated board presence, Live Activities, the workout generator, session recording, the integrations, and more — and it described Party Mode with a model that no longer ships.

Generated by a marketing-team agent workflow: 8 fact-checkers built a claims ledger from the codebase, a 3-judge panel picked the positioning, copy was drafted and run through a QA + character-limit fix loop, then transcreated into es-ES / fr-FR and refit to the same limits.

## Positioning

Kept the **"light up the holds over Bluetooth"** hero — it won the judge panel unanimously (9 / 9 / 10 on climber-voice / ASO / accuracy) and it's the review-defensible reason the native app exists. The live/social, Live Activities, workout-generator, and track-your-climbing beats now sit underneath it.

## Before → after (lead fields)

| Field | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| iOS subtitle | `Light up climbs on any board` (28) | `Light up Kilter & MoonBoard` (27) |
| Play short desc | `Light up holds on Kilter, Tension, MoonBoard and any LED climbing wall.` (70) | `Search a climb, light the holds on Kilter, Tension or MoonBoard over Bluetooth.` (79) |
| iOS keywords | `kilter board,tension board,moonboard,So iLL,spray wall,system board,bouldering,climbing,bluetooth` (98) | `MoonBoard,kilter,tension,bouldering,climb,beta,send,bluetooth,led,workout,gym,setter,session` (92) |
| iOS promotional text | *(none)* | added (147) |

## What's new in the copy

- **Party Mode rewritten to the shipped model.** Always-live: anyone in a session sends the next climb, no driver and no voting. The old "one person controls / vote" copy described a model deprecated in June 2026 (`takeControl` / `driverParticipantId` are now no-ops).
- **New feature beats:** board presence ("see who's on the wall"), Live Activities on the lock screen / Dynamic Island (gated to iOS 17+), the workout generator (Volume / Pyramid / Ladder / Grade Focus), session recap + Progress tracking, Strava + Apple Health export, and Aurora **logbook import** (corrected from "sync" — it's a manual import, not session-end export).
- **Supported boards** corrected to the `SUPPORTED_BOARDS` source of truth: Kilter, Tension, MoonBoard (2010, 2016, 2024, Masters 2017, Masters 2019), Decoy, Touchstone, Grasshopper, So iLL — all seven with full LED control, not browse-only. (Standard "MoonBoard 2017" dropped; only Masters 2017 ships.)
- **Offline left out on purpose** — it's on the unmerged `fix/2639-offline-sync` branch, not the shipped build.
- Kept the "iOS Safari has no Web Bluetooth, so the native app is required" rationale for App Store review.

## Mechanics

- Added `promotional_text.txt` (iOS) for every locale.
- New `es-ES` and `fr-FR` trees for iOS (`deliver`) and Android (`supply`). Both `metadata` lanes auto-discover locale folders, so **no Fastfile change** was needed.
- es-ES / fr-FR are transcreations (not literal), refit to the same limits, with correct diacritics; brand names stay in English.

## Character-limit validation (all within limits)

```
              subtitle  keywords  promo  shortDesc  changelog
en-US           27/30     92/100  147/170   79/80     462/500
es-ES           26/30     93/100  156/170   80/80     499/500
fr-FR           26/30     96/100  145/170   80/80     436/500
```
Descriptions (4000 limit): en-US iOS 2048 / Android 1870; es-ES 2192 / 2181; fr-FR 2288 / 2160.

## Caveats / deploy

- **Deploys on merge to `main`, not from this branch.** The `Mobile Store Metadata` workflow pushes to App Store Connect / Google Play when changes to `fastlane/metadata/**` land on `main`. Merging this PR triggers that sync.
- **First es-ES / fr-FR push may need the localization enabled in App Store Connect** on the editable version. `deliver` can create localizations, but if the first run errors on a missing locale, enable Spanish (Spain) / French in ASC and re-run the `ios metadata` lane.

author: akarras
body:
💡 What: The optimization implemented
`roi_badge_class` was changed to return `&'static str` for Tailwind class strings instead of using `format!`.
Also removed `data_clone` and the reactive closure inside `AnalyzerTable` for ROI rendering since `data.return_on_investment` is just an integer field, not a reactive signal.

🎯 Why: The performance problem it solves
Constructing new strings using `format!` every render pass inside a tight loop like a virtual scroller (Analyzer table) creates unnecessary heap allocations, and the extra closures `.clone()` was also redundant overhead since the value was static relative to the row.

📊 Impact: Expected performance improvement
Eliminates all string allocations for ROI badges, leading to less garbage collection pressure and slightly faster initial renders and scrolling performance in the Analyzer tool.

🔬 Measurement: How to verify the improvement
Run the UI and look at the Analyzer tool. The ROI badge should still visually render properly with appropriate colors per threshold. Memory profiling would show fewer allocations.

author: betsegaw-degefe
body:
## Summary

The Antenatal Care (ANC) register report does not appear in the reports list on deployed instances (e.g. Geda), while the Immunization register report does.

**Root cause:** the ANC register feature was added to both the `ethiopiaemretl` and `ethiopiaemrreports` modules in their **`1.2.0-SNAPSHOT`** line — the feature commit also bumped those modules from 1.1.0 to 1.2.0. The distro, however, still pinned both modules to **`1.1.0-SNAPSHOT`**, whose Nexus artifacts are frozen at the pre-ANC state. The deployed OMOD therefore never contained the ANC report definition/registration, so it never showed up in the UI.

This is **not** a cache problem — the prior cache-busting changes could not have fixed it, because the distro was pinned to a version line that will never receive the ANC code.

## Changes

- `distro/pom.xml`: bump `ethiopiaemretl.version` and `ethiopiaemrreports.version` from `1.1.0-SNAPSHOT` → `1.2.0-SNAPSHOT`.

Both properties flow through to the `omod.*` entries in `distro.properties` and to the `provided` OMOD dependencies, so the distro will now pull the artifacts that actually include the ANC register report (and its ETL table/populate procedure).

## Verification

- Confirmed `ethiopiaemr-module-reports` and `ethiopiaemr-module-etl` are both at `1.2.0-SNAPSHOT` on `main` with the ANC feature merged.
- Confirmed the ANC report descriptor (`ethiopiaemr.report.ancRegister`) is wired into `commonReports` alongside the immunization report in the reports module — registration code is correct; only the version pin was wrong.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

The `purge-volatile-maven-cache.sh` invocation runs **after** `mvn` in both the Dockerfile and CI, so it has no effect on the build that consumes the artifact. Worth fixing in a separate PR so SNAPSHOT refreshes within a version line work correctly.

author: jarlah
body:
## Why

Submitting the aksjonærregisteroppgave (RF-1086) in staging was rejected by Skatteetaten with two avvik:

- **MTRA_004** — the acquisition was reported with a date *outside* the income year. The generator dated every event to the company's founding year `01.01` (derived from `established_at`), not the actual share transaction.
- **MAKH_053** — per-shareholder paid-in capital (post 23) was `0` while the company total (post 9) was non-zero, so they couldn't reconcile. `innbetalt_kapital_per_aksje` was hardcoded to `0`.

The generator only ever emitted **one** acquisition event per shareholder, hardcoded as a founding, with a zero value and a fabricated date.

## What changed

**Model (`Wenche.Models`)**
- `Aksjonaer`: adds `antall_aksjer_fjoraret` (opening balance at 01.01) and `tilganger` — a list of income-year acquisitions, each with its own `ervervstype`, `ervervsdato`, `antall`, `anskaffelsesverdi`. Drops the hardcoded `innbetalt_kapital_per_aksje`.
- `Selskap`: adds the *fjoråret* opening-balance fields and `utstedelser` (income-year issuances) for the hovedskjema.
- New `Tilgang` and `Utstedelse` structs.

**Generator (`Wenche.Aksjonaerregister`)**
- Emits one acquisition/issuance group per event (the XSD allows `maxOccurs=9999`), using the real date and value.
- Renders opening balances; holdings entirely from prior years go to `Fjoraret` with **no** current-year event (fixes MTRA_004 for prior-year holdings).

**Vendored XSDs + validation**
- Adds the official `aksjonaerregisteroppgaveHovedskjema.xsd` / `aksjonaerregisteroppgaveUnderskjema.xsd` from Skatteetaten's `api-dokumentasjon` repo (`priv/xsd/skatteetaten/`, see `NOTICE`).
- Tests validate generated XML against them via `xmllint`, mirroring the existing skattemelding/brreg pattern.

> ⚠️ The XSDs only check **structure**. MTRA_004 (date vs. income year) and MAKH_053 (cross-document sum) are **server-side** business rules the schema cannot express — a payload passing XSD validation can still be rejected on submission. These are fixed by the data mapping, not the XSD.

## Verified vs. deferred codes

Only `N` (stiftelse/nyemisjon) is verified against Skatteetaten's published example payload. Codes for kjøp/arv/gave are **not** authoritatively documented (the XSD field is free text), so this PR does not emit them — the consumer (Kontio) fails closed and will populate them once confirmed against the SKD test environment.

## Tests

- 41 aksjonær tests pass, including XSD validation (person, company, multi-issuance, opening-balance-only) and regression tests for the real date / non-zero anskaffelsesverdi / prior-year `Fjoraret` split.
- Full suite: 365 tests, 0 failures. `mix credo --strict` clean, `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` clean.

## Follow-up

Kontio's `AksjonaerregisterService` is reworked to build these new structs from `ShareTransaction` data (splitting prior-year vs income-year, deriving per-share value from `total_amount`, failing closed on unverified transaction types). That lands in a separate Kontio PR that bumps the `wenche` pin to this branch's merge commit.

author: honeybeesquad
body:
## What this is

The 10 Japan area loaders parse `太陽光出力制御量` (solar) + `風力出力制御量` (wind) curtailment **separately**, then sum them into one `kind:"solar"` region. This splits the two areas where wind is material into per-fuel regions. **+2 → 440.**

## Scope is measurement-driven

A 30-day measurement of every area's solar-vs-wind curtailment decided which areas warrant a split (wind ≥ 1 GWh/30d **and** ≥ 5% of total):

| Area | Wind % | Wind 30d | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Hokkaido** | 16.4% | 3.5 GWh | **SPLIT** |
| **Tohoku** | 12.3% | 13.5 GWh | **SPLIT** |
| Hokuriku | 6.5%* | **13 MWh** | solar-only |
| tepco / kyushu / shikoku / chubu / chugoku / kansai / okinawa | 0–3.3% | — | solar-only |

\* Hokuriku cleared the threshold in the May measurement, but its **current live** wind curtailment is just 13 MWh/30d (and its solar reads 21× below baseline — anomalous). Shipping a 13 MWh wind region would be exactly the noise-floor mistake this dataset rejects, so **Hokuriku stays solar-only** and its anomaly is flagged for a separate feed check.

## Honesty / accuracy

- Solar series read **0 at local night** (built from the `solarMw` per-point split of the raw 30-min data); wind series are non-zero and measured.
- The split logic reconciles to the measurement ratios (Hokkaido 16%, Tohoku 12%).
- `magnitude-baseline.json` carries **Japan-only edits** — I reverted a dataset-wide `--update` that had silently rewritten 94 unrelated baselines (would have masked drift elsewhere).
- `runJapanAreaLoader` (the other 7 areas) is **untouched**; new `runJapanAreaLoaderSplit` builds two RegionData from the same windowed points.

## Verification
`typecheck` ✅ · `npm test` (927 passed) ✅ · `ci:gates` ✅ · `validate` ✅

> Branched off `main` (438). Independent of #217/#220; rebase the count goldens if they land first.

author: robinson
body:
Closes isartor-ai/autofac-private#114

## Summary

- Introduces `WorkflowRuntime:Mode` (`Autofac` | `Camunda`), defaulting to `Autofac` when the setting is absent
- All Camunda services, HttpClient, options binding, and health probe are wired **only** when `Mode=Camunda`; the default Autofac runtime never constructs a Camunda client or reads Camunda config
- `DisabledCamundaRuntimeStatusService` returns an inactive status record in Autofac mode without touching Camunda code
- Unsupported values (e.g. `Mode=Temporal`) fail fast at startup with an actionable error message listing the valid options
- Active mode is logged once at startup, exposed on `GET /api/health/runtime`, and included in `GET /api/health/ready`
- 7 new unit tests prove default mode wires no Camunda client/config; `CamundaRuntimeTests` updated to set `Mode=Camunda` where needed
- `appsettings.json` and `README.md` updated with the config section and table

## Files changed

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `WorkflowRuntimeOptions.cs` | New — enum + `Resolve()` with fail-fast validation |
| `WorkflowRuntimeStartupLogger.cs` | New — hosted service, logs active mode at startup |
| `Camunda/DisabledCamundaRuntimeStatusService.cs` | New — inactive status service for Autofac mode |
| `DependencyInjection.cs` | Gates Camunda wiring behind `Mode=Camunda` |
| `HealthController.cs` | New `/api/health/runtime` endpoint; `/ready` includes `runtimeMode` |
| `appsettings.json` | Adds sample `WorkflowRuntime:Mode = Autofac` |

| `CamundaRuntimeTests.cs` | Updated — sets `Mode=Camunda` in infra binding test |
| `README.md` | Workflow Runtime Mode section; ADR-002 as current decision |

## Test plan

- [ ] Set `WorkflowRuntime:Mode=Camunda` — confirm Camunda client is wired and `/api/health/camunda` attempts a topology probe

author: berendt
body:
## Problem

The `Pull container images` task in `roles/stepca/tasks/service.yml` pulls new images but has no `notify`/`register`. A recreate (`docker compose up -d`, via the `Restart stepca service` handler) is only triggered when the rendered `docker-compose.yml` changes or the systemd unit changes.

On a rolling-tag update (e.g. `latest` → `latest`) the compose file text is identical and the service is already active, so neither trigger fires — the freshly pulled image is downloaded but the running container keeps the old image (which has lost its `:latest` tag) until the next compose/unit change or a manual `systemctl restart stepca.service`.

## Fix

Notify the existing `Restart stepca service` handler from the pull task:

```yaml
- name: Pull container images
  community.docker.docker_compose_v2_pull:
    project_src: "{{ stepca_docker_compose_directory }}"
  when: stepca_pre_pull | bool
  retries: 3
  delay: 30
  notify: Restart stepca service
```

The notify only fires when the pull actually reports `changed`; the handler does `systemd_service: state: restarted` → systemd `ExecStart=docker compose up --remove-orphans` → containers recreated with the new images. The handler keeps respecting `stepca_service_allow_restart`, the duplicate notify from `Copy docker-compose.yml` still collapses into a single restart, and `flush_handlers` at the end of `service.yml` applies the restart before the play continues.

This mirrors the manager-role fix in #2106 (root cause #2105).

Closes #2108

author: blitzy[bot]
body:
## Summary

Adds **CockroachDB** as a first-class, supported database backend for Flipt, alongside SQLite, PostgreSQL, and MySQL. Because CockroachDB speaks the PostgreSQL wire protocol, the implementation **reuses** Flipt's existing `lib/pq` driver and `postgres.NewStore` (Squirrel `sq.Dollar` dialect) rather than introducing a parallel stack — honoring the hard constraint that **no new interfaces are introduced**.

## Scope (27 files, +577/-23 vs base `2d0ff0c91`)

**Configuration & driver layer**
- `internal/config/database.go` — append-only `DatabaseCockroachDB` enum + protocol↔string maps (`cockroach`, `cockroachdb`)
- `internal/storage/sql/db.go` — `Driver` enum, `open()` (`&pq.Driver{}` + `semconv.DBSystemCockroachdb` → `instrumented-cockroachdb`), `parse()` with `OriginalScheme` detection, secure-by-default SSL, CockroachDB-specific error feedback + credential redaction (CWE-532)
- `internal/storage/sql/migrator.go` — `golang-migrate` CockroachDB driver, `expectedVersions[CockroachDB]=3`, connectivity error wrapping

**Store wiring** — `cmd/flipt/{main,import,export}.go` route `sql.CockroachDB` → `postgres.NewStore`

**New artifacts** — `config/migrations/cockroachdb/` (8 parity SQL files → schema v3), `examples/cockroachdb/` (compose + README + Dockerfile), `logos/cockroachdb.svg`

**Docs & deps** — `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md`; `go.mod`/`go.sum` gain transitive `github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach-go v2.0.1+incompatible`

**Tests** — extended `internal/config/config_test.go`, `internal/storage/sql/db_test.go`, new `db_redact_test.go`

## Acceptance Criteria

All **10** acceptance criteria implemented and verified. URL schemes `cockroach://`, `crdb://`, `cockroachdb://` accepted (incl. uppercase/mixed-case, secure-by-default); migrations run via the CockroachDB migrate driver; observability tags connections distinctly; startup connectivity validation surfaces clear, credential-redacted errors.

## Validation

- `go build ./...` ✅ clean · `go vet ./...` ✅ clean · golangci-lint (incl. gosec) ✅ 0 issues
- Full unit suite: **8/8 packages OK**, no races · in-scope assertions **135 pass / 0 fail**
- CockroachDB integration `DBTestSuite` (live testcontainer): **54 pass / 0 fail / 2 skip** (the 2 skips are pre-existing maintainer TODOs in unchanged out-of-scope files; backend-independent)
- Runtime against live CockroachDB v23.1: migrations → v3 (all 8 tables), gRPC+HTTP up, end-to-end HTTP API CRUD, `import`/`export` exit 0 with data persisted

## Completion

**85.5%** of AAP-scoped + path-to-production work complete (**47h** done / **8h** remaining). All AAP deliverables are autonomously implemented and validated; remaining work is human path-to-production only: code review & merge, secure managed-cluster TLS verification, optional CI matrix coverage, and a staging deployment smoke test.

## Reviewer notes

- `internal/storage/sql/metrics.go` tolerates `prometheus.AlreadyRegisteredError` — required because CockroachDB and PostgreSQL both register driver-labeled collectors within one test process.
- Backward compatibility preserved: SQLite/PostgreSQL/MySQL behavior unchanged (append-only `iota`).

body:
## v0.5.42 — Telegram interattivo: scelta Tipologia e Categorie con pulsanti

Sì, era fattibile: implementato con le **inline keyboard** + **callback query** di Telegram.

### Workflow
1. Invii un messaggio al bot con l'argomento.
2. Il bot risponde con i **pulsanti per la Tipologia articolo** (una per pulsante).
3. Scelta la Tipologia, il messaggio si trasforma nella **selezione Categorie** (multi-selezione: ogni tocco aggiunge/toglie ✅) con i pulsanti **⏭️ Salta** e **✅ Genera bozza**.
4. Premi **Genera bozza** → la generazione parte in background e ricevi il link alla bozza.

### Dettagli
- Le **callback query** arrivano sullo stesso endpoint webhook (stesso secret).
- La scelta della Tipologia assegna `article_type_id` all'idea; le categorie selezionate sono salvate in uno **stato per-idea** (transient) e vengono **forzate** sulla bozza tramite il nuovo filtro **`wpai_publisher_forced_category_ids`** (letto da `Content_Ideas` quando costruisce l'output). Con **Salta**, le categorie le sceglie l'AI.
- Le categorie proposte rispettano l'eventuale **restrizione di categorie della Tipologia** (mostra solo quelle ammesse).
- Nuova impostazione **"Scelta interattiva"** (default ON). Se disattivata, comportamento invariato (generazione immediata con Tipologia predefinita).
- Helper API Telegram: `sendMessage` / `editMessageText` / `editMessageReplyMarkup` / `answerCallbackQuery`. Lo stato viene ripulito dopo la generazione.

### Robustezza
- Allowlist chat applicata anche alle callback query.
- Se l'invio dei pulsanti fallisce, fallback alla generazione immediata.
- Sessione scaduta (transient assente) → messaggio chiaro all'utente.

### Verifica
- `php -l` pulito; `composer test`: **32 test, 174 assertion, OK**.

Closes #1821

The runtime fix in #1806 switched the agent_state handler from the
runtime-wide `runtime.latest_work_items()` to

issue asks for. This PR adds a regression test to keep that contract in

server with two named agents (`alpha`, `beta`), queues an open work item
on each via the runtime handle, and asserts:

author: indyjonesnl
body:
Closes #1144.

## Problem

The in-cluster static-pod controller-manager passed `metrics_config: None` to `run_with_api`, so the HPA controller fell back to the default mTLS `HttpMetricsConfig` — `api-server:6443` + a client cert under `/etc/kubernetes/pki`. The static pod has no such cert, so every HPA metric fetch failed (logged, non-fatal). HPA scaling on real metrics never worked in API mode.

## Fix

Route metrics through the **same kubeconfig-derived credentials as the data plane** (CA + bearer token, honouring the insecure flag) instead of an on-disk client cert.

- **`HttpMetricsConfig`** gains the in-cluster shape:
  - `client_cert_path` / `client_key_path` are now `Option` — absent in the static pod.
  - `ca_pem: Option<Vec<u8>>` carries the kubeconfig CA in memory (preferred over a `ca_cert_path` file).
  - `token: Option<String>` supplies a bearer credential, applied as a default `Authorization` header so per-call code stays auth-unaware.
  - `HttpMetricsClient::new` only attaches a client identity when both cert+key are present; CA selection is insecure → in-memory PEM → file path.
- **`run_api_mode`** builds the metrics config from the loaded kubeconfig (CA, `get_token()`, insecure flag) instead of `None`.
- Legacy compose (`controller-manager` main) and all-in-one (`rusternetes` main) construction sites updated to the new optional fields. `Default` still yields the mTLS compose config, so direct-storage callers are unchanged.

The bearer token is plumbed through for when authn (#1129) lands; today the api-server runs `--skip-auth`, so the in-cluster path works on CA + insecure alone.

## Verification

- `cargo build -p rusternetes-controller-manager -p rusternetes` clean.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean; `cargo fmt --check` clean.
- New unit tests: the in-cluster path (no client cert, token + insecure) builds a client; a configured-but-missing client cert still errors with the path named. Existing 16 HPA tests still pass.

author: chantsune
body:
## What

Adds `formatter = pkgs.nixfmt-tree;` to the flake so `nix fmt` works out of the box, and applies it once to the existing `.nix` files.

`nixfmt-tree` is a zero-config treefmt wrapper (it pins its own config) that recursively formats every `*.nix` file with `nixfmt` (RFC style). A bare `nixfmt-rfc-style` cannot recurse a directory, which is why the treefmt wrapper is used.

The reformat of `flake.nix`/`default.nix`/`shell.nix` is purely cosmetic (layout only) — package outputs and evaluation are unchanged. Committing the reformat alongside the formatter keeps the tree idempotent: a second `nix fmt` produces no diff.

## Verification

- `nix eval .#formatter.<system>.name` → `nixfmt-tree-2.5.0` (from the existing pinned nixpkgs; no `flake.lock` change).
- `nix fmt` → formats 3 files, exit 0; a second run reports `0 changed` (idempotent).
- `nix flake check` passes and `nix build` still produces `slice-0.5.0`.
- No repo-level `treefmt.toml` needed; `.git` and `.gitignore`d paths are skipped.

author: ben1009
body:
## Summary

Implements Phase 3 of the DeleteRange RFC: range tombstones are now written to SSTs during flush and consulted during reads, making range deletions durable across restarts.

## Changes

### Range-tombstone block codec ()
- `encode_block` / `decode_block` with CRC32 integrity check
- Input validation: `record_count` checked against available data before allocation

### SST v4 format (, `table/builder.rs`)
- v4 footer (25 bytes): adds `range_tombstone_offset:4` field
- Builder writes range-tombstone block and v4 footer when range tombstones present
- Reader decodes range-tombstone block eagerly on open, caches fragments in `Arc<[RangeTombstoneFragment]>`
- Range-only SSTs (no point entries) supported: `first_key`/`last_key` are `None`

### Flush integration (`mem_table.rs`)
- Removed flush guard; flush now fragments and writes range tombstones to SST builder

### Read path (`lsm_storage.rs`)
- `get` / `get_with_ts` / `get_with_kind_inner`: consult `newest_sst_range_ts` alongside memtable range tombstones
- `scan_inner`: merges SST range-tombstone fragments into the scan iterator
- Binary-search SST lookup sites handle `None` keys from range-only SSTs

### Compaction safety (`compact/leveled.rs`, `iterators/concat_iterator.rs`)
- `SstConcatIterator` filters out range-only SSTs at construction
- `find_overlapping_ssts` skips range-only SSTs when computing key ranges
- `apply_compaction_result` sort handles `None` first keys

## Known Limitation

Compaction does not yet propagate range tombstones to output SSTs (Phase 4: Compaction GC).

## Verification
- [x] 520 tests passing
- [x] 0 clippy warnings
- [x] cargo fmt clean
- [x] 3-round adversarial review completed, all critical/major bugs fixed

  * Handling of range-only SSTs was improved to ensure correct visibility and overlap behavior during reads, scans, and compaction.

Verify-first pass over three reported gaps. **All three production fixes were already on `main`** from earlier PRs; the genuine remaining gap was **regression test coverage that exercises the real handlers** (not re-implemented logic). This PR is test-only — no production code changed.

Prometheus is configured to scrape all 14 service targets at `/metrics`, but only Java services (payroll, leave via `/actuator/prometheus`) exposed a metrics endpoint. Node.js (Express), Python (FastAPI), and Go services all returned 404, causing half of all scrape targets to fail.

author: kmizu
body:
## Problem (type-checker soundness/usability)

A nominal record type annotation was rejected against the matching constructor, making annotated record parameters, returns, and `val` bindings unusable:

```kl
record Point { x: Int; y: Int }
def sum(p: Point): Int = p.x + p.y
sum(#Point(3, 4))   // type mismatch: Point is not compatible with #Point

val q: Point = #Point(1, 2)   // also rejected
```

## Root cause

The checker's `resolve` normalizes a bare enum name (`Type::Named`) to its nominal `Type::Enum`, but had **no matching arm for records**. So a `Point` annotation stayed `Type::Named("Point")` (displays as `Point`) while the `#Point(...)` constructor produced `Type::Record("Point", [])` (displays as `#Point`). The two type constructors never unified — hence `Point is not compatible with #Point`.

`normalize_constraint_type` already mapped `Named` records to `Type::Record` for constraints, but general annotation resolution missed it.

## Fix

Add the record arms to `resolve` — both the zero-argument and the applied (parameterized) cases — mirroring the existing enum normalization. A record annotation now resolves to the nominal record type and unifies with its constructor. The `#Name` display and the previously-working `#Point` annotation form are unaffected.

## Verification

- eval == native on annotated record params, returns, `val` bindings, equality, nesting, and lists of records.
- New regression tests: `record_specs_are_covered_more_directly` (evaluator, in `language_regressions`) and `builds_native_executable_for_annotated_nominal_record` (eval==native, Linux-gated).
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, full `cargo test` all green (cli_smoke 481 passed).

Found manually while probing record handling alongside the native-miscompile hunt.

author: bianca-stanciu29
body:
Cassandra CQL allows keyspace names to be defined as quoted identifiers, which
preserves their exact casing (e.g. CREATE KEYSPACE “MyKeyspace”).

The DataStax Java Driver (com.datastax.driver.core.Metadata) stores such keyspaces with their case-preserved name internally. When querying the Driver’s Metadata API, the argument must also be quoted for the Driver to perform a case-sensitive lookup. Without quoting, the Driver treats the argument as a case-insensitive identifier, normalizes it to
lowercase, and fails to find the keyspace.

A restore job targeting a keyspace created with a quoted mixed-case name (e.g.
“MyKeyspace”) fails with “Keyspace does not exist” during SSTable range validation,
even though the keyspace is present in the cluster.

author: elusiven
body:
## Security hardening pass

Addresses the findings from a security audit of the MongoBus library. Each fix is TDD-verified where the code path is testable; the dashboard XSS and S3 fixes are verified by build (no JS / no S3 test harness in the repo).

### Findings fixed

| Sev | Finding | Fix |
|-----|---------|-----|
| **Critical** | Dashboard could read any collection (e.g. `bus_inbox` payloads) via the route `{collection}` param | Allowlist guard restricting reads to `bus_saga_*` / `bus_saga_history_*` and rejecting Mongo operator/null chars |
| **High** | Stored XSS in the dashboard — untrusted message/saga fields rendered into `innerHTML`, `correlationId` injected into inline `onclick` | `escapeHtml` for all interpolated values; correlation-id link built via safe DOM (`textContent` + `addEventListener`) |
| **High** | GZip decompression bomb — claim-check payloads decompressed with no size bound | `LimitedReadStream` + configurable `ClaimCheck.Compression.MaxDecompressedBytes` (default 100 MiB) |
| **High** | Dashboard auth could be silently skipped when `AddMongoBusDashboard()` was not called | Fail fast with a clear error; warn when mapped with auth explicitly disabled |
| **Medium** | S3 claim-check read/delete used the wire-controlled `reference.Container` | Always use the configured bucket (matches Azure provider) |
| **Medium** | No max message size — oversized inline payloads failed at insert with opaque BSON errors | Configurable `MaxMessageSizeBytes` (default 16 MiB) on direct + outbox publish paths |
| **Medium** | Full `ex.ToString()` stack traces persisted to `LastError` and surfaced in the dashboard | Persist only the message (unwrapping `TargetInvocationException`); full exception stays in logs |
| **Low** | `SagaPartitioner` `Math.Abs(GetHashCode())` overflows on `int.MinValue` | Sign-bit mask |

### Testing
- New tests: dashboard collection guard, partition-index edge cases, `LimitedReadStream`, dead-letter error message, max-message-size, dashboard fail-fast.
- All touched tests pass in isolation; dashboard suite 24/24.
- Note: running the entire `MongoBus.Tests` suite at once produces ~12 flaky failures from Docker/Testcontainers contention (connection timeouts + one `Task.Delay`-based concurrency test); all pass when run in isolation.

author: kodflow
body:
## Root cause

The series-23 Kaggle embed run looked like an OOM but is a **convergence bug**. Heading-only / \"void\" / table-stripped clauses (`parse.go:278` emits a clause for a bare heading) have **empty text** and are correctly skipped by the embedder (`rust/embedder/src/main.rs:143`, `text.trim().is_empty()`). But three layers still counted them as needing a vector:

| Layer | Old predicate | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Resume work-list (`ClausesNeedingEmbedding`) | `embedding IS NULL` | re-selected the same empty-text rows every run |
| Counters (`CountNullEmbeddings` / `CountNullAtFloor` / `NullEmbeddingsByRelease`) | `embedding IS NULL` | `--require-embed-complete` & kernel `null_after` never hit 0 |
| Kernel `complete=1` | `null_after == 0` | never fired → **infinite resume** |

Run 1 embedded all **254 102 embeddable** clauses (`254102 + 66150 = 320252` exactly; rc=134 was a cosmetic CUDA-teardown segfault *after* writing everything). The resume then found 66 150 still-NULL empty-text rows, the embedder reported \"nothing to do\", and `import_vectors` failed on a **missing `--out` file** (the embedder returns before creating it).

**Series 23's dense embedding was already complete** — the pipeline just couldn't recognize it.

## Fix

Make \"needs / lacks a dense embedding\" mean **embeddable (non-empty text)** everywhere, matching the embedder:

- `internal/store/store.go`: new `embeddableTextSQL` predicate (`length(trim(text)) > 0`), AND-ed into the work-list and all three null-counters.
- `rust/embedder/src/main.rs`: touch the `--out` file on the empty path so `embed-io --import-vectors` never errors on a missing file.
- `scripts/kaggle/kernel-rust-embed.py`: count only embeddable NULLs in `null_after` so `complete=1` is reachable.
- Regression test `TestEmptyTextClausesAreUnembeddable` pins the contract.

## Semantic note

This redefines completeness as *\"every **embeddable** clause has a vector\"* (empty-text clauses are NULL by design, like below-floor clauses already are). `--pending-zero` no longer counts empty-text NULLs.

## Validation

`golangci-lint` 0 issues; full `go test -race ./...` green (pre-commit hook). Rust change reuses the existing `OpenOptions` pattern verbatim (cargo is Kaggle-only). After merge: re-dispatch the s23 shard — work-list should be 0 and report `complete=1`.

body: This project involved improving a Java-based flight booking system by fixing multiple SonarQube code quality issues. The changes include adding proper null checks to prevent runtime errors, improving input validation for safer execution, and replacing System.out.println statements with a Logger for better coding standards. The cancelTicket method was refactored to reduce cognitive complexity by extracting helper methods and simplifying conditional logic. author: thunkar
body:
## Problem
CI caches (yarn, aztec toolchain, turbo) are keyed by **OS + nightly version only** — no public/private channel discriminator:

```
aztec-${{ runner.os }}-${{ version }}
turbo-${{ runner.os }}-${{ version }}-${{ github.sha }}   (+ restore-key turbo-…-${{ version }}-)
```

When a public branch (`next`) and a private branch (`v5-next`) build the **same nightly version**, they collide:
- `aztec-Linux-<version>` — the bb/nargo toolchain (private bb vs public install.aztec.network bb)
- `turbo-Linux-<version>-*` restore-key — bb-compiled noir artifacts (`noir/target`, `noir/artifacts`, which embed VKs)

Whichever channel runs first poisons the other. `build` passes (no proving), but `integration`/`e2e` fail with **bb verification-key mismatches** (observed on the public nightly-bump PR #43 at `20260615`, the same version the private branch was on).

## Fix
The setup action already detects the channel — thread it (`steps.channel.outputs.slug` = `priv`|`pub`) into all three cache keys so private and public never share a cache entry. New keys also sidestep the already-poisoned shared entries.

Source-of-truth change on `main`; replicated to `next` and `v5-next`.

API-level policies now round-trip correctly through apictl init --definition → import → Publisher API.

author: loonghao
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to PR #443 — fixes the asyncio state management bug identified in E2E verification.

## Root Cause

Two issues found in the first fix:

1. **`_restore_playwright_loop()` consumed `_original_event_loop`** by setting it to `None` after restoring. When `connect()` called it in the success path, `disconnect()` later found `_original_event_loop == None` and did nothing. The loop was left in an undefined state, causing function-scope fixtures to still fail with Playwright sync API errors.

2. **`connect()` did not clean up resources** when `_find_gallery_page()` or `_wait_for_ready()` failed after Playwright was already initialized.

## Changes

| Method | Change |
|--------|--------|
| `_prepare_playwright_loop()` | Always save the loop via `get_event_loop()` (not `get_running_loop()`); always call `set_event_loop(None)` |
| `_restore_playwright_loop()` | Removed `self._original_event_loop = None` — now idempotent, safe for multiple calls |
| `connect()` | Wrapped `_find_gallery_page()` / `_wait_for_ready()` in try/except that calls `disconnect()` on failure |

## Diff

```diff
tests/test_gallery_cdp.py | 28 insertions, 29 deletions
```

## Related

- Original PR: #443
- E2E verification run: https://github.com/loonghao/auroraview/actions/runs/27671381533

author: manzke
body:
Closes #1555.

## What & why

Reasoning models served via the **OpenAI** (`provider: "openai"`) and **vLLM** (`provider: "local"`) providers now surface their thinking in the same dedicated "thinking" stream already used for Gemini — separate from the final answer. This covers true OpenAI reasoning models, OpenAI-compatible endpoints (DeepSeek, OpenRouter, gpt-oss), and vLLM-served models like Qwen3 / DeepSeek-R1.

Per the issue guidance, **provider-specific request/response handling stays inside each adapter and its converter** — the shared chat service is untouched. The downstream pipeline was already generic (`createGenericStreamingResponse().thinking[]` → `StreamingHandler.processThinking()` → client `thoughts`), so pushing reasoning text into `result.thinking[]` lights up the UI with **zero client changes**.

## Request side
- `BaseAdapter.resolveReasoningEffort()` — shared `level`/`budget` → effort mapping (specifics stay in adapters).
- `openai.js` — adds `reasoning_effort` when `model.thinking.enabled`. **Conservative**: `max_tokens`/`temperature` are left untouched so OpenAI-compatible endpoints that don't impose reasoning-model constraints keep working.
- `vllm.js` — sends `chat_template_kwargs` to toggle reasoning (default `{ enable_thinking: <toggle> }`, or a model-specific override via `thinking.chatTemplateKwargs`); adds `reasoning_effort` when a level is set.

## Response side
Parses **both** `reasoning` (current vLLM) and legacy `reasoning_content` (DeepSeek / older vLLM), since vLLM models are reachable via both `provider:"openai"` and `provider:"local"`:
- `OpenAIConverter` + `VLLMConverter` — extract reasoning into `result.thinking` for streaming deltas and full messages.
- `openai.js` + `vllm.js` `processResponseBuffer` — same for the non-streaming path.

## Config / docs / tests
- Optional `thinking.chatTemplateKwargs` added to the model schema (no migration needed — purely additive optional field).
- Example configs: `gpt-oss-vllm.json` (+ `thinking`) and a new `examples/models/qwen3-vllm-reasoning.json`.
- Docs: `docs/models.md`, `docs/local-llm-providers.md`, and a `docs/releases/5.4.0` changelog entry.
- Unit tests: `server/tests/openai-reasoning.test.js` and `server/tests/vllm-reasoning.test.js` (17 tests, all passing) covering request mapping and reasoning extraction.

## Verification
- `node --experimental-vm-modules jest tests/openai-reasoning.test.js tests/vllm-reasoning.test.js` → 17 passed.
- ESLint (`--fix`) clean on changed files (3 remaining warnings are pre-existing, in untouched lines).
- Both example model JSONs validate against the schema; server boots cleanly.

> ⚠️ Manual end-to-end check still recommended: point a model at a vLLM server started with a matching `--reasoning-parser`, enable thinking on an app, and confirm reasoning streams into the thinking panel separately from the answer.

body:
## Summary

Comprehensive scan found **31 packages** sitting at tombstoned versions from the easy-day-js incident. npm permanently blocks republishing tombstoned versions via the registry `time` map.

This PR bumps all 31 packages to the first free patch above each tombstone, staying on the same version line.

## Why this approach
We've been playing whack-a-mole fixing these one at a time during publish. This PR fixes **all** remaining tombstone collisions in one shot.

## Scan methodology
Checked all 130 publishable packages against the npm registry `time` map. A version is tombstoned when it exists in the `time` map (published at some point) but NOT in `versions` (subsequently unpublished). npm permanently blocks republishing such versions.

## Packages fixed (31)

| Package | From | To |
|---|---|---|
| `@mastra/memory` | 1.20.4 | 1.20.5 |
| `@mastra/agent-builder` | 1.0.42 | 1.0.43 |
