# Network Observatory Phase 1: Core Infrastructure & Validator Intelligence

## Overview
Real-time validator intelligence platform monitoring Stellar/Soroban network infrastructure, consensus health, and topology trust relationships.

## Changes

### Database (Prisma)
- **NetworkNode** — Validator registry with 30+ fields (version, quorum, latency, uptime, agreement rate, geolocation)
- **NetworkNodeEvent** — State change tracking (version upgrades, connectivity)
- **NetworkNodeMetric** — Time-series performance metrics
- **NetworkConsensusRound** — Per-ledger consensus data
- **NetworkAlert** — Alert lifecycle management

### Indexer Service
- `network-indexer.ts` — Polls Stellar RPC every 10-60s for node state, consensus rounds, metrics
- `topology-analyzer.ts` — Graph algorithms: quorum intersection, partition detection, centrality scoring, version drift analysis

### API Endpoints (15 Total)
**Node Management:** `/nodes`, `/nodes/:publicKey`, `/nodes/:publicKey/{quorum,events,metrics}`, `/nodes/import`
**Consensus:** `/consensus`, `/consensus/rounds`, `/consensus/history`
**Topology:** `/topology`, `/topology/{quorum-slices,intersection,partitions,centrality}`
**Metrics:** `/versions`, `/versions/{outdated,history}`, `/geography`, `/health`

### Integration
- Registered at `/api/v1/network` in Express router
- Integrated into startup sequence (non-blocking async)
- Zero breaking changes, fully backward compatible

## Acceptance Criteria
✅ NetworkNode fields populated from Stellar network
✅ Nodes fetched every 10-60 seconds
✅ GET /nodes with filtering, sorting, pagination
✅ Quorum topology parsed and stored
✅ Consensus health reflects network performance
✅ Version distribution tracking
✅ Geographic distribution mapping
✅ Node events tracked

## Points
**400/1200 pts** (🔴 Must-Have Tier)

## Testing
bash
npm run build          # Compiles without errors
curl http://localhost:3000/api/v1/network/health  # Health check

## Deployment
bash
DATABASE_URL=postgres://... npx prisma migrate deploy
npm run dev

Closes #325

## Summary

- **`NativeImageHintsConfig`** を追加: GraalVM native image で Hibernate Validator が起動できなかった問題（`Log_$logger` リフレクション未登録）と Flyway マイグレーション SQL がスキャンできなかった問題（`resource:` プロトコル非対応）を修正
- **`application.yml`**: 不要な `hibernate.dialect` 設定を削除（`HHH90000025` 警告の解消）
- **`ecs_service.tf`**: ADR-0028 (i) 実装 — `data "aws_ecs_task_definition" "webapi_pre_apply"` で apply 前の稼働 ECR イメージを読み取り、Terraform が busybox で上書きしないよう保持する
- **`deploy.yml`**: `deploy-webapi` を `apply-tasks` の後に実行するよう変更。Terraform が低リビジョン (busybox) を先に作成し、その後 deploy-webapi が高リビジョン (ECR image) を登録することで `max(revision)` パターンが正しく機能する

## 背景

v0.1.15 デプロイ後、webapi が起動できずにいた。根本原因は 2 つ:

1. **busybox 問題**: `deploy-webapi` と `apply-tasks` が ADR-0028 の設計とは逆順で実行されていた。deploy-webapi (ECR image) が先に高リビジョンを作成 → apply-tasks (Terraform) が後から busybox でさらに高いリビジョンを作成 → `max(revision)` で busybox が選ばれる
2. **Hibernate Validator 起動エラー**: GraalVM native image で `Log_$logger` がリフレクション未登録 + Flyway が `resource:` プロトコルを解釈できず SQL スキャン不可

## Test plan

- [ ] CI (Verify artifacts, compile, spotless) が通ること
- [ ] 所定の手順でデプロイ (tag → Release Build → Deploy)
- [ ] ECS ログで `Started TasksWebapiApplication` が確認できること
- [ ] Flyway マイグレーションが実行されること (`Migrating schema...` ログ)
- [ ] `/actuator/health` が 200 を返すこと

O A3 (600k) assumiu o limite de CPU dos Workers standalone (30s), mas o projeto roda em Cloudflare PAGES Functions (pages_build_output_dir no wrangler.toml), cujo teto é ~50ms por request mesmo no plano pago. 600k (~60-90ms) estourava ("Error 1102: Worker exceeded CPU time limit") → HTTP 500 no login por senha de policiais e admins de banco. Volta a 100k (~10-15ms, valor original comprovadamente funcional) e desfaz o re-hash agressivo de isHashLegado (que somava uma 2ª derivação por login). O comentário foi corrigido com o diagnóstico correto (Pages vs Workers).

author: mvanhorn
body:
## Summary

Adds a way to detect and report `Attachment` rows whose backing file has gone
missing from storage:

- A new `Attachment.file_exists` property that checks the file's storage backend
  (`self.attachment.storage.exists(...)`), treating a blank file name as missing
  rather than raising.
- A `check_attachments` management command that scans finalized attachments,
  prints a tab-separated report (`pk`, `owner`, `path`) of any whose file is
  missing, and exits non-zero with a summary so it can run from cron/monitoring.
- A blank-name guard in `is_in_tmp` so an owned row with an empty file name is
  treated as finalized and reported instead of crashing the audit on
  `FieldFile.path`.

The command uses `select_related(*Attachment.OWNER_MODELS)` to avoid a per-row
owner query when scanning large attachment tables. Scope is intentionally
limited to detection + reporting; the periodic email notifier discussed on the
issue is left to a follow-up since it depends on scheduling choices still under
discussion.

Run it with:

```
python manage.py check_attachments
```

## Why this matters

On long-running servers, attachment files on disk can disappear (manual cleanup,
failed migrations, storage moves) while the `Attachment` DB row still points at
them, so a missing file is only discovered when a user tries to open it. The
`Attachment` model previously had no "does the backing file actually exist?"
check. This gives admins a scriptable audit to surface broken attachments
proactively (#765).

## Testing

- `qatrack/attachments/tests/test_models.py`: `file_exists` true/false/blank-name
  cases, and `is_in_tmp`/`finalized` blank-name safety.
- `qatrack/attachments/tests/test_commands.py`: all-present (exit 0), a missing
  file is reported with a non-zero exit, and tmp/unfinalized attachments are
  excluded from the audit.
- `flake8 --max-line-length=120` clean on all touched files.

Fixes #765

author: markus7017
body:
# Description

Bugfix.

When a Gen2 addon sensor (temperature, humidity, voltmeter, or input) reports a transient read failure, the firmware sends null value fields alongside a read-error indicator.
The binding did not check for this condition and wrote 0 °C / 0 % to the channel instead of preserving the last valid reading.
This fix skips the channel update on read error and prevents \`sensors#lastUpdate\` from advancing — preserving the last-valid-data timestamp.
Channel values remain at the last known reading; no \`UNDEF\` is posted, so rules and persistence are not disturbed.

See #20994.

# Testing

- Tested with DS18B20 and AM2301 sensors on Shelly Plus 1PM and Plus 1 via the Plus Addon.
- To reproduce: briefly disconnect the sensor probe while the binding is running; the firmware emits a read-error on the next poll cycle.
- Expected: temperature channel holds its previous value; \`sensors#lastUpdate\` does not advance during the error and resumes once the sensor recovers.
- 9 new unit tests cover all four addon sensor types (temperature, humidity, voltage, input) for both the error and valid-reading paths.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Implementation done
- [x] Verified by Community
- [x] Documentation is up-to-date

## Closing

- #20994

## Backport assessment

Self-contained bugfix; qualifies for cherry-pick to the patch release branch.

author: mishcazzulani
body:
## Summary

Fixes three related bugs that caused welle-cli to crash after days of operation due to resource exhaustion.

## Bugs Fixed

### 1. CLOSE_WAIT socket leak
`ProgrammeSender::wait_for_termination()` only slept on a condition variable — it never checked whether the TCP socket was alive. Over days, dead sockets accumulated in CLOSE_WAIT until the FD limit was exhausted.

**Fix:** TCP keepalive (`SO_KEEPALIVE`, `TCP_KEEPIDLE=60s`, `TCP_KEEPINTVL=10s`, `TCP_KEEPCNT=3`) on accepted sockets + drain `recv()` on every wait loop iteration to detect peer FIN.

### 2. eventfd leak from std::async
`serve()` used a blocking `accept()` call — stale `std::async` futures were only cleaned up when a new connection arrived. Each async future allocates an internal eventfd that leaked until consumed.

**Fix:** `select()` with 1-second timeout before `accept()`, so cleanup runs every second regardless of new connections.

### 3. MSG_PEEK false negative
`recv(MSG_PEEK | MSG_DONTWAIT)` returned leftover data length instead of 0 even after FIN was received, preventing peer disconnect detection. 614 threads + 611 FDs accumulated over 4 days.

**Fix:** drain-buffer approach — `recv()` into a discard buffer instead of `MSG_PEEK`. Stale data is consumed, and when the buffer is finally empty, `recv()` returns 0 → clean shutdown.

### 4. SIGABRT from uncaught std::system_error
`std::async(launch::async)` throws `std::system_error` ("Resource temporarily unavailable") when the cgroup pids limit is hit. This was not caught, calling `std::terminate()` → SIGABRT crash.

**Fix:** wrap `std::async` in try-catch. Also increased systemd `TasksMax` from default (~759) to 2048.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/various/Socket.h` | + `native_handle()` for select() |
| `src/various/Socket.cpp` | + `#include <netinet/tcp.h>`, keepalive in accept() |
| `src/welle-cli/webprogrammehandler.h` | removed `const` from `wait_for_termination()` |
| `src/welle-cli/webprogrammehandler.cpp` | drain recv() instead of MSG_PEEK, removed const |
| `src/welle-cli/webradiointerface.cpp` | `select()` timeout, deferred handling, try-catch |

5 files changed, 79 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)

## Testing

Running 24/7 on a Raspberry Pi with two ffmpeg clients reconnecting hourly. Previous crashes occurred within 1-4 days. Current uptime: stable.

## Notes

- The `#include <netinet/tcp.h>` was needed because modern glibc no longer transitively includes it via `<netinet/in.h>`.
- An `#include <sys/select.h>` was added for `select()`/`fd_set`.
- `TasksMax=2048` is set in the systemd unit to prevent SIGABRT from thread creation failures.

author: ideotion
body:
Log-driven session: analysed the five 2026-06-17 field exports (keyword log, debug bundle, date diagnostics, network preflight, perf report) against the live ~2.3k-article corpus and fixed what they surfaced. Four focused commits — one critical bug, one regression, two log-driven optimizations. Each verified against the real data and tested.

## 1. 🔴 CRITICAL BUG — `database is locked` at ingest (data loss)

The debug bundle held **163** `OperationalError: database is locked` failures during the collect pass — 87 *link indexing*, 62 *keyword indexing*, plus *when/where/who persistence* — each silently dropping that article's analytics. `collect_perf` proved the contention: writer-gate **peak 17 waiters, 806 contended, max_wait 213 s**.

Root cause: the single-writer gate acquires only on the ORM **`before_flush`** event, but **bulk DML** (`Query.delete()`/`update()`) executes immediately and does *not* fire it. So the idempotent re-index `.delete()` in `index_article` (`KeywordMention`) and `whostore` (`ArticleMentionedPlace`/`ArticleEntity`) grabbed the SQLite write lock **outside** the gate; under the parallel collector it collided with a long-held gate-holder.

Fix: also acquire the gate on **`do_orm_execute`** for DML writes (`is_insert`/`is_update`/`is_delete`). Every write — flush or bulk — now serialises. Reproduced the exact error; both new tests in `tests/test_write_gate.py` fail with the old wiring, pass with the hook.

## 2. 🟠 REGRESSION — source self-names leaking (all-caps acronyms)

The keyword log showed `CORRECTIV` leaking from *Correctiv* (14/14 of its articles). The entity detector keeps acronyms UPPERCASE (2026-06-16 ruling) but `_self_name_forms` is casefolded, so the `normalized in self_forms` check missed it. Fix: compare casefolded (full-form match only, so shared words like `moscow` stay content). Regression test added.

## 3. 🟢 OPT — date-extractor month vocabulary for 11 more languages

Date diagnostics showed near-zero date coverage for languages with real article volume, purely from a missing month table: sr 6.8 %, hu 3.7 %, tr 8.9 %, ro 15.6 %, da 25.8 %, sk/pl/fi/bg ~0 % (all `in_month_vocab:false`). Added native month names for **ro/hu/tr/da/sv/nb/fi/pl/sk/sr/bg** (Slavic genitive + Finnish partitive forms; Latin + Cyrillic for Serbian/Bulgarian) plus a year-first pattern for Hungarian's `2024. október 23.`. **Safe by construction**: a month name only yields a date with an adjacent day/year, so vocabulary raises recall without inventing dates — verified by a precision-guard test (Romanian `mai`=more, Turkish `ocak`=hearth, es/it `marca`=brand all correctly yield nothing).

## 4. 🟢 OPT — keyword stoplist batch (login/subscribe widget chrome)

Per-source concentration suspects surfaced account-wall chrome in ~every article of a source (Le Nouvelliste's `connectez-vous`/`inscrivez-vous`/`gratuitement`, 27/27 articles) + leaked French function words. Added the unambiguous chrome only; dual-use platform names (facebook/twitter…) and content-capable words (comments/follow) are **deliberately left out** for a maintainer ruling, staying visible in the diagnostics.

---

### Not changed (deliberate, flagged for a ruling)
- **Dead `google-hol-*` calendar feeds** (all robots-disallowed): removing them would contradict `configs/calendar_feeds.yml`'s explicit "entries stay listed; the UI shows the honest verdict" design, and the per-feed cost is a cached robots lookup (no network). Left for a maintainer call.
- **`keyword_export` run2 22 s** (perf self-test): same write-contention root as #1; the gate fix reduces it but the encrypted single-connection export contention is a separate, larger thread.

author: mosch
body:
## Summary

Stacked on top of #2. Optimizes the `graphql-monetization-outbound` policy so it stops decoding and `JSON.parse`-ing **every** successful response body just to check for a top-level `errors` array.

This mirrors the approach taken in zuplo/core#8061 for the GraphQL analytics policy: scan the response byte stream for the `"errors"` token as chunks arrive, and skip the expensive decode/parse on the common error-free path.

## What changed

`modules/graphql-monetization-outbound.ts` previously did, on every 2xx response:

```ts
const body = (await response.clone().json()) as { errors?: unknown[] };
hasErrors = Array.isArray(body?.errors) && body.errors.length > 0;
```

That full decode + `JSON.parse` runs even though the vast majority of GraphQL traffic succeeds with no `errors` array.

Now a `readBodyForErrors()` helper scans the cloned body chunk-by-chunk for the UTF-8 `"errors"` token:

- **Scan window (128 KiB):** if the token isn't seen in the leading window, the response is treated as error-free and the rest of the body is never read — no merge, no decode, no parse. This is the hot path.
- **Token found:** the body is buffered (up to a 5 MiB cap) and `JSON.parse`d to confirm a *real* top-level `errors` array. The byte scan over-approximates (`"errors"` can appear nested under `data`), so the parsed structure is re-checked before deciding not to bill.
- **Cross-chunk matching:** match state is carried across chunk boundaries so a token split between two reads (`…"err` / `ors"…`) is still found. Since no proper prefix of `"errors"` is also a suffix, mismatches restart cleanly (no KMP table needed).
- **Stream safety:** the scan reads from a `clone()`; the original response stream flows to the client untouched. The clone's reader is abandoned (not awaited) on early exit to avoid the tee-deadlock.

## Billing semantics (conservative)

Per the existing "bill nothing on any error" design, every uncertain outcome meters nothing rather than risk over-billing:

- non-2xx response → meter nothing
- token found but body exceeds the parse cap → meter nothing
- stream read failure or `JSON.parse` failure → meter nothing
- token absent / empty body → confirmed error-free → **meter the computed meters**

author: tobechukwu278
body:
## Summary

Quick composer posts (from the logged-in home page) were auto-generating bogus titles by truncating content to 60 characters and appending "...", creating a poor UX. This PR removes that auto-generation and handles untitled posts gracefully across feeds and the post detail page.

## Changes

**Backend:**
- `src/models/Post.js`: Removed `required: true` from `title` field, added `displayTitle` virtual that returns a ~60-word plain-text content excerpt when no title is set
- `src/routes/api.js`: Removed auto-title generation from `POST /api/posts` — composer posts now save without a title

**Frontend - Feeds:**
- `home-activity-feed.ejs`: Shows `displayTitle` (content excerpt) when post has no title. Updated `aria-label` on Read CTA accordingly
- `explore-feed.ejs`: Same treatment — content excerpt shown as heading for untitled posts

**Frontend - Post Detail:**
- `post.ejs`: Updated JSON-LD `headline`, breadcrumb `name`, image `alt` text, and H1 heading to use `displayTitle` fallback

## How it works

The `displayTitle` virtual strips HTML tags from content, extracts the first ~60 words, and appends "..." if truncated. This ensures feeds and post pages always show readable content regardless of whether a title was supplied.

## なぜ
GitHub起票 [anthropics/claude-code#69059](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/69059) で、auto-acceptモードが `php artisan migrate:fresh` を確認なく繰り返し実行し、ローカル開発DBを消した事例が報告された(MySQLのbinlogが偶然有効で辛うじて復旧)。核心は「Bashの安全検査は `rm -rf` 等は弾くが、同じ破壊力のフレームワーク/ORMのDBリセットは素通りする」非対称性。
既存の `block-database-wipe.sh` は正確な事故コマンド(`migrate:fresh`)は弾くが、報告者の推奨一覧を実機で点検したところ以下を素通りさせていた。新hookでなく既存hookの被覆の隙間を塞ぐ。
- Laravel: `migrate:refresh`
- Django: `migrate <app> zero`
- Rails: `db:schema:load`
- TypeORM/Sequelize: `schema:drop` / `db:drop`
`tests/block-database-wipe.test.sh` を追加。破壊13件はblock(exit 2)、安全7件(`migrate`/`db:migrate`/`prisma migrate dev`/`typeorm migration:run`等)はallow(exit 0)で、**20件全て期待通り・誤検知なし**。

## Summary
- Preserve the form element during async submit so saved meeting forms can reset reliably after a successful create action.
- Add coverage for `SavedMeetingForm` to verify fields clear and the page refreshes after submit.
- Improve chat stream error handling by reporting AI provider failures as handled telemetry while ignoring client aborts.
- Add route tests for both provider-error and abort cases.

## Testing
- Added unit tests for meeting form reset behavior.
- Added API route tests for AI stream error telemetry and abort handling.
- Not run (not requested)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Localized UI submit handling and observability-only chat error reporting; behavior is covered by new unit and route tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **saved meeting** (and schedule-bot) forms that failed to clear after a successful submit by capturing the form DOM node at submit start and calling **`reset()`** on that reference after the async server action finishes—avoiding a stale **`currentTarget`** after **`await`**.
> 
> Adds a **`SavedMeetingForm`** component test that asserts fields clear and **`router.refresh`** runs after a successful create.
> 
> On **`/api/chat`**, stream **`onError`** now emits **handled** telemetry (**`reportHandledEvent`**, message **`chat_stream_ai_provider_error`**) with model and Timeline AI error tags instead of **`reportCaughtError`**. **Client aborts** (**`AbortError`**) are ignored so navigations away mid-stream are not counted as provider failures. Route tests cover both paths.

body: ## 概述 在 `polar_codes/` 目录下实现完整的极化码（Polar Codes）编译码仿真系统，涵盖构造、编码、多种译码算法及蒙特卡洛实验。 ## 主要模块 - `construction.py` — 高斯近似（GA）极化码构造 - `encoder.py` — Arikan 蝶形编码（等价于 \(x = u F^{\otimes n}\)） - `channel.py` — BPSK 调制与 AWGN 信道 - `decoder_sc.py` — SC 译码（树遍历非递归 + 递归等价实现） - `decoder_scl.py` — SCL / CA-SCL 译码（含 CRC-8） - `decoder_bp.py` — BP 译码（min-sum + 早停） - `simulation.py` — 蒙特卡洛仿真主循环 - `utils.py` — 结果保存、绘图、BPSK 容量限计算 - `verify.py` — 单元测试与数值校验 - `run_exp1/2/3.py` — 三组实验脚本 ## 验证 - 编码器：N=4, u=[1,0,1,1] → x=[1,1,0,1]（与生成矩阵一致） - GA：N=8,K=4 → info=[0,3,5,6] - SC/SCL/BP 无损帧测试全部通过 ## 运行方式 ```bash cd polar_codes pip install -r requirements.txt python verify.py python run_exp1.py # SC 仿真 python run_exp2.py # SCL/CA-SCL 仿真 python run_exp3.py # BP 对比仿真 ``` 设置 `POLAR_QUICK=1` 可启用缩减参数的快速仿真模式（CI 友好）。 ## 输出 实验结果自动保存至 `polar_codes/results/`（CSV 数据、BLER 曲线图、冻结位集合等）。

author: oneilltomhq
body:
## Summary

- `faust2mathdoc` only converted `process.svg` in each mathdoc SVG directory, but `--mathdoc` can emit named `<diagram>expr</diagram>` SVGs that the generated `.tex` references as PDFs.
- Switch the main loop to use the existing `convert_svgdirs2pdf` helper (same approach as `faust2mathviewer`) so every generated `.svg` is converted before `xelatex` runs.
- Add `tests/mathdoc/signalFlowPatternsMathdoc.dsp`, a small repro with multiple `<diagram>` tags.

## Problem

For DSP files with `<diagram>parallel_tank</diagram>` (and similar), `faust --mathdoc` writes SVGs like `parallel-*.svg` under `*-mdoc/svg/svg-*/`, and the TeX output references the corresponding PDFs. The script never created those PDFs, so `xelatex` failed with missing file errors:

```
! LaTeX Error: File `../svg/svg-01/parallel-0x...' not found.
```

## Repro

```bash
faust2mathdoc tests/mathdoc/signalFlowPatternsMathdoc.dsp
```

Before this fix, only `process.svg` was converted (1 PDF for 39 generated SVGs); the named diagram PDFs were missing and `xelatex` aborted. After the fix, all 39 generated SVGs are converted and the PDF builds successfully (46 pages).

## Test plan

- [x] `faust2mathdoc tests/mathdoc/signalFlowPatternsMathdoc.dsp` completes and writes `*-mdoc/pdf/*.pdf`
- [x] Verified 39 `.svg` files and 39 matching `.pdf` files under `svg/`
- [x] Existing `tests/mathdoc/rms.dsp` still builds (no regression)

## Notes

- Inkscape CLI flags left unchanged for compatibility.
- Missing `supertabular` (or similar LaTeX packages) on some systems is a separate dependency issue, not addressed here.

## Summary

Adds a complete Cucumber BDD test suite for a Petstore-style REST API covering pets CRUD operations.

**New test infrastructure:**
- `PetController` — mock REST controller at `/api/pets` with validation (name/status required → 400), not-found handling (→ 404), and paginated list endpoint (`page`, `size`, `status` query params returning `{content, page, size, totalElements, totalPages}`)
- `PetDTO` — model with `id`, `name`, `category`, `status`, `tags`

**21 Gherkin scenarios in `petstore.feature`:**
- **CRUD success**: create (inline JSON + fixture file), read by ID, update, delete (with verify-after-delete)
- **Validation errors**: missing `name`, missing `status`, both missing — asserts error messages in response body
- **Not-found**: GET/PUT/DELETE for non-existent pet → 404
- **Pagination**: page 0 size 2 → 2 items + correct `totalPages`; page 1 → remaining item; beyond-data page → empty content
- **Filtering**: `?status=available` filters list correctly

All scenarios reuse the framework's built-in step definitions (`DefaultRestApiBddStepDefinition`) — no custom glue code needed.

author: corranhornet
body:
## Summary

This PR refactors the MediaUnit model to support polymorphism using inheritance instead of storing book and audiobook-specific properties directly on MediaItem.

A MediaUnit is now represented as either:

* PhysicalBookUnit
* AudiobookUnit

The implementation ensures that only one type-specific value can be supplied.

## Changes

### Domain

* Introduced abstract `MediaUnit` base class
* Added `PhysicalBookUnit`
* Added `AudiobookUnit`
* Removed book/audiobook-specific properties from `MediaItem`

### Validation

Added validation rules to enforce that:

* Exactly one of `PageCount` or `DurationMinutes` must be specified
* Both values cannot be supplied simultaneously
* Empty media units are rejected

### DTOs and Mapping

* Replaced the previous MediaUnit response model with polymorphic DTOs
* Added:

  * `PhysicalBookUnitDTO`
  * `AudiobookUnitDTO`
* Updated Mapster configuration to support polymorphic mapping

### Application Layer

Updated:

* Commands
* Queries
* Handlers
* Service interfaces

to work with the new MediaUnit hierarchy.

### Infrastructure

* Added EF Core migration
* Updated database schema to reflect MediaUnit inheritance model

## Testing

Verified through Swagger:

### Valid Book

Returns:

* `UnitType = Book`
* `PageCount` populated
* `DurationMinutes = null`

### Valid Audiobook

Returns:

* `UnitType = Audiobook`
* `DurationMinutes` populated
* `PageCount = null`

### Invalid Requests

Validation correctly rejects:

* Both `PageCount` and `DurationMinutes`
* Neither `PageCount` nor `DurationMinutes`

## Result

The system now models books and audiobooks as distinct domain concepts while preserving a shared MediaUnit abstraction and enforcing business rules through validation.

### Motivation
- The Pochi adapter treated any bare `~/config.json` file as evidence of Pochi being installed and would back up and write a top-level `mcp` entry into that file, risking mutation of unrelated user configs.
- The change prevents accidental data-integrity/path-confusion by ensuring only genuine Pochi-shaped configs are modified.

### Description
- Change `Exists()` to verify the live config contains a Pochi-shaped top-level `mcp` object instead of returning true on mere file existence (added `hasPochiMCPSection`).

- Preserve the relay-stdio write path and hub-shaped detection by reusing the embedded `jsonMCPClient` semantics (`serversKey: "mcp"`, `urlField: "command"`).
- Update tests in `internal/clients/pochi_test.go` to assert the guarded behavior and adjust the existing relay write test to start with an explicit `"mcp": {}` stub.

- Added `TestPochi_ExistsRequiresMCPSection` and `TestPochi_RefusesToMutateUnrelatedConfig` and updated `TestPochi_AddEntry_WritesRelayStdioUnderMcpKey`, and ran `go test ./internal/clients -run 'TestPochi' -count=1`, which passed.

author: sebulino
body:
## Teil 2 von zwei Forum-Verbesserungen

Avatare im Forum-Thread (und anderswo) nutzten `AsyncImage(url:)` direkt ohne
gemeinsamen Cache. Verlässt man einen Thread und geht erneut hinein, wurden alle
Avatare **neu geladen** und blitzten zuerst als Platzhalter auf.

## Lösung (Entscheidungen: Memory **+ Disk**, **keine** aktive Revalidierung, **app-weit**)

- **`AvatarImageCache`** (`Core/Data/Storage`): zweistufig.
  - **Memory** (`NSCache`) mit synchronem `cachedImage(for:)` → ein bekanntes
    Avatar wird im **ersten Frame** gezeichnet, kein Platzhalter-Flash.
  - **Disk** unter `Caches/avatars` (SHA-256-Dateiname, Trim auf 200, ältester
    zuerst) → überdauert App-Neustart.
  - `image(for:)` löst memory → disk → network. **Keine** HTTP-Revalidierung:
    Discourse-Avatar-URLs enthalten die `avatar_id`, ein neues Bild ist also
    eine neue URL, die den Cache natürlich verfehlt.
- **`CachedAvatarView`** (`App/Views/Components`): Drop-in-Kreisavatar, seedet
  aus dem synchronen Memory-Peek, sonst Platzhalter (anpassbar — Aufrufer mit
  Initialen-/getöntem Platzhalter behalten ihn) + Laden via `.task(id: url)`.
  Cache kommt über einen neuen `avatarImageCache`-Environment-Wert.
- **Wiring:** ein `AvatarImageCache` in `AppContainer`, am Root injiziert
  (`RootView`), und in den Logout-Fan-out (`LogoutOrchestrator`) aufgenommen
  (Avatare sind personenbezogen).
- **App-weit übernommen**, ersetzt die wiederholten AsyncImage-Avatar-Blöcke in
  TopicDetailView, ForumView, HomeView, MessagesView, UserProfileView,
  ProfileView und MessageThreadDetailView (dessen eigener `@State`-Avatar-Loader
  entfällt zugunsten des geteilten Caches). Netto **−95 Zeilen**.

## Test plan
- [x] `xcodebuild ... test` (seriell) — **TEST SUCCEEDED**, volle Suite grün
- [x] `LogoutOrchestratorTests` an die neue Abhängigkeit angepasst
- [ ] Manuell (Simulator): Thread öffnen → Avatare laden einmal; zurück → erneut
      derselbe Thread → Avatare **sofort** da (kein Flash). App neu starten →
      Thread öffnen → Avatare sofort aus Disk. Logout → `Caches/avatars` geleert.
      (Reviewer)

author: fdelbrayelle
body:
## Summary

Ported from kestra-io/plugin-ee-kubernetes#139.

When the worker liveness coordinator restarts a task that was running on an existing pod, two code paths blocked for the full `waitUntilRunning` budget instead of returning immediately:

- **RC1 ()**: The resume guard only checked for `RUNNING` phase. Pods in `Succeeded`, `Failed`, or `Unknown` phase fell into the init-container / `waitForPodReady` block, timing out instead of skipping straight to log collection.

- **RC2 (`PodService.waitForContainersStartedOrCompleted`)**: No fast-path check before starting the watch loop. A pod already in `Running` or `Succeeded` state that emits no new events drained the full `waitUntilRunning` budget before timing out.

### Changes

- `PodService`: add `isCompletedPhase` / `isStartedOrCompleted` helpers; add fast-path GET before the watch loop; check condition (not just existence) on the fallback GET after each chunk timeout; add `Logger` parameter for debug-level watch error logging.
- `PodCreate`: extend the resume phase guard to also skip completed phases via `isCompletedPhase`; pass `logger` to `waitForContainersStartedOrCompleted`.

## Test plan

- [ ] All 6 unit tests in `PodServiceTest` pass (fast-path Succeeded, fast-path Running, fallback-GET after timeout, deletion on fast-path, deletion after watch, existing `waitForPodReady` regression)
- [ ] No integration test regressions

author: glyh
body:
## Summary

Fix CI failure in `dev unit-tests` job where `dune runtest src/app/mina_healthcheck` failed with exit 127 (`dune: command not found`), and refactor duplicated CI job definitions into a shared library.

## Problem

In PR #18746, mina-healthcheck tests were wired into the DaemonUnitTest buildkite job by appending ` && dune runtest src/app/mina_healthcheck` to the command chain inside `DaemonUnitTest.dhall`. This broke the job because:

- `unit-test.sh` sources `~/.profile` internally to set up the opam environment (placing `dune` on PATH), but this sourcing does not propagate to subsequent commands in the `&&` chain.
- After `unit-test.sh` exits, the outer `bash -c` process running the remaining `&& dune runtest ...` command cannot find `dune`.

## Changes

### 1. Split mina-healthcheck into its own CI job

Created `buildkite/src/Jobs/Test/MinaHealthcheckUnitTest.dhall` — a standalone CI job inspired by the `RosettaUnitTest` pattern. It runs `unit-test.sh` on `src/app/mina_healthcheck` under `Size.Small` / `Fast`.

Removed the broken `dune runtest src/app/mina_healthcheck` from `DaemonUnitTest.dhall`.

### 2. Extract `SimpleUnitTestJob` library

Factored the common `buildTestCmd` logic shared by `RosettaUnitTest`, `ZkappTestToolUnitTest`, and `MinaHealthcheckUnitTest` into `buildkite/src/Lib/SimpleUnitTestJob.dhall`. Each job is now a ~15‑line configuration record specifying `name`, `keyPrefix`, `label`, `testPath`, `testProfile`, `tags`, and `cmdTarget`.

author: maximebicmtl
body:
This PR adds the `DTZ` linting rules to our linter configuration, which notably forces Python code to handle timezones when creating a date.

Previously, our code did not handle timezones at all, making all datetime objects created with the system timezone.
With this PR, "absolute" datetimes (such as "now") are created and stored in the database with the UTC timezone. User-supplied timezone strings are parsed using a timezone aware-parser (`dateutil`) or with no timezone when not available (which uses the system timezone AFAIK).

author: sdbondi
body:
## Description

The swarm daemon web UI was passing a bare string to `get_stdout` for the validator node, wallet daemon, and indexer instances (e.g. `"vn 0"`, `"dan 0"`, `"indexer 0"`). The server handler deserializes params into `ListLogFilesRequest` (`{ instance_type, index }`), so these calls produced server-side errors:

```
WARN 🌐 JSON-RPC params error: Invalid params: invalid type: string "indexer 0", expected struct ListLogFilesRequest
```

## Motivation

The stdout log panel was silently broken for VN, wallet daemon, and indexer instances. The `MinoTari*` `get_stdout` calls already used the correct struct shape; this aligns the remaining three.

## Changes

- `get_stdout` for validator node: `"vn ${index}"` → `{ instance_type: "TariValidatorNode", index: Number(index) }`
- `get_stdout` for wallet daemon: `"dan ${index}"` → `{ instance_type: "TariWalletDaemon", index: Number(index) }`
- `get_stdout` for indexer: `"indexer ${index}"` → `{ instance_type: "TariIndexer", index: Number(index) }`

Variant names verified against the `InstanceType` enum in `applications/tari_swarm_daemon/src/config.rs`.

author: pierdipi
body:
Add a merge-append-lists annotation on LLMInferenceServiceConfig (and LLMInferenceService) that declares specific array fields should be concatenated (base + override) instead of atomically replaced during strategic merge. This is useful for container args, command, and other +listType=atomic fields where an override config should extend the base rather than replace it entirely.

The annotation uses Kustomize-style field paths with kyaml Lookup for traversal:
```
  serving.kserve.io/merge-append-lists: |
    template.containers.[name=kserve-container].args
    router.scheduler.template.containers.[name=main].command
```

Without the annotation, merge behavior is unchanged (backward compatible).

author: proggeramlug
body:
## Summary

Implements Annex B **B.3.3** legacy block-level function declarations. In sloppy mode, a `function f(){}` declared inside a block must ALSO create a `var`-style binding in the enclosing function/program scope: `f` is visible (as a `var` that is `undefined` until the declaration runs) outside the block, while the block keeps its own independent binding. Perry previously only block-scoped it, so referencing `f` outside the block threw `ReferenceError: f is not defined` — the dominant `annexB/language` test262 failure (126× in the issue).

Fixes #5297.

## What changed (HIR lowering only)

- **New traversal** `collect_annexb_block_fn_decl_names` (in `lower_decl/block.rs`) walks a body's nested `block`/`if`/loops/`switch`/`try`/`labeled`/`with` (never entering nested function or class bodies) and yields, in one pass, **every** block-nested function name plus the **subset** that gets the legacy `var`. The `var` is suppressed when the name collides with a parameter or an enclosing `let`/`const`/`class` (which would make the equivalent `var` an early error) or is `arguments`, per spec — this clears the `skip-*` cases too.
- **Wired into all three body-lowering paths**: function declarations / arrows (`predefine_var_bindings_in_function_body`), function **expressions** — the IIFE shape the `function-code` tests use (`lower_fn_expr_anon`), and **program** scope (`lower_module_fn`). Each registers one hoisted, undefined-initialised enclosing slot per eligible name and records `name -> slot` in the new `annexb_block_fn_var_ids` context map (saved/restored across nested bodies alongside `annexb_block_fn_names_all`).
- `lower_nested_fn_decl` now gives every block-nested declaration a **fresh block-local** (so it never clobbers an enclosing same-named parameter/var) and, for the eligible subset, copies that closure into the enclosing `var` **at the declaration point** — keeping later block-local mutation independent of the outer binding (`block-decl-*-block-scoping`).

Strict bodies and ES modules are untouched (pure block scoping, no outer var).

## Measurement

test262 `annexB/language` (node v26 differential, `scripts/test262_subset.py --dir annexB/language --all-features`):

| | pass | parity |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | 385 / 801 | 48.1% |
| this PR | **498 / 801** | **62.2%** |

**+113 cases.** The bulk of the remainder is `eval-code` (needs eval enablement, separate issue) and a few non-B.3.3 Annex B features (catch-var redeclaration, legacy regex escapes, `CallExpression`-as-LHS).

author: jorenham
body:
before:

```console
$ optype infer "import colorsys; colorsys.hls_to_rgb"
[T: CanLe[float, CanBool] & CanMul[T1169 | T1168 | T1167 | ...   # 72_913 chars, ~5600 typevars
```

after:

```console
$ optype infer "import colorsys; colorsys.hls_to_rgb"
InferError: more than 26 type parameters
```

A loop over a spy result (`colorsys.hls_to_rgb`, `base64.encode`, `random.vonmisesvariate`, `difflib.get_close_matches`, ...) can spawn thousands of distinct result spies, each rendered as its own typevar, yielding a valid-but-useless multi-thousand-character signature. Beyond `_TYPEVAR_LIMIT` (26) typevars the signature reports cleanly instead.

The limit is a judgement call (open to tuning); 26 clears every legitimate case in the test suite (max 3) with wide margin while catching all the runaway ones.

closes #671

body:
### Motivation
- Fix a behavioral regression introduced when `onPanic` was converted to an `atomic.Pointer`: calling `SetPanicHandler(nil)` previously stored a non-nil pointer to a nil function which caused a secondary nil-call panic during dispatch instead of clearing the observer.

### Description
- Update `SetPanicHandler` to clear the atomic pointer when `f == nil` by calling `l.onPanic.Store(nil)`; otherwise store `&f` as before so concurrent access remains race-free.
- Add `TestEventLoop_SetPanicHandlerNilClearsObserver` to ensure `SetPanicHandler(nil)` restores the pre-atomic semantics: a cleared observer does not fire and the original handler panic propagates unchanged.

- Ran `go test ./internal/api -run '^TestEventLoop_SetPanicHandlerNilClearsObserver$' -count=1 -v` which passed.

author: turkenh
body:
<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes the long-lived RBE daemon (watcher, retries, process handlers) and the install path after remote builds; failures are mostly logged rather than fatal, but a buggy watcher could still affect tunnel reliability.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **auto-install** to `lim xcode rbe`: while the RBE tunnel runs (foreground or background daemon), a new BEP watcher reacts to each **successful, fully flushed** Bazel build and calls `installRbeBuildFromBep` so the `.ipa` lands on the attached simulator (or is recorded for a later attach). **`--auto-install`** is on by default; **`--no-auto-install`**, **`--target`**, and **`--bep-file`** control behavior when inference or paths are ambiguous.
> 
> The detached **`--serve`** child gets **`--workspace-root` / `--target` / `--bep-file`** via `buildServeChildArgs`, starts the watcher when auto-install is enabled, and uses **crash guards** so watcher faults do not drop the tunnel mid-build. Watcher teardown runs **before** tunnel/stack shutdown to avoid racing installs.
> 
> **BEP handling** is centralized: `defaultBepPath` / `resolveBepPath`, generated bazelrc honors a custom log path, and **`.limrun/rbe.pid`** stores `bepFile` (and `target` when watching) so **`lim xcode rbe install`** picks the same log. The SDK gains **`inspectBuildCompletion`**, typed **`RbeBepError`**, and stricter **BLAKE3 / non-SHA256** detection in bytestream URIs.
>

body:
## Summary

`narrow_by_property_presence` (the `"k" in x` positive branch) synthesized a
**required**-property intersection (`source & { p: T }`, `optional: false`)
whenever a non-union receiver already declared the property. That over-narrowed
an existing **optional** own property in two tsc-divergent ways:

1. It stripped the property's optionality, so `delete x.p` after `"p" in x`
   reported a false **TS2790** ("operand of a 'delete' operator must be
   optional").
2. It excluded `undefined` from the property's value type, **unsoundly**
   accepting `const y: T = x.p` where tsc keeps `x.p: T | undefined`.

tsc's `narrowTypeByInKeyword` adds no structural information when the property
is already declared on the receiver — the union branch already kept members
as-is for present narrowing. The fix returns the receiver unchanged in that
case; the `Record<prop, unknown>` synthesis stays scoped to the
genuinely-absent-property case (unchanged).

Goal: hold

## Structural rule

When `"p" in x` is checked and `p` is already a member of the (non-union)
receiver type `x` (own property or apparent-type member), tsc adds no
structural information: the receiver type is unchanged, so an optional `p`
stays optional (its value type keeps `undefined`). tsz now returns the
receiver unchanged in that case through `solver narrowing::narrow_by_property_presence`,
matching the union-branch policy that already kept present members as-is. The
absent-property case still narrows to `x & Record<p, unknown>`.

## Provenance

Machine: Mac
Assistant: claude-code
Model: claude-opus-4-8
Effort: high

## Verification

- New solver-narrowing parity tests (`tsz-checker` `in_narrow_apparent_member_tests`):
  `in_narrowing_keeps_optional_own_property_deletable`,
  `in_narrowing_preserves_undefined_in_optional_property_value`,
  `delete_optional_property_without_in_narrowing_is_legal`,
  plus the existing apparent-member and object-union cases — 5/5 PASS.
- Conformance, 0 PASS→FAIL on touched/adjacent families:
  `delete` 13/13, `inOperator` 5/5, `inKeyword` 4/4, `narrowing` 29/29,
  `controlFlow` 94/94, `typeGuard` 86/86, `discriminated` 8/8.
- Corpus no-regression (canary, dist-fast baseline vs patched):
  kysely 118→118, msw 97→97, tanstack-router 234→234, ofetch 12→12.
- Determinism: 3× identical diagnostics on the witness repros.
- clippy clean (`tsz-solver`, `tsz-checker`).

Note: this is a correctness/parity fix (witnessed by ofetch
`delete options.query`). It does **not** by itself change ofetch's tsz-only
count (12→12); the ofetch `delete`-site TS2790 is a separate, entangled root
(truthy-narrow + `Omit<RequestInit>`-heritage member resolution + generic
instantiation of `ResolvedFetchOptions<ResponseType>`) that this change does
not address.

body:
## Breadcrumb spec (BLOCK 2)

<planning>
Wave-1 track HTTP-INT. T2 (net.* socket surface) is already merged on the base branch.
This breadcrumb composes teko_http.c (HTTP/1.1 codec, Wave 0) + teko_socket.c (client, T2)
into a synchronous http.get/post client surface, following the exact T2 pattern.
</planning>
<current_task>
<description>Make the `http.*` CLIENT surface live end-to-end on native AND WASM. ids 80-81 (http.get/post). Gate behind uses_http / wasm_emit_http (ZERO-INIT confirmed). Proof: native loopback GET "hello-http" + WASM host-import mock "hello-http". NO dead surface.</description>
<minimal_context>Pattern = T2 (net.*). teko_http.c API: build_request + parse_response. teko_socket client API: tcp_connect/send/recv/close. Bars: 1 increment/commit; ASan+UBSan BOTH dispatch paths + TSan; 16 goldens BYTE-IDENTICAL; MSVC-safe; SAST.</minimal_context>
<expected_format>Sub-PR body including SAST self-review and proof outputs.</expected_format>
</current_task>

## Status

**id range 80-99 (http) LIVE; gated by `uses_http`; `wasm_emit_http` zero-init confirmed; goldens byte-identical.**

## What landed

- `teko_rt_http_get` (id 80) + `teko_rt_http_post` (id 81): synchronous HTTP/1.1 client composing `teko_http_build_request` + `teko_socket_tcp_connect/send/recv` + `teko_http_parse_response`. URL parsed by a bounded scanner (`parse_http_url`: no `strtol`; host capped at 253 bytes, port decimal-only, path verbatim).
- `BytecodeBuffer.uses_http` flag: zero-initialized in `codegen_li_buffer_create`; set to 1 when ids 80 or 81 are emitted.
- `MetalContext.wasm_emit_http`: **zero-initialized in `teko_metal_create`** (the T2 lesson: `malloc` does not zero-init; the prior T2 ASan regression was exactly this). Setter `teko_metal_set_emit_http` mirrors the pattern of all sibling flags.
- WASM: `env.teko_http_get`/`teko_http_post` imports gated on `wasm_emit_http`; dispatch in `emit_wasm.c` ids 80-81.
- Native: `emit_native_hosted.c` ids 80/81 → `teko_rt_http_get`/`teko_rt_http_post`.
- Frontend: `codec_id_for` returns 80/81; `runtime_arity` returns 2 for http.post.

## SAST self-review

**URL + response are attacker-controlled inputs; all bounds are explicit.**

- `parse_http_url`: host scan is bounded by `TEKO_HTTP_MAX_HOST` (253) + NUL before any copy; port is decimal-only with a digit count limit (5) and a value cap (65535) — no `strtol`; path is copied verbatim bounded by `TEKO_HTTP_MAX_PATH + 1`; no format-string, no shell exec, no path traversal.
- `http_recv_response`: recv loop grows a heap buffer capped at `TEKO_HTTP_RESP_MAX` (1 MiB) checked before each `malloc`/grow; chunk size is fixed (4096); no integer overflow in the size arithmetic.
- `do_http_request`: `req_len > (uint32_t)-1u` guard before the `uint32_t` cast for `teko_socket_send`; `calloc` for the body copy ensures NUL-termination even if `body_len == 0`.
- `teko_http_parse_response`: already KAT-hardened (duplicate `Content-Length` → `SMUGGLING`, obs-fold → `OBS_FOLD`, body cap 64 MiB, chunked-decode hex overflow guards).
- **Gating**: `uses_http` initialized to 0 in `codegen_li_buffer_create`; `wasm_emit_http` initialized to 0 in `teko_metal_create` (explicit, not relying on `malloc`). Non-HTTP programs produce zero new emission — byte-identical to the pre-HTTP-INT output confirmed by the net.wat check.
- **Host-import boundary (WASM)**: `url_ptr`/`body_ptr` are i32 module pointers bounded to the module's linear memory; the mock in `run-http.mjs` caps reads at `MAX_BUF` before scanning; `writeCStr` caps the write; no untrusted data escapes the memory region.

## Proof outputs

**Native:**
```
OK: http -> loopback GET [hello-http]
All native runner proofs passed.
```

**WASM:**
```
OK   http(wasm): http.get -> env.teko_http_get -> body: ["hello-http"] (host-import mock, reactor-backed)
```

**Sanitizers:**
```
ASan+UBSan default dispatch: 348/0/0
ASan+UBSan portable dispatch: 348/0/0
TSan: 348/0/0
```

**16 goldens:**
```
test_codegen_emitters_arithmetic_per_target: PASS
348 Tests 0 Failures 0 Ignored
```

**Byte-identical gate:** `net.wat` contains no `teko_http` imports (grep returns empty). ✓

## DO NOT MERGE

Base is `feat/phase-19-networking`. The PM merges this sub-PR after review + SAST + CI. The PO merges the principal PR into `main` at the end of Phase 19.

author: salmartinez-design
body:
## Problem

Sal: *"on desktop techs can be logged in and view the system just like office staff can. This cannot happen."*

Three layers of leak today, fixed in this PR:

| Layer | Today | After |
|---|---|---|
| Frontend routes | No role check. Tech hits `/dispatch` URL → sees full office page | Redirected to `/my-jobs` |
| Sidebar | Half the items lacked `roles` array; tech saw Dashboard / Jobs / Customers / Employees / Invoices | Tech sees only Cleancyclopedia, Training, My Jobs, Leave |
| Backend | `routes/dispatch.ts` and `routes/dashboard.ts` had **0** `requireRole` calls. Tech could `curl /api/dispatch?date=...` and get full company payload | 403 Forbidden |

## Fix

### Frontend route guard — allowlist (App.tsx)

New `<TechRouteGuard>` wraps the Router. When the authenticated user is `technician` or `team_lead` and the current path is NOT in the tech allowlist (my-jobs, my-day, training, lms (not lms/admin), leave, notifications, token-based pages like `/sign/`, `/pay/`, `/portal/`, `/onboard/`, `/book/`, `/survey/`, `/accept-invite`), redirect to `/my-jobs`. Owner / admin / office / super_admin pass through unchanged.

**Allowlist, not denylist** — a future office route added without a guard can only cost a tech UX bug, never a data leak.

### Sidebar (app-sidebar.tsx)

- Added the office-tier `roles` array to every `NAV_SECTIONS` item missing one (Dashboard, Jobs, Customers, Messages, Accounts, Employees, Invoices, all Reports)
- Pre-filter at the **section** level: when all items in a section are filtered out, skip the section entirely so we don't render an orphan "Operations" / "Sales" / "Insights" label with nothing under it
- Added a "My Day" section with **My Jobs** + **Leave** links visible only to technician / team_lead

### Backend (dispatch.ts + dashboard.ts)

- `dispatch.ts` — added `dispatchOfficeGate = requireRole("owner", "admin", "office", "super_admin")` to all 3 routes (`/`, `/week-summary`, `/zone-coverage-audit`)
- `dashboard.ts` — added `officeGate` to every `router.get` / `router.post` (10 routes: `/metrics`, `/today`, `/kpis`, `/revenue-chart`, `/techs-today`, `/commercial-alerts`, `/weekly-forecast`, `/business-health`, `/mobile-cards`, `/card-prefs`)

## Files
- `artifacts/qleno/src/App.tsx` — TechRouteGuard + imports
- `artifacts/qleno/src/components/layout/app-sidebar.tsx` — roles arrays + section-skip + tech My Day
- `artifacts/api-server/src/routes/dispatch.ts` — officeGate on 3 routes
- `artifacts/api-server/src/routes/dashboard.ts` — officeGate on 10 routes

## Verification
- Api-server tsc flat at baseline (zero new errors)
- Frontend tsc flat at baseline (zero new errors)
- No DB / schema change

## After Railway redeploys

- Tech who types `/dispatch` / `/payroll` / `/employees` in the URL bar → redirected to `/my-jobs` instantly
- Tech sidebar shows only: Cleancyclopedia, Training, My Jobs, Leave
- Tech hitting `GET /api/dispatch?date=...` via curl/devtools gets 403

## Known follow-up (not in this PR)

Many other office routes (payroll, reports, clients, accounts, invoices, etc.) still lack `requireRole` at the API layer — the frontend guard catches them in the UI, but a curl-savvy tech could still hit them directly. Should be swept in a separate audit PR, but this PR closes the biggest leak (dispatch, which exposes the full company payload) and the most visible UI leak.

author: jason-easyazz
body:
## Why
This closes the **last** operator-touch on the idea→merged-PR path. The closeout phase runs the greploop merge guard (Greptile confidence + squash-merge when CLEAN/green/0-unresolved), but it depended on a closeout **agent worker** invoking the guard script. Live (ZOE-5832) the worker bailed *"cannot proceed without a valid PR URL"*, leaving an objectively-mergeable PR at `closeout/merge_blocked` and forcing an operator merge.

## What
Apply the #632/#677 pattern to the merge step. The **harness** invokes the proven greploop guard CLI itself (`run_greploop_guard.sh --pr N --merge-when-ready` — which already enforces confidence/threads and **squash-only, never `--admin`/`--force`**) and confirms the PR ended up `MERGED`, then records the closeout `greptile` evidence (with merge SHA) and completes `closeout → retro` — regardless of the agent. Fail-open: if the guard didn't merge, it falls through to the agent outcome and retries next cycle.

- **`pipeline_closeout.run_closeout_merge(pr_url)`** (new): short-circuits if already merged, else runs the guard (bounded 900s) and re-checks `gh pr view state == MERGED`.
- **`pipeline_store`**: `_append_harness_closeout_merge` + a closeout override in `sync_pipeline_from_chain`, mirroring the verify/review overrides. Gated by `ZOE_PIPELINE_HARNESS_CLOSEOUT_MERGE` (default on).

Now **verify, review, and closeout-merge are all harness-driven** — no flaky-agent dependency anywhere on the critical path.

## Testing
- Runner: no-PR / already-merged / guard-then-merge / not-merged / guard-missing (fail-open).
- Integration: merge → `retro`; not-merged → stays `closeout`; `ZOE_PIPELINE_HARNESS_CLOSEOUT_MERGE=false` → stays `closeout`.
- `pytest -k "pipeline or verify or review or closeout or ..."` → **614 passed**; structure validator clean.

author: boshen
body:
Use the **unstable** itertools sort (`sorted_unstable_by`/`sorted_unstable_by_key`) instead of the stable one at sites where the sort key is **unique**, so stability buys nothing. Stable sort only differs from unstable in the relative order of *equal* elements — and at these sites no two elements compare equal, so the output is identical. Unstable sort is also marginally faster (no scratch allocation, smaller routine). This mirrors how the std slice sorts are already used.

## Flipped (key is unique ⇒ output unchanged)
- `generate_stage/manual_code_splitting.rs` — by `stable_id` (unique)
- `generate_stage/compute_cross_chunk_links.rs` (×3) — by chunk `exec_order` (the unique `chunk.exec_order = i` index), external-module map entries by `exec_order`, and by export `name` (unique map key)
- `generate_stage/code_splitting.rs` — the `(group, chunk-index / chunk exec_order)` tuple key (unique across all chunks)

## Left stable (on purpose)
- `compute_cross_chunk_links` cjs-namespace sort by `owner.exec_order()` — multiple ns bindings can share an owner (→ equal keys), and the surrounding logic relies on the relative order ("first reference").
- `code_splitting.rs` chunk comparator (`:194`) — its same-kind branches return `Equal` when two chunks' representative **module** `exec_order`s tie. Assigned `exec_order`s are unique (`sort_modules.rs` monotonic counter), but unvisited modules keep the `u32::MAX` sentinel; the cross-kind `if a == b { a_should_be_first }` tiebreaks and the trailing comment *"other chunks has stable order at per entry chunk level"* show the code relies on stable ordering to break those ties deterministically. (Reverted from an earlier revision of this PR after review.)

## Verification
The full bundler-output integration/snapshot suite passes with **no snapshot changes** (the only failures in an isolated worktree are pre-existing environment issues — a missing `node_modules` package and the `test262` submodule — which fail identically on `main`). `cargo clippy` (with `--features experimental`) and `cargo fmt` are clean.

author: dmytro-yemelianov
body:
## What

Follow-on to #50: extends the columnar (numpy) fast-path to the **validate** backend's geometric checks, which fold over Segments exactly like `simulate` does.

**~1.53× faster validate** end-to-end on a 100k-point design (350ms → 230ms). Lower than simulate's 2.37× because validate's config/ordering checks (temperatures, speeds, retraction, stringing, cold-extrusion) still walk the resolved step list — only the geometric checks move to columns.

## Changes

- **`ColumnarToolpath`** gains `width`/`height` columns (NaN where undefined); `from_toolpath`, `from_lists` and `resolve_columnar` all populate them.
- **`resolve_columnar()`** gains a `state=` param mirroring `ir.resolve`, so validate reuses its single `State` (keeps the one-State optimization from #49) and skips ~N per-`Segment` allocations.
- **`validate()`** — `_check_bounds` / `_check_first_layer` / `_check_extrusion_geometry` are now vectorized numpy folds over the columns. Reported coordinates/geometry go through `_reported()` (NaN→None, else plain `float`) so message text is **byte-identical** to the object version.

## Correctness

- New **`test_validation_geometry.py`** pins the *exact* messages and reported coordinates for every geometric rule (characterization — green before *and* after the refactor).
- `test_columnar.py`'s field-by-field pin extended to `width`/`height`, so the geometry columns stay locked to the canonical `resolve`.
- Verified byte-identical against the pre-refactor object validate across 10 designs × 3 init configs (arcs, multi-out-of-bounds, undefined axes, no-extrusion, stationary extrusion, no-build-volume, cold): **27/27 real combos identical**; the 3 empty-design cases raise the same pre-existing exception in both.

**417 tests pass** (was 411), ruff clean, gcode/plot golden lock untouched.

author: hzhaoy
body:
## What & Why

`migrate_shared_skills()` in `optional-skills/migration/openclaw-migration/scripts/openclaw_to_hermes.py` scans `Path.home() / ".agents" / "skills"` directly as one of its skill sources. The existing tests isolate `source_root`/`target_root` via `tmp_path`, but this one source path escaped the sandbox and pointed at the developer's **real** `~/.agents/skills` tree.

On a real machine that directory can be large (in my case ~45k files / 1.3 GB), so every `execute=True` test that ran the full migration did a real `shutil.copytree` of it into `tmp_path`. Effects:

- 5 tests took **170–200s each**; the whole file took **~16 minutes** and was being SIGKILL'd by the 140s-per-file CI timeout.
- Results were **non-reproducible** — they depended on whatever skills happened to live in the runner's HOME. On a clean CI HOME the branch silently didn't execute at all.

### Fix

- Add an `autouse` fixture `isolate_home` that redirects `Path.home()` (and `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` as a fallback) to a temp directory, so the migrator can never reach into the real user tree.
- Add `test_personal_skills_migrated` to actually cover the `~/.agents/skills` (personal-skills) branch of `migrate_shared_skills()` — previously this branch was executed by accident but never asserted.

No production code changed; this is a tests-only change.

## How to test

```
pytest tests/skills/test_openclaw_migration.py -v
```

- Before: 41 passed in ~945s (0:15:45), with 5 cases at 170–200s each.
- After: 42 passed in ~1.3s.

## Platforms tested

- macOS (Apple Silicon), Python 3.11.11, pytest 9.0.2.
- The fixture also patches `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` so the isolation holds on Windows; the migrator code itself is unchanged.

author: mak1e
body:
💡 **What**: Refactored the `getStaticProps` in `pages/index.tsx` to utilize `Promise.all` for concurrently fetching repository GitHub data, both across the list of repositories and within the specific API fetches (avatars and contributors count) for each repository.

🎯 **Why**: The application was making sequential unauthenticated HTTP requests (8 total round-trips for 4 repositories) inside a loop. This blocked the event loop unnecessarily, increasing page generation time and potential timeout risk, especially over slower network paths. 

📊 **Impact**: Reduces total fetch time from O(N * 2) network roundtrips to roughly O(1) concurrent latency (bounded by the single slowest request). This significantly speeds up local development cold starts and production Next.js build times.

🔬 **Measurement**: Verified the Next.js static build using `pnpm build` completes much faster when fetching without cache. The build runs successfully and preserves all fallback error handling logic for robust degraded functionality.

author: kido-luci
body:
## Why

The blog comment thread fetched **every** comment on a post in one request. This is the frontend half of the #4 pagination work — it consumes the backend's new comment pagination (companion PR: `kido-luci/luci_dev_backend#7`).

## What changed (`src/pages/blog/[slug].astro`)

- Loads the first **20 top-level comments** (each with its replies) and shows a **"Load more comments"** button when the server reports more, fetching the next page on click.
- Reads pagination metadata from response **headers**: `X-Total-Count` (count badge) and `X-Has-More` (button visibility). The JSON body is still a flat comment array, so the existing tree-builder is unchanged.
- Accumulates pages into `cachedComments` with **id-dedupe** — a freshly posted comment shifts the server's offsets, so a later page can re-return a row we already hold; dedupe keeps the list clean with no skips.
- **Fixes a latent bug:** session-posted comments/replies are now tracked in `cachedComments`, so a re-render (sort toggle or load-more) keeps them. Previously, toggling sort right after posting made the new comment vanish (it lived only in the DOM, not the cached array).
- **Graceful degradation:** against an un-upgraded backend (no headers, returns all), it shows the full set and simply hides the button.

## Notes / limitations

- The newest/oldest **sort toggle** operates on the currently-loaded set (unchanged behavior). Not-yet-loaded older comments appear as you "Load more" — expected for offset pagination at this scale.
- Requires the backend PR deployed for true pagination; safe to merge independently thanks to the graceful-degradation fallback.

## Verification

`npm run build` compiles the page cleanly (Vite transform ✓). Full prerender needs the backend reachable (the static blog bakes API data at build time) — recommend a local `npm run build && npm run preview` with the backend up, posting/loading comments to eyeball the button and dedupe.

body:
Adds the adapter layer and the first adapter. Closes #16.

## What this adds

- **`AdapterRegistry`** — records approved adapters and the external protocol each wraps; the credit system only routes calls through adapters listed here.
- **`UniswapV3Adapter`** — first adapter. A margin account calls it via its own `execute`; the adapter pulls the input from the calling account, swaps on the Uniswap V3 router, and forces the output recipient to that same account, so proceeds cannot be diverted.
- **`IUniswapV3SwapRouter`** minimal router interface.

## Tests

- `AdapterRegistry` register/unregister and owner-only gating.
- Account-routed swap through the adapter against a mock router: output lands back in the account, nothing stuck in the adapter, and the minimum-out bound is enforced.
- `UniswapV3Adapter.fork.t.sol` — swaps real USDC for WETH on a mainnet fork; self-skips when `MAINNET_RPC_URL` is unset so CI stays green.

body:
## Problem
The **Deploy Database Migrations** workflow runs `npm ci` on **Node 18**, but the repo now depends on **`prisma@7.8.0`**, which refuses to install on Node `<20.19` via a preinstall engine gate:

```
Prisma only supports Node.js versions 20.19+, 22.12+, 24.0+.
current: node v18.20.8
npm error command sh -c node scripts/preinstall-entry.js
```

So `npm ci` exits 1 **before** `prisma migrate deploy` ever runs. The job has been failing on every push to `main` that touches `prisma/migrations/**`.

**Production impact:** the most recent `main` run (after #303 merged) failed this way, so the `20260614120000_add_proposal_tally` migration was **not applied** — the `ProposalTally` table is missing in prod and the governance vote-tally router (#302) errors until it exists.

## Fix
- Bump `setup-node` to **22** (matches `pr-checks`, `unit-tests`, `trpc-integration-tests`, `ci-smoke-preprod`).
- Add a **`workflow_dispatch`** trigger. The workflow otherwise only fires on a push under `prisma/migrations/**`; since the migration is already merged (no new file to push), `workflow_dispatch` is the only way to apply it once this fix reaches `main`.

## After this lands on `main`
1. Re-run / manually dispatch **Deploy Database Migrations** to apply the pending `ProposalTally` migration to prod.
2. `daily-balance-snapshots.yml` also pins Node 18 but installs from the self-contained `scripts/` dir (no root Prisma) — left untouched here.

Cron automation reported job failure with no task-level problem. (Issue #83959)
- **Why now:** P1 for background/cron Codex turns; the issue's own local mitigation confirmed the direction (raise the startup-close retry budget + add a bounded backoff).
- **Intended outcome:** Startup tolerates a short replacement-server warm-up window before declaring failure, and when it does give up it says so distinctly instead of surfacing a misleading "client is closed".
- **Out of scope:** The separate per-run replay retry gate in `embedded-agent-runner/run.ts` (already correct, untouched) and the shared-client eviction work tracked under #79495.

author: elronbandel
body:
Doctrine half of #187.

## What

Rewrites [`.agents/models/RULES.md`](.agents/models/RULES.md) rule 1 (and the abstract, rule 2, rule 12) so the doctrine matches the implemented reality: **the model service is a generic gateway that selects `<provider>/<model>` at runtime from `EVAL_MODEL`.** Any LiteLLM-supported model works with no new image — no build, no publish. Pinned images (`replay`, a fixed corporate endpoint) are the exception.

## Why

The model layer is **already generic**:
- [`gpt-5.4--bifrost/Dockerfile`](containers/models/gpt-5.4--bifrost/Dockerfile) (the *default* gateway): *"Provider and model name come from a single `EVAL_MODEL` env var."*
- [`gpt-5.4--litellm/config.yaml.template`](containers/models/gpt-5.4--litellm/config.yaml.template): `model: "${EVAL_MODEL}"`.
- [`services.yaml`](containers/compose/services.yaml) passes `EVAL_MODEL` to the gateway as the handle.

But rule 1 still said *"one model per image, pre-configured,"* which mandates a per-model build + publish and directly contradicts rule 9 (*"any provider **without modifying Eval Containers**"*). The stale rule is what makes the obvious `EVAL_MODEL=openai/gpt-5.4` look unsupported.

## Scope

**Doctrine only** (rules-only PR). The code/docs half — renaming the gateways to `models/{bifrost,litellm}`, retiring the leftover hardcoded per-model images, a CLI `--gateway` flag, and docs using `<provider>/<model>` handles — is tracked in #187 and lands as a separate PR.

## Rules checked

- [`.agents/meta/rules/RULES.md`](.agents/meta/rules/RULES.md) — rule form (outcome-based, RFC-2119); Changelog entry added (no silent drift).
- [`.agents/contributing/RULES.md`](.agents/contributing/RULES.md) — rules-only change (rule 2); declared rules (rule 3).

body:
Closes #819

Two related single-source-of-truth gaps around battle constants/parity.

## 1. Enemy loadout cap → `GameConstants.MaxSelectedSkills`

`MaxBattleSkills = 4` was a private literal on `Game.Core/Enemies/Enemy.cs`, outside the `[ClientMirrored]` `GameConstants` class that single-sources cross-boundary constants.

Rather than add a *new* `MaxBattleSkills` constant to `GameConstants`, `Enemy` now consumes the existing `GameConstants.MaxSelectedSkills`. The two values were both `4` and conceptually the **same** cap — the `MaxSelectedSkills` doc comment already states *"Enemies bring the same cap into battle for player/enemy symmetry."* Adding a second mirrored constant holding `4` would have replaced one duplication (a private literal) with another (two public constants to keep in sync), defeating the single-source goal. So the stray literal is folded into the constant that already represents this cap and is already mirrored to the client.

Because no new cross-boundary constant was introduced, the generated client (`UI/src/lib/api/types/game-constants.ts`) is unchanged — the codegen diff-check (#282) stays clean. (Two test comments that named the old constant were updated to match.)

## 2. `BattleAttributesParityTests` — shared scenario table, no re-hardcoded coefficients

`BattleAttributesParityTests.cs` and its frontend mirror `battle-attributes.test.ts` re-encoded the derived-stat coefficients as literals (`50 + 20*20 + 5*10`) on both sides — a second hand-maintained copy of numbers already single-sourced in `StaticAttributeModifiers.All` and generated to the frontend via `STATIC_ATTRIBUTE_MODIFIERS`.

Both suites are restructured into a single named `Scenarios` table (mirrored row-for-row, the same shape as the battle-simulation parity suite): each scenario carries input allocations + the derived attributes to check. The **expected value is composed from the single-sourced modifier table**, not a literal — every static modifier is additive, so a base value contributes its raw amount and a derived modifier contributes `amount × allocation[derivedSource]`, the same reduction the production `AttributeCollection` / `BattleAttributes` performs. A coefficient retune now flows into both the production path and the expectation, so the assertions can no longer rot out of step. Coefficient values themselves are unchanged.

The 9 scenarios (`maxHealth`, `defense`, `cooldownRecovery`, `criticalChance`, `criticalDamage`, `dodgeChance`, `blockChance`, `blockReduction`, `zeroBaseStats`) are identical on both sides.

## Verification

- Backend: `dotnet build` clean; full `Game.Core.Tests` 614/614 pass; `BattleAttributesParity` 9 theory cases pass; Enemy/BattleFactory tests pass; `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` clean on `Game.Core` and `Game.Core.Tests`.
- Codegen: `dotnet run --project Game.Api -- codegen` produces a clean `git diff` (no generated change).
- Frontend: `npm run check` 0 errors/0 warnings; `npm run lint` (eslint + check) clean; `battle-attributes` unit tests 31 pass (9 parity scenarios mirror the backend).

body:
## Summary
Adds automated release APK signing infrastructure for CI/CD, with keystore material managed entirely through environment variables to keep sensitive data out of the repository.

## Key Changes
- **New GitHub Actions workflow** (`.github/workflows/release-signing.yml`):
  - Triggers on APK-affecting changes to `main` branch (app, domain, platform, gradle configs)
  - Decodes base64-encoded keystore from `ANDROID_KEYSTORE` secret
  - Builds signed release APK using environment variables for keystore credentials
  - Cleans up decoded keystore after build (even on failure)
  - Uploads signed APK as artifact
  - Supports manual workflow dispatch for testing

- **Gradle signing configuration** (`app/build.gradle.kts`):
  - Detects release signing availability via `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_FILE` environment variable
  - Conditionally creates `release` signing config only when keystore file exists and is readable
  - Applies signing config to release build type when available
  - Leaves release builds unsigned locally (when env vars unset) without breaking the build
  - Debug builds remain unaffected

## Implementation Details
- Keystore material never persists in the repository; CI decodes it from secrets at build time
- Local development builds unsigned release APKs gracefully when signing env vars are absent
- Path filter prevents workflow runs on docs-only or STATE-only changes
- Gradle cache configured to speed up builds
- Keystore file cleaned up with `if: always()` to ensure cleanup even on build failure

author: dvaerum
body:
## Why

PR #166 added a Path A asset-prefix sentinel regression guard inside `nix/tests/vm-single-tenant.nix` (and the matching multi-tenant test), but discovered that **`.github/workflows/ci.yml` does not run any nixosTests**. The two existing jobs are:

- `python` — pytest + ruff across Python 3.10/3.11/3.12
- `dashboard` — Next.js `npm run build`

`flake show` lists 5 checks under `checks.x86_64-linux.*`:

- `agent-mcp` (Python package build — already covered by `python` job)
- `agent-mcp-dashboard` (Next.js build — already covered by `dashboard` job)
- `agent-mcp-router-wrapper` (small wrapper script)
- `vm-single-tenant` (full nixosTest: VM boot + HTTP curl assertions, asset-prefix sentinel grep)
- `vm-multi-tenant` (same, multi-tenant mode)

The VM checks were therefore only effective if a contributor manually remembered to run them. That makes the regression guard in #166 unreliable.

## What

Add a third CI job `nix-flake-check` that builds **just the VM checks** rather than the full `nix flake check`:

```yaml
nix-flake-check:
  name: Nix flake check (VM tests)
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  timeout-minutes: 60
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - uses: DeterminateSystems/nix-installer-action@main
    - uses: DeterminateSystems/magic-nix-cache-action@main
    - name: Build VM tests
      run: |
        nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.vm-single-tenant \
                  .#checks.x86_64-linux.vm-multi-tenant \
                  -L --print-build-logs
```

### Scope choice

Builds **only** `vm-single-tenant` + `vm-multi-tenant`, **not** the full `nix flake check`. The other two flake checks (`agent-mcp` Python build, `agent-mcp-dashboard` Next.js build) duplicate the existing `python` and `dashboard` jobs and would inflate CI time for no signal. The VM checks are the unique value — they boot the full server inside a NixOS VM and exercise the HTTP surface end-to-end, including the asset-prefix sentinel grep from #166.

### Modern Nix CI actions

- `DeterminateSystems/nix-installer-action@main` — recommended over legacy `cachix/install-nix-action`
- `DeterminateSystems/magic-nix-cache-action@main` — free, no token required, GitHub-hosted caching

### Required check, blocks merge

This is added as a regular job, so it becomes part of the required-checks set by default and will block merge if the nixosTests regress.

## Expected CI time

- **First run** (cold cache): ~30 minutes (downloads NixOS VM closure, builds dashboard via Nix, boots two QEMU VMs sequentially)
- **Cached runs** (warm magic-nix-cache): ~5-10 minutes
- `timeout-minutes: 60` gives generous headroom

## Local verification

Ran `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.vm-single-tenant .#checks.x86_64-linux.vm-multi-tenant -L --print-build-logs` locally on a clean worktree at this branch's tip. Both VMs booted, both finished their test scripts (~17s VM-time each), exit code 0. The asset-prefix sentinel curls all returned 0 status:

```
vm-test-run-agent-mcp-single-tenant> machine: (finished: must succeed: curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:1337/agent-mcp/app/only-project/ | grep -c '__AGENT_MCP_ASSET_PREFIX__' || true, in 0.06 seconds)
vm-test-run-agent-mcp-multi-tenant> test script finished in 17.27s
vm-test-run-agent-mcp-single-tenant> test script finished in 17.67s
```

## Version

Bumps `pyproject.toml` 5.0.49 → 5.0.50 per release convention.

body: fix(fivepaisa): use real intraday history timestamps + cubic.dev review fixes --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes FivePaisa intraday history to use real IST candle timestamps, preventing mid‑session cutoffs and preserving legitimate quiet-minute candles. Also hardens order logging and makes streaming subscriptions more reliable. - **Bug Fixes** - Intraday history: keep the API’s IST timestamps; remove renumbering; only drop fully empty candles. Daily keeps stricter holiday filters; indices keep all‑zero rule. - Parse candle time as IST instead of localizing to UTC, removing a hidden +5:30 offset. - Index mapping: exact symbol match only to avoid remapping cash instruments like NIFTYBEES to `*_INDEX`. - Order placement: log only the request body (exclude `head.key`) to prevent API key leakage in logs. - Streaming: on unsubscribe, remove any queued subscribe for the same scrip to avoid stale re‑subscriptions; fix a lost‑wakeup race by deciding empty-queue exits under lock and clearing the worker handle. body:
## What

Aligns the CSV exporter with the ad-hoc converter naming convention and consolidates its docs, following a docs review.

### Naming
`parquet2csv` was the only converter whose **function name equalled its module name** — the others use `convert_<src>_to_<dst>` functions inside `<src>2<dst>` modules.

- Function renamed to **`convert_parquet_to_csv`** (module `parquet2csv.py` kept — it already matches the `*2*` module pattern).
- Backward-compatible **`parquet2csv` alias** retained, marked deprecated for removal in a future release. Both are exported from `format_converters/__init__`.

### Docs
- Folded the standalone `parquet2csv` API page into the converters page, now **"Ad-hoc converters & exports"**.
- Broadened the intro to distinguish **round-trip converters** (overlap-resolving write path, class counterparts) from **one-way exports**, with a new **"Export to CSV"** section that states `convert_parquet_to_csv` has no overlap-resolving write path and no class counterpart.
- Updated `mkdocs.yml` nav, the API index table (grouped with the converters, alias noted), and the architecture diagram.

## Why

`parquet_to_csv` (the originally-floated name) matches neither convention; `convert_parquet_to_csv` matches the function convention and groups cleanly with `convert_parquet_to_zarr` et al. CSV is a terminal export rather than a working pipeline format, so the docs now make that distinction explicit instead of listing it as just another converter.

## Testing

## What

A high-value, DB-free test tranche for the money/engine paths the audit flagged as under-tested. Everything is deterministic via the repo's recording-fake / node:test pattern — no live DB (RLS is verified separately by the orchestrator), no Stripe, no network.

## New / extended tests

**NEW `web/src/lib/payments/refunds.test.ts` (8 tests)** — event-based refund idempotency (`recordPartialRefund`):
- A re-delivered `charge.refunded` (same `provider_refund_id`) is a no-op → NO second clawing row.
- A genuinely new partial (new id) records exactly once, carrying ITS OWN slice (not the cumulative charge total).
- Legacy no-id payload dedups on the prior `(txn, amount, status='refunded')` probe.
- A concurrent `23505` unique-violation on insert is a benign re-delivery race → `false`, not an error.
- Zero/negative slice + missing-parent short-circuits.
- `recordPartialRefund` is now **exported** (purely additive — doc comment + `export`, no behavior change) so the dedup contract is unit-testable without a live DB. The handler entry points (`handleBookingRefund`) resolve their own service-role client and aren't injectable, so the contract lives in this function.

**EXTEND `web/src/lib/billing/commission.test.ts` (+11 tests)**:
- Odd-cents subtotals that don't divide evenly still hold the per-row invariant (Σ lanes == `gross_charged`) through the `Math.round`/`floor` seams.
- Client/seller split ratio (`client_surcharge_bps`) incl. clamp to `[0, take]`: 0 share, full share, over-take clamp, negative→0.
- Talent-protective seller deduction capped at a thin margin (shortfall surfaced, talent never clawed below quote).
- Multi-participant largest-remainder reconciliation across 4 ugly-cents lanes (zero drift) + a multi-cent injected drift routed to the largest-gross participant.

**EXTEND `web/src/lib/inquiry/retry-failed-engine-effects.test.ts` (+3 tests)**:
- A replayable row whose listener throws on re-run is NOT resolved (attempt++ + `next_retry_at` backoff).
- Backoff escalates with `attempt_count` (exponential, capped — poison rows can't hot-loop the sweep).
- The selection SELECT applies the cap (`attempt_count < 5`) + the `next_retry_at` due-or-null window + the 50-row batch.

## CI target

New `test:money` npm script aggregating `commission*`, `refunds`, `transfers`, `booking-payouts-ledger`, `disburse`, `payout-rail-policy`, `offers`, `retry` (uses the `register-server-only-test.cjs` shim, mirrors the other `test:*` targets). Wired into the `ci` chain right after `test:billing`. This is what brings the new refunds + retry coverage into CI — they were in no prior script.

## Verification

Ran locally against the shared checkout's toolchain (the worktree has no node_modules): commission 43/43, refunds 8/8, retry 7/7; full `test:money` aggregate **140/140 pass**, 0 fail.

## Gaps intentionally left (need a live DB or a seam not in this lane)
- `handleBookingRefund` / `reconcilePartialRefund` end-to-end (full vs partial routing, clawback wiring, dispute lost/won) — these resolve `createServiceRoleClient()` / `getStripe()` internally with no injection seam; covered only at the boundaries here (`recordPartialRefund` dedup + the `charge.refunded` slice/id extraction already pinned in `webhook-routing.test.ts`).
- `submitTalentRate` margin (item #3) and the action guards (`requireOwner`/`requireStaff`/`requireAdmin`/`requireTalent`/`requireClient` + `requireInquiryManagerAction`) were already thoroughly covered (`inquiry-engine-offers.test.ts` A1/A1b, `action-guards.security.test.ts`); `computeTalentProtectiveClawback` is covered in `booking-payouts-ledger.test.ts`. No new tests added there to avoid duplication.
- The retry cap/backoff *DB filter* is asserted at the query layer (the SELECT applies `.lt`/`.or`/`.limit`); whether Postgres honors it is RLS/DB-level and out of unit scope.
