- Derivation lives in a small `day-sport` helper (keeps `build-week-summary` under its line cap), unit-tested for coaching-first precedence + the workout-sport map.
- **Duration-proportional width is deferred** (so this *refs*, not closes, #744): the per-source durations are heterogeneous (free-string coaching durations + KRD seconds) with no shared parser, and encoding magnitude as size is exactly what #736 deliberately avoided. It deserves a dedicated design pass rather than a fragile parse here.

## Tests
- `day-sport` (precedence + map + null fallbacks), `weekstrip-mark` (glyph vs dot vs empty), updated `build-week-summary` expectations.
- All Today-dir tests green (65); tsc + lint clean.

body:
## Overview

Data-driven shop, an on-deck vending-machine automat, weapon switching, and a round-end augment draft.

> **Stacked on #5.** Base is `feature/track-a-weapons`, so this diff shows only the shop/automat/augment work. GitHub will retarget it to `main` automatically once #5 merges.

## What's implemented

**Shop (Track B)**
- Data-driven `UpgradeDefinition` (polymorphic ScriptableObjects) + `ShopManager`. Base upgrades: weapon damage, fire rate, ferry health. Master upgrade: Pistol **Querschläger** (ricochet to nearest enemy).
- Purchase caps: each upgrade max **3×**, Querschläger **1×**. Shop shows `Name ($cost) count/max`.

**Vending-machine automat (Track C)**
- `ShopInteractable` on the deck: walk into range, press **B** to open/close the shop **any time during a round** (the round keeps running). Close button in the overlay too.

**Weapon switching**
- Mouse scroll + keys **1** Harpoon / **2** Pistol / **3** Shotgun / **4** Flamethrower. HUD shows the active weapon + slot.

**Round-end augment draft (Track C)**
- At each round end the player drafts **1 of 3** random augments (replaces the old round-end shop popup); picking applies the effect and starts the next round.
- Augments v1: **Tailwind** (crossing 15% faster), **Repair Kit** (heal 5% ferry HP per round), **The Swarm** (2× enemies, ½ HP), **Bruisers** (½ enemies, 2× HP).
- Draft buttons render a bold name + a description line so picks are informed. Effects stack across picks and reset on New Game (`EnemySpawner` count/HP multipliers, `GameManager` crossing speedup + per-round heal).

## How to test

1. Open the project in Unity and let it compile — Console should be clean.
2. Run **`Rollfaehren Fury > Build Prototype Scene`** (regenerates `Main.unity`, creates the Upgrade + Augment assets, wires the UI). A rebuild is required for the purchase caps and the new round flow.
3. Press **Play**.

**Shop automat** — walk to the orange box on deck, press **B**: shop opens while the round keeps running. Buy upgrades (watch money + the active weapon's stats in the HUD), then press the Close button or **B** to exit. Confirm each upgrade caps at 3 buys and Querschläger at 1.

**Weapon switching** — scroll or press 1–4; the HUD weapon indicator updates and the fire behaviour changes (hitscan / spread / arcing harpoon).

**Augment draft** — survive a round (the crossing timer fills). At round end the **"Choose an Augment"** panel shows 3 cards with name + description. Pick one → the next round starts and the effect applies:
- **Tailwind** → the next crossing is visibly shorter.
- **Repair Kit** → the ferry heals at each round end (take some damage first to see it).
- **The Swarm** → next round has more, weaker enemies.
- **Bruisers** → next round has fewer, tankier enemies (count is clamped to ≥1, so the drop is small in early rounds).

Effects stack if you pick the same one again and persist for the run; **New Game** resets them.

## Not in scope (deferred)

- Mechanic-heavy augments (mines, gulls, oil slick, shield, deck defense, economy/synergy) — need new mechanics that don't exist yet.
- Per-weapon master upgrades (Vogelschreck-Munition, Ketten-Harpune, Brennendes Öl) — need magazine/reload, knockback, fuel/burn.
- Second enemy variant.

author: ciankellyy
body:
💡 What: Replaced a `groupBy` and subsequent `findMany` with a dynamically generated `OR` array with a single `findMany` using `distinct: ['userId']` and `orderBy`.
🎯 Why: The previous approach required two queries and built a potentially massive `OR` array, which scales poorly with many users and causes an N+1-like database bottleneck.
📊 Impact: Reduces query time and memory footprint by executing a single indexed database operation instead of two, eliminating the generation of large SQL `OR` clauses.
🔬 Measurement: Review the performance of the `/api/admin/members` endpoint when a server has thousands of members and shifts. Time-to-first-byte should be significantly faster and database load reduced.

author: nvolpe2007-cell
body:
## Summary
- `LiveTrader.reconcile_positions()` (`src/live_trading.py`) called the raw, unprotected `ccxt` method directly (`self.exchange.exchange.fetch_positions(...)`), bypassing the exchange wrapper's retry/circuit-breaker protection, and swallowed **any** failure — including transient network errors, not just genuine "no positions" responses — into an empty position dict.
- That's a real safety gap for live trading: a crash/restart during a network blip could let the bot open a duplicate position on top of one already live on Kraken, or silently drop SL/TP management on a real position. It directly contradicts the file's own documented safety guarantee ("Startup reconciliation: syncs bot state with actual Kraken open positions").
- Added `ExchangeConnection.get_positions()` — a retrying wrapper that **raises** after exhausting retries instead of returning `[]` (deliberately unlike `fetch_ohlcv`/`fetch_order_book`, where "no data" is a safe fallback — here "couldn't ask the exchange" must not be conflated with "no positions").
- `reconcile_positions()` now uses it and no longer catches the error itself.
- `run_live_trading_session()` now catches that failure at startup, sends a Telegram alert, and aborts **before** any background task (OFI/HTF fetchers, SL/TP watcher, candle refresher) or the main trading loop starts — instead of proceeding with an unknown position state.

## Scope / lane note
- Touches `src/live_trading.py` (directional-strategy lane) and `src/exchange.py` (shared/neutral infra, not in either lane). No strategy/signal logic changed — confined to the reconciliation path and its call site.
- `DIRECTIONAL_ENABLED=0` by default, so this path isn't live in production today, but it's the correct fix before that engine is ever switched on.
- Avoided touching `LivePosition`/`open_long()`/`close_long()` to stay clear of PR #16 (open, unmerged, touches those same areas).

## Test plan
- [x] `python -m pytest tests/test_exchange.py tests/test_live_trading.py -q` → 181 passed
- [x] `python -m pytest tests/ -q` → 2521 passed (full suite, no regressions)
- Added `TestGetPositions` (4 tests: success, retry-then-succeed, raise-after-exhausting-retries, symbols passthrough).
- Rewrote `TestReconcilePositions`'s exception test (`test_fetch_failure_propagates_instead_of_assuming_empty`) to assert the new raise-don't-swallow behavior.
- Added `TestRunLiveTradingSessionReconcileAbort` (2 tests: aborts + alerts when reconciliation fails, doesn't blow up when no notifier is configured).

author: besendorf
body:
## Summary

Adds custom module loading for module-running `check-*` commands on iOS and Android. Users can load external Python modules from a file or folder with `--load-module`, or configure a folder globally with `MVT_CUSTOM_MODULES`.

Custom modules can declare `supported_commands` platform/command tuples so MVT only lists and executes modules that apply to the active command. The filtering happens before dependency ordering, and applicable custom modules are appended after built-in modules so built-in ordering remains stable while custom modules can still depend on existing MVT module classes.

AndroidQF now propagates loaded custom modules into nested bugreport, backup, and intrusion-log checks, where each nested command applies its own command filter.

## Impact

This lets researchers and developers run local experimental modules without installing them into the MVT package, while keeping unsupported modules out of command listings, dependency graphs, and execution.

body:
## Summary

Free drawing now supports five distinct brush personalities: Pencil, Marker, Brush, Technical, and Calligraphy. People can switch the character of future strokes or restyle existing free-draw elements without adding another toolbar tool, while pen input reliably uses physical pressure.

## Design

- Store a semantic `strokeShape` on each free-draw element and resolve rendering through one typed profile source.
- Keep Pencil pixel-compatible with the previous hardcoded `perfect-freehand` options so legacy drawings retain their appearance.
- Use the existing property-action and history paths for current defaults, selected elements, mixed selections, undo, redo, and style copy/paste.
- Expose the same accessible five-option control in full, compact, and mobile property surfaces.
- Detect stylus pressure from `pointerType === "pen"`; mouse and touch continue using simulated pressure.

## Compatibility

- Missing or unknown preset values normalize to Pencil during construction and restore.
- The chosen preset persists with each element for canvas rendering, SVG export, erasing, hit testing, and later sessions.
- The current preset preference persists in browser state but is excluded from exported and server app state.

## Test Plan

- `yarn fix`
- `yarn test:typecheck`
- Focused free-draw, restore, and style tests: 58 passing
- `yarn test:update`: 106 files and 1,418 tests passing
- Browser verification at 1440x1000, 800x700, and 390x844:
  - five controls fit without overflow
  - presets produce distinct visible strokes
  - mixed selection, undo, and redo behave correctly
  - browser preference survives reload

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

No additional operational monitoring is required because this is client-only drawing behavior.

- Validate during the first 24 hours by creating, restyling, exporting, and restoring each preset in production.
- Healthy behavior: preset selection persists, geometry renders consistently, exports match the canvas, and no console errors appear.
- Failure signals: legacy strokes change appearance, preset controls disappear, or restored strokes fall back unexpectedly.

author: tumult1337
body:
## Finding L6 — No fuzz tests for the wire-facing parsers

The wire parsers consume untrusted network bytes and had no fuzz coverage. This PR adds Go native `go test -fuzz` harnesses for the five untrusted-input parsers and fixes the OOB/DoS bugs the fuzzers surfaced.

### Fuzz targets (`core/fuzz_parsers_test.go`)
Each is seeded with valid AND malformed inputs via `f.Add(...)` and asserts: no panic, no hang, and no success result with out-of-bounds/negative offsets or lengths exceeding the input.

| Target | Parser | Invariant asserted |
|---|---|---|
| `FuzzParseH1RequestHead` | `ParseH1RequestHead` (`core/h1_plain.go`) | on `ok`, `0 < headerEnd <= len(data)`; `ok=false` ⇒ `headerEnd==0`; `contentLength >= -1` (−1 is the unparseable-CL sentinel) |
| `FuzzQPACKDecode` | `QPACKDecoder.Decode` (`core/qpack.go`) | no panic; header count within the 128 cap |
| `FuzzHpackDecode` | `HpackDecoder.Decode` (`core/hpack.go`) | no panic; header count within the 128 cap |
| `FuzzQuicParseFrames` | `quicParseFrames` (`core/quic_frame.go`) | every visitor-delivered slice (CRYPTO/STREAM data, NEW_TOKEN, NEW_CONNECTION_ID) has `len <= len(input)` |
| `FuzzQuicParseLongHeader` | `quicParseLongHeader` (`core/quic_packet.go`) | on success `total <= len(data)`, `payloadOff+payloadLen <= len(data)`, dcid/scid/token slices within input |

### Real bugs found and fixed
The fuzzers found 4 crashers across 2 bug classes. All are reachable from decrypted/parsed untrusted input and are panics (DoS). Fixes are trivial bounds guards mirroring the existing `HpackDecodeString` pattern; the crashing inputs are kept as regression seeds under `core/testdata/fuzz/`.

**1. QPACK integer→int cast before bounds check (OOB slice / index panic).** A huge wire-supplied length or static-table index was cast `int(uint64)` *before* the bounds comparison; on 64-bit the cast overflows negative, the `< len` / `> len` check then passes, and the subsequent slice/index panics (`slice bounds out of range [:-5882...]`, `index out of range [11038...] with length 99`). Fixed in four spots in `core/qpack.go` by comparing the `uint64` against the table/input length before any cast:
- indexed static reference (`idx < uint64(len(qpackStaticTable))`)
- literal name-reference index (`nameIdx < uint64(...)`)
- literal name length (`nameLen > uint64(len(data))` guard)
- `qpackDecodeString` value length (`sLen > uint64(len(data))` guard)

Crasher seeds: `FuzzQPACKDecode/b882cb72fe738775`, `7467afe6b57b1f9b`, `6d4447a2cb56f916`.

**2. QUIC ACK unbounded allocation (`makeslice: len out of range`).** `parseACK` did `make([]quicAckRange, rangeCount)` directly from an untrusted varint (up to 2^62), panicking / allowing unbounded allocation. Fixed in `core/quic_frame.go` by rejecting `rangeCount > p.remaining()` before the `make` (each range needs ≥2 bytes, so a larger count is unsatisfiable anyway).

Crasher seed: `FuzzQuicParseFrames/83519612b79aa7c2`.

### Smoke-run results (`-fuzztime`, post-fix, no crashers)
- `FuzzParseH1RequestHead` — ~1.98M execs / 10s, PASS
- `FuzzQPACKDecode` — ~2.46M execs / 30s, PASS (clean after fixes)
- `FuzzHpackDecode` — ~0.56M execs / 10s, PASS (no bugs found)
- `FuzzQuicParseFrames` — ~2.66M execs / 20s, PASS (clean after fix)

author: cianfru
body:
## The problem
Every video post was silently downgrading to a static PNG on X. The bot logs show it clearly (run #35, the **landscape** `milestones` cube — so this **predates the 4:5 portrait work**):

```
media upload attempt 1/4 failed (code 503) — retrying in 2000ms
... 2/4 ... 3/4 ...
video upload failed after retries → posting PNG instead: Request failed with code 503
```

The tell: in that same run the **PNG fallback uploaded fine through the same client**. So **image uploads work on X's v2 media endpoint; video uploads reliably 503** on our app tier.

## The fix
Route **video** through the battle-tested **v1.1 chunked upload** endpoint (`client.v1.uploadMedia`) and attach the resulting `media_id` to the v2 tweet. Images stay on v2 (already working). The app already authenticates against v1.1 (credential verification), so this needs no new permissions.

The **PNG fallback stays** as the ultimate safety net — if v1 ever fails, we post the image just like today, so there's **no regression**, only upside.

## Notes
- `twitter-api-v2@1.29.0` exposes both `v1.uploadMedia` and `v2.uploadMedia`; `media_id`s are interchangeable between v1 upload and v2 tweet.
- Updated `media-retry` tests for the v1 (video) / v2 (image) split, plus a new routing test. **37/37 pass.**

All 4 steps (44–47) delivered as real shell scripts, config files, systemd unit files, and design docs.

## Steps Delivered

| Step | What | Files |
|---|---|---|
| 44 | OS detector, dependency installer, Fennacminer config | `install.sh`, `fennac-config.sh`, `fennac-pool.conf` |

```
Fennacminer (port 4433)
  → WireBruce tunnel (127.0.0.1:4435)
  → stunnel TLS 1.3 (pool.fennac.io:4434)
  → Fennac pool server
```

| Port | Service | Direction |
|---|---|---|
| 4433 | Fennacminer local | Outbound from miner |
| 4435 | WireBruce listener | Local loopback |

```
stunnel-fennac.service
```

- TLS 1.3 enforced (`sslVersion = TLSv1.3`)

body:
# PR Summary: Space Templates (`feature/space-templates`)

**Branch:** `feature/space-templates` → `dev`  
**Commits:** 17 feature commits  
**Scope:** 47 files changed, +1633 / −576 lines

---

## Overview

This PR introduces a full **space-scoped template system** — the ability for space authors to publish templates into a space, have members auto-loaded into those templates on entry, and manage which template is the space default. It also consolidates space navigation, refactors how the current space is accessed in schemas, and includes schema-system bug fixes that unblock the new UI patterns.

---

## What Changed

### 1. New Data Models (`packages/models`)

**`Template`** — added a `slug` property (`we://slug`) and removed the `HasMany` relationship to `ChatSession`. Chat sessions now carry a `templateId` property directly, removing a redundant link and simplifying queries.

**`SpaceTemplatePreference`** (new) — stores a per-agent, per-space preference of `'space'` or `'user'`. Written to the we-root perspective. Used by the auto-apply logic to let users opt out of a space's default template for that specific space.

**`AgentSettings`** — two additions:
- `useSpaceTemplate: boolean` — global flag for whether the agent wants space-default templates applied.
- `spaceTemplatePreferences: SpaceTemplatePreference[]` (HasMany) — per-space overrides.

---

### 2. SDNA Registration (`packages/app-framework/src/sdnaModels.ts`)

`SpaceTemplatePreference` and `Template` registered in SDNA so they're available in both the we-root and space perspectives.

---

### 3. TemplateStore Refactor (`packages/app-framework/src/frameworks/solid/stores/TemplateStore.tsx`)

The single `templates` accessor has been split into three:

| Accessor | Content |
|---|---|
| `personalTemplates` | Core templates + user-installed custom templates, excluding space templates |
| `spaceTemplates` | Templates stored in the current space perspective |
| `coreTemplates` | Built-in templates from the registry only |

**New infrastructure:**
- `spaceTemplateMap` — tracks AD4M `Template` model instances for the current space (needed for edits/saves).
- `spaceTemplateCache` (session-scoped, keyed by perspective UUID) — prevents redundant AD4M fetches when re-visiting a space in the same session. Cache hits restore synchronously; misses trigger a full fetch and populate the cache.

**New methods:**
- `loadSpaceTemplates(perspective)` — fetches all `Template` models from a space perspective, decodes their schemas, and merges them into `allTemplates` as space-owned entries.
- `preloadSpaceTemplates(perspective)` — cache-aware wrapper: sync restore on hit, async fetch on miss.
- `clearSpaceTemplates()` — removes space templates from reactive state before switching spaces.

**Auto-apply logic:** A `createEffect` fires on every space navigation. If the cache is already warm (pre-loaded by `navigateToSpace`), the default template is applied synchronously. On deep-link or page refresh, it falls back to an async path that fetches both the templates and the `SpaceTemplatePreference` from the root perspective. Priority: per-space `'user'` override > space `defaultTemplateId` > nothing.

**`saveTemplateAs`** — accepts an optional `destination: 'root' | 'space'` argument. When `'space'`, the template is written to the current space perspective (not linked to `AgentSettings`), and `loadSpaceTemplates` is called to refresh.

---

### 4. SpaceStore Refactor (`packages/app-framework/src/frameworks/solid/stores/SpaceStore.tsx`)

**`currentSpace`** — the current space's `Space` model is now held as a reactive signal in SpaceStore, subscribed directly via `Space.query(p, { where: { uuid: p.uuid } })`. Previously, templates accessed space data via a `$single` query embedded in the schema (see below). Moving it to the store makes the data available immediately to any store or component.

**`spaceDefaultTemplateId`** — derived signal from `currentSpace()?.defaultTemplateId`, writable for optimistic updates via `setSpaceDefaultTemplate`.

**`setSpaceDefaultTemplate(templateId)`** — optimistically updates local state, writes the new `defaultTemplateId` to `Space` in the perspective, and keeps the `mySpaces` cache in sync.

**`navigateToSpace` consolidated** — `enterSpace` and the old synchronous `navigateToSpace` have been merged into a single async function. It now:
1. Resolves the perspective from either a CID or UUID segment.
2. Calls `preloadSpaceTemplates` **before** switching the perspective, so templates are ready by the time the route renders.
3. Routes to the target path and notifies embedded iframes.

**Deep-link / refresh handler** — a new `createEffect` watches the route segments. When the URL already points to a space (deep link or F5), it resolves the perspective and pre-loads templates, mirroring what `navigateToSpace` does for intentional navigation.

---

### 5. New Schema Routes

**`SettingsRoute`** (`packages/app-framework/src/shared/schemas/DefaultTemplate/routes/SettingsRoute/index.ts`)  
A new `/settings` route for spaces. Displays:
- **Core templates** — always listed; "Set as default" button (writes `Space.defaultTemplateId` via `spaceStore.setSpaceDefaultTemplate`); highlighted when active.
- **Space templates** — conditionally rendered section listing templates saved to the current space.

**`TemplatesList`** (`routes/CardsRoute/TemplatesList.ts`)  
A new content type in CardsRoute. Queries `Template` models in the current space, renders each in a card with:
- Author avatar + name + handle.
- "Apply" button to switch template locally.
- "Set as default" button (space author only, guarded by `$if` comparing `spaceStore.currentSpace.author` to `adamStore.me.did`).
- Version badge + "Space default" badge when applicable.

`CardsRoute/index.ts` updated to include `'templates'` as a recognised `contentType` so the `$if` fallback to `blocksList` doesn't trigger.

---

### 6. SpaceSidebar — Remove `$single` Gate (`SidebarLayout/SpaceSidebar.ts`)

The entire `$single` query wrapper (which blocked rendering until an AD4M fetch resolved) has been removed. Space data (`name`, `avatar`, `coverImage`, etc.) now comes directly from `spaceStore.currentSpace`, which is already populated before the route renders.

**Sidebar template list** (`shell/Sidebar.schema.ts`) updated to reference `templateStore.personalTemplates` instead of `templateStore.templates` so space-specific templates don't appear in the user's personal template sidebar.

---

### 7. AI Chat Destination Toggle (`AiStore`, `ChatPanel`)

When a user creates or forks a template inside the AI chat:
- `AiStore` now exposes `pickerShowDestination: boolean` (true when `adamStore.currentPerspective()` is set, i.e. when inside a space).
- `confirmPicker` accepts `destination: 'personal' | 'space'` and passes `'space'` to `saveTemplateAs` when appropriate.
- `ChatPanel` renders a "Save to" toggle between **My templates** and **This space** when `pickerShowDestination` is true.
- AI model string updated from `claude-sonnet-4-20250514` to `claude-sonnet-4-6`.

---

### 8. Schema System Fixes (`packages/schema-system/shared/src`)

**`indexer.ts` — props-embedded SchemaNode traversal**  
`ensureNodeIds` and `findNodeById` previously skipped SchemaNodes embedded directly in `props` (e.g. `$if.props.then`, `$if.props.else`). Two new helpers fix this:
- `isPropsSchemaNode(val)` — distinguishes a SchemaNode from style objects, data items, and operator tokens by checking `type` matches a component naming pattern (PascalCase, hyphenated, or `$`-prefixed).
- `forEachPropsNode(node, fn)` — walks every value in `node.props`, calling `fn` for each SchemaNode-shaped value (including arrays). Called inside both `collectIds` and `assignIds` passes.

`findNodeById` similarly extended to search prop-embedded nodes, returning the correct `key` (`pro

### Motivation
- The build failed because `useSearchParams()` was being used in a component that prerenders, causing a CSR bailout error for `/reset-password` during export. 
- The root layout fetched Google Fonts at build time which caused network fetch failures during production builds. 
- Email routes instantiated `Resend` at module load time which crashed build-time route analysis when `RESEND_API_KEY` was missing.

### Description
- Moved the `useSearchParams()` usage into a client-only `ResetPasswordForm` component and render it inside a `Suspense` boundary so `/reset-password` can be prerendered; changed `src/app/reset-password/page.tsx` accordingly. 
- Removed `next/font/google` imports and class variables from `src/app/layout.tsx` to avoid build-time Google Fonts network fetches and simplified the `<html>` element. 
- Replaced top-level `new Resend(process.env.RESEND_API_KEY)` with a lazy `getResend()` helper that throws a clear error when `RESEND_API_KEY` is not configured, and updated calls to use `getResend()` in `src/app/api/emails/route.ts`, `src/app/api/vault/[id]/send/route.ts`, and `src/app/api/tasks/reminders/route.ts` so missing env vars no longer crash the build. 

### Testing
- Ran `npm run build` which completed successfully after the fixes. 
- Ran the TypeScript check via `npm run lint` (`tsc --noEmit`) which completed successfully.

## What changed

Implements issue #75:

1. **Removed default file labels except "Done".** New projects previously seeded four status labels (Not started, Not Reviewed, Done, Dead end); now only **Done** remains as a file label.
2. **Added a separate "information level" label category** with defaults: **Fact, Opinion, Misinformation, Disinformation.**

## How

Labels now carry a `type` discriminator (`'file' | 'information'`, default `'file'`) on the `labels` table. The two categories are managed and displayed in distinct UI sections.

- **Schema** (`lib/drizzle/schema.ts`): added `type text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'file'`. Migration `0004_brainy_supreme_intelligence.sql` — existing label rows get `'file'` via the column default, so no separate backfill is needed.
- **Server** (`lib/projects.server.ts`): split `DEFAULT_LABELS` into `DEFAULT_FILE_LABELS` + `DEFAULT_INFORMATION_LABELS`; `getLabels`/`createLabel` now read and return `type`.
- **Types & client** (`lib/projects.ts`): `Label.type` added; `createLabel` accepts a `type` argument.
- **API** (`app/api/projects/[id]/labels/route.ts`): POST forwards `type` from the request body.
- **Project Settings modal**: one label list → two sections ("File Labels" / "Information Level Labels"), each with its own add button.
- **File Sidebar**: one "Labels" section → two subsections ("File Labels" / "Information Level"), each with its own picker, filtered by `type`.

## Reviewer notes

- Both categories remain fully editable (add/rename/recolor/delete) per the original request.
- Backward compatible: pre-migration label rows and any payloads without `type` fall back to `'file'`.

author: juanlu-a
body:
## Problem
Every `Deploy → Staging` / `Deploy → Prod` run has been failing at the **E2E tests** stage on a single test:

```
test_ingest_then_list_pipeline
  assert ingest_r.status_code == 200
  AssertionError: Ingest failed: {"status": "accepted", "session_key": "9158",
                  "message": "Ingestion started. Data will be available shortly."}
```

`ingest_session` is **asynchronous** — it fires an EventBridge `IngestRequested` event and returns **202 Accepted** immediately, while `ingest_worker` + `save_session` populate data afterwards. The test still asserted a synchronous **200**.

## Fix
Accept `200` or `202` for the ingest call (one line). The existing `time.sleep(5)` and the `_DB_OK = (200, 404, 500)` tolerance on the downstream `/sessions` assertion are unchanged.

The sibling `test_ingest_then_drivers_pipeline` already passed because it doesn't assert the ingest status code.

## Scope
Test-only; no app or infra change. Unblocks the deploy pipelines' e2e stage.

author: hairyboy
body:
First real social step — **friend-keys with no backend**. A friend you add can approve an early vault unlock from **their own wallet**, replacing the custodied server-signing sim.

## What's in it
- **Friends store** (`web/lib/friends.ts`) — add friends by wallet address + nickname, kept in localStorage per-device. Seeds the Anvil accounts locally; starts empty on testnet/prod. Replaces the hardcoded Ana/Luis.
- **Friends tab** — add-by-address form + an editable list (was a stub). No-friends-yet create picker links here.
- **Create** — the keyholder picker reads *your* friends; their real addresses go on-chain as keyholders.
- **Vault detail is role-aware** via the connected wallet:
  - **Keyholder** → a real **"Approve unlock"** signing `approveEarlyExit` from their own MiniPay wallet (gas in USDC via fee abstraction — no CELO needed).
  - **Owner** → Deposit / Withdraw / Request; **Request** copies the vault link to share out-of-band.
  - **Stranger** with the link → read-only note.
- Removed the now-orphaned `/friends/[id]` stub.
- **`e2e/`** — saved the adversarial testnet harness into the repo (own package, env-parameterized, no hardcoded keys; README included).

## Verification
Adversarial testnet e2e (3 wallets, production build, real signing) — **19/19**:
- the self-approve path unlocks the vault (signed by the friend's own wallet);
- owner can't self-approve; a non-keyholder is barred (UI **and** on-chain revert);
- once unlocked the button is gone; a redundant approve is an idempotent no-op (can't inflate the threshold);
- funds recovered (deposits withdrawn — net cost ~cents of gas).

Plus `tsc`, `eslint`, `next build` all clean. Solo-only; shared vaults remain a v2 stub. Targets the **Celo Sepolia testnet** preview, not mainnet.

body:
## Workstream C — verify-first result

Only **one** of the audit's four claimed cross-cutting dedups survived verification as a genuine, clean swap:

**✅ Done — MLX tool-call extraction.** `mlx_provider._extract_tool_calls_from_content` was a *less-capable* near-duplicate of `openai_compat.extract_tool_calls_from_content` (missing the planning-keyword false-positive guard + the `<TOOL_OUTPUT>`/inline shapes). Parameterized the canonical with `id_prefix` and routed MLX through it (`id_prefix="mlx"`) — same output shape, strictly better extraction. Deleted the copy. 130 provider tests pass.

### The other 3 claims were verified FALSE / not-clean (audit over-reach):
- **Code-block regex "5 copies":** only `tool_extraction.py` ↔ `tool_call_extractor.py` share an identical pattern set; `context_compactor` (generic), `grounding_verifier` (`(?:\w+)?`), and `adapters` (`tool_code`-specific) are **distinct patterns sharing a variable name** — not duplicates.
- **`chunking.py` vs `tokenizer.py` `count_tokens`:** **not identical** — different native-fast-path usage and different fallbacks (`words*1.3` vs `words+punctuation`). Consolidating would change behavior, not dedup.
- **Semantic dedup "scattered across 4 files":** only **one** `_deduplicate_semantic` exists (`conversation/assembler.py`).

This matches the pattern seen in PR-B: the exploration audit systematically over-claimed duplication; the verify-first approach correctly filtered it.

Part of the approved plan (`.claude/plans/swirling-humming-dahl.md`).

author: devtank42
body:
## Summary

Renovate (self-hosted via this reusable workflow, ADR-0017) runs and pushes update branches but **opens no PRs** — every update stalls on the consumer's dependency dashboard as *"Errored"*. Root cause (see qnophq/qnop#67): the org enforces **"Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests = OFF"**, so the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` gets a 403 on `POST /pulls`. The repo-level toggle returns 409 — it can't override the org policy.

Even if the org toggle were enabled, PRs created by `GITHUB_TOKEN` do **not** trigger the consumer repos' `pull_request` workflows (GitHub anti-recursion), so they'd land without CI/CLA checks and be un-mergeable.

## Change

Authenticate Renovate as an **org-installed GitHub App** instead:
- Mint a short-lived installation token with `actions/create-github-app-token` (pinned `v3.2.0`), scoped by default to the repo running the workflow.
- Pass that token to `renovatebot/github-action` (and to checkout).
- Callers expose `RENOVATE_APP_ID` + `RENOVATE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` via `secrets: inherit`.

An App token is a distinct identity: it is not subject to the Actions-can't-create-PRs policy, **and** its PRs trigger the consumers' CI normally. Still single-repo — the installation token only reaches the calling repo.

## Consumer requirements (per repo opting in)

1. Install the Renovate GitHub App on the repo (Contents, Pull requests, Issues, **Workflows** = read/write).
2. Add `RENOVATE_APP_ID` + `RENOVATE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` as **repository** secrets (or an org secret scoped to selected private repos — not "All repositories", to keep it off public repos).
3. Add `secrets: inherit` to the caller stub. (qnophq/qnop PR: separate, references this.)

## Test plan

- [ ] Merge, then in a consumer with the App installed + secrets set, run `gh workflow run renovate.yml` — Renovate opens PRs, and their CI runs.

Refs qnophq/qnop#67.

author: copilot
body:
The API diff comment emits a redundant `+ [Stage] Experimental` line when a new experimental type is introduced — the type header already carries the `[Experimental]` tag (e.g. `+ [Experimental] MyType`). The stage line is only meaningful when the stage of a pre-existing type changes.

### Changes
- In `ApiModel.CreateTypeDelta`, gate `addedStage`/`removedStage` on `stageChanged` (both `currentType` and `baselineType` present with differing stages) instead of also firing when one side is `null`. Added/removed types fall through to `Stable`, so `AppendStageDiffLine` no longer emits a line for them.

### Resulting output
```diff
- + [Experimental] Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Foo
- + [Stage] Experimental
+ + [Experimental] Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Foo
```

Stage-change diffs on existing types are unaffected:
```diff
  Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Foo
- [Stage] Experimental
+ [Stage] Stable
```

author: gunnjake
body:
Closes #99.

## Problem
Frontend API response types were hand-written and validated by nothing. Backend↔frontend shape drift shipped green — two runtime crashes (dashboard birthdays, `/admin/users` pagination) reached dev/prod because lint/tsc/build can't see the real contract.

## Change
- **Generator:** `scripts/gen-api-types.mjs` + `npm run gen:api-types` emit `src/types/api.gen.ts` from fa-web-api's `/openapi.json` (defaults to the dev deployment; override via `API_SCHEMA_URL`).
- **Schema normalization:** response models are normalized to required-nullable (`field: T | null`) — matching FastAPI's runtime serialization and the prior hand-written contract — so openapi-typescript's "optional → `| undefined`" quirk doesn't force ~40 noisy call-site edits. Request models (`*Create`/`*Update`/`*Request`/`Body_*`) keep their real optionality so partial-update forms still type-check.
- **Adoption:** `src/types/api.ts` exposes `Schema<"...">`; `profile.ts`, `tasks.ts`, and the core `alumni.ts` types alias the generated schema. **All 64 call sites became schema-checked with zero edits**, and 6 alumni fields the frontend was silently missing (`source_id`, `mst_id`, `birth_name`, `birth_year`, `manually_edited_at`, `last_imported_at`) are now present.
- **CI guard:** new `api-contract` job ("API types in sync with backend") regenerates from the served schema and fails on drift, forcing a regen that then makes `tsc` fail on stale usage.

## Acceptance
A backend field rename/removal that a frontend page depends on now fails CI before merge ✅

## Verified
lint ✅ · typecheck ✅ · build ✅ (24 routes) · generator deterministic ✅ · YAML valid ✅

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- **Geography endpoints return untyped `dict`s** in the backend (no `response_model`), so they can't be derived and stay hand-typed in `geography.ts` — the map surface is *not* covered by this guard. Needs a backend change in fa-web-api.
- To make the guard **block** merges, add the **"API types in sync with backend"** check as a required status check on the dev/prod rulesets.

author: mafarrag
body:
# Description

The `pyramids-gis` wheel bundles a vendored GDAL built with **no JPEG2000 driver**, so reading a
**JP2-compressed GRIB2** message (WMO packing template 5.40 — common from NCEP/HRRR, ECCC MSC Datamart
GDPS/RDPS/HRDPS, several ECMWF outputs) fails with:

```
... not recognized as being in a supported file format. It could have been recognized by driver
JP2OpenJPEG, but plugin gdal_JP2OpenJPEG.dll is not available in your installation.
```

The wheel-build env only installed `gdal` + `libgdal-netcdf`/`-hdf4`/`-grib` — never `libgdal-jp2openjpeg` —
so the JP2OpenJPEG plugin and its `libopenjp2` were never extracted or bundled. **This is a missing-driver
bug, not a GDAL-version issue** — JP2OpenJPEG is an optional plugin in 3.12 and 3.13 alike, so a version
bump would not fix it. The fix is to bundle the driver.

- Add `libgdal-jp2openjpeg` to the shared `[tool.pixi.feature.gdal.dependencies]` pin (pulls `openjpeg`).
  The existing plugin-vendoring (`setup-gdal-from-pixi.sh` → `install-and-vendor-osgeo.py`) then bundles
  `gdal_JP2OpenJPEG` + `libopenjp2` on Linux/Windows automatically.
- `setup-gdal-micromamba.sh`: install it on the macOS cross-build path too.
- `tests/test_gdal_pin.py`: add it to the enforced package set (feature + micromamba lists).
- `ci/verify-wheel.py`: assert the `JP2OpenJPEG` driver registers and round-trips — a regression gate.
- `pixi.lock`: re-solved via `pixi update` to add `libgdal-jp2openjpeg` + `openjpeg` (`gdal` stays 3.12.4).
  The `pixi update` re-solve also refreshes unrelated build hashes (the repo's sanctioned relock path).

Trade-off: the wheel grows by `openjpeg` (a few MB) — the size guardrails added in #475 account for it.

# Issues
- Fixes #600

Check relevant points.

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)

# How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] `tests/test_gdal_pin.py` — 13 passed: the shared gdal feature pins exactly the 5 packages
      (incl. `libgdal-jp2openjpeg`), every env references the feature, and `ci/gdal-pin.py` resolves it.
- [x] `ci/verify-wheel.py` extended with a JP2OpenJPEG register + write/read round-trip; runs in the
      `test-wheels` matrix against every bundled wheel.
- [ ] CI: `bundle-pypi-wheels.yml` full build + `test-wheels` matrix — confirms `gdal_JP2OpenJPEG` +
      `libopenjp2` are bundled and the new driver check passes on all 5 platforms. (dispatched)

author: ppryga-nordic
body:
How Kconfig defaults are evaluated:
Kconfig merges all `default` lines for a symbol into one list, walks it top to bottom, and uses the first entry whose condition is true. Later entries are ignored after a match. Conditions from parent `if` blocks and `depends on` are ANDed into each line.

When sdk-nrf Kconfig is parsed before another module that adds `default` lines for BT_RX_STACK_SIZE, sdk-nrf entries registered earlier take precedence whenever they match. Catch-all sdk-nrf defaults therefore blocked another module from setting a different value. Scoping sdk-nrf defaults to known SDC SoCs removes that block for SoCs outside the list.

Parse order among modules is not fixed: another module parsed before sdk-nrf cannot override BT_RX_STACK_SIZE via appended `default` lines either. Extension via later `default` lines only works when that module is parsed after sdk-nrf.

Kconfig load order:
1. soc/board Kconfig.defconfig
2. Zephyr modules (sdk-nrf included here)
3. Zephyr subsys (e.g. host BT_RX_STACK_SIZE) sdk-nrf is always processed before Zephyr subsys. Relative order among modules in step 2 is not defined by west manifest root.

sdk-nrf is always processed before Zephyr subsys. Relative order among modules in step 2 is not defined by west manifest root.

Existing sdk-nrf SDC SoCs (nRF52, nRF54L, nRF5340 net, nRF54H20 CPURAD, nRF71, BSIM, etc.) keep the same effective defaults.

Closes #555
Closes #556

Implements the `#` path-alias import mechanism (#555) and converts the in-repo apps, examples, and scaffold templates to use it (#556). #556 hard-depends on #555 (the alias must resolve before any import can be converted), so both ship together here.

## The alias shape: `#*` catch-all (Bun-safe, zero-maintenance)

The scaffold ships a single root catch-all in `package.json`:

```jsonc
"imports": { "#*": "./*" }
```

So `import { db } from '#db/connection.server.ts'`, `#components/...`, `#lib/...`, `#modules/...`, and any NEW top-level folder all resolve with no config change. Two findings drove the shape (verified on Node 26 + Bun 1.3.14):
- A `#/`-prefixed key (`"#/*": "./*"`, spelled `#/lib/...`) does **NOT** resolve on Bun (`Cannot find module '#/lib/x'`), only on Node. Since the blog runs on Bun on Railway, that would break the deploy. The slash-free `#*` form (spelled `#lib/...`) resolves natively on both.
- A single key keeps it zero-maintenance (a new folder needs no config), which per-directory keys would lose.

## #555: the mechanism (framework)
- `resolveImport` (module-graph) expands a matching `#` specifier to its real path BEFORE the relative branch (driven off the app's `"imports"` map), so the auth gate, modulepreload, elision, and `no-server-import-in-browser-module` all see through the alias. An alias cannot launder a `.server.ts` past the boundary (counterfactual test included).
- `importAliasBrowserEntries` (importmap) derives the browser scope from the SAME map. A bare `#` cannot be an importmap prefix key, so the `#*` catch-all is expanded into one trailing-slash scope per top-level dir (`#lib/` -> `/lib/`, ...) from a directory scan (`dev.js` `appTopLevelDirs`); a new folder is covered on the next boot. Server + browser stay in lockstep.
- `versionModuleImports` (asset-hash) rewrites a `#` import in prod served source to a base-path-safe versioned relative specifier, so it gets the same `?v` immutable cache + matched preload as a relative import (no #369 wasted preload); a `#` alias to a `.server.ts` is left unversioned.

The alias addresses a top-level SUBDIRECTORY (`#lib/...`); a root-level file is imported relatively (the browser scope is per-directory).

## #556: the conversion (apps + templates)
- `examples/blog`, `website`, `docs`, `packages/ui/packages/website`: app-internal deep relatives rewritten to `#` (including the Drizzle `db/` imports from #551). Imports that escape the app root (to `packages/server`, the ui registry sibling) stay relative.
- Scaffold template files + `create.js` / `saas-template.js` emit `#` (including the registry `cn` rewrite to `#lib/utils/cn.ts`), so a fresh app demonstrates the feature.

## Verification
- Unit + mechanism + scaffold tests green; `#` resolves natively on Node 26 AND Bun 1.3.14 (`test/bun/path-alias.mjs`, wired into CI).
- Dogfood: blog smoke 8/8, blog e2e 87/87, website/docs/ui-website boot 200 with the auto-derived `#` importmap scopes and no broken preloads; a real blog module imports clean on Bun.
- Self-review ran two rounds (round 1 found a real saas `cn`-rewrite regression + two missed real imports, fixed; round 2 found only `#/`-vs-`#` wording, fixed).

author: austinywang
body: Closes #5970 ## Problem Selecting any bundled extension-sidebar preset (e.g. "Project Worktrees", `com.example.cmux.sidebar.project-worktrees`) puts the app into a sustained ~100% CPU SwiftUI re-render loop and spinning beachball. Because the selection persists to `cmuxExtensionSidebar.providerId`, the loop fires again on next launch — effectively bricking the app on startup until the pref is cleared. ## Root cause Two compounding issues in the `VerticalTabsSidebar` body path (`Sources/ContentView.swift`): 1. **Self-sustaining re-render loop.** The extension-sidebar branches rebuilt their `.onReceive` observation publishers *inline on every body pass* (`Publishers.MergeMany(...).receive(on:)…`), handing SwiftUI a brand-new publisher instance each render. SwiftUI re-subscribes `.onReceive` to a new instance, and the merged `@Published`/`CurrentValueSubject` chains replay their current value on subscription — so each render re-fired the handler → bumped `extensionSidebarUpdateToken` (`@State` the body reads) → invalidated the body → rebuilt the publisher → re-subscribed … forever. The default workspaces sidebar has no such token/`.onReceive`, which is why it idles. 2. **Per-pass CPU catastrophe.** The branch condition called `descriptor(for:)` → `descriptors`, which constructs a full `SettingCatalog` *twice* (via `isEnabled`/`customSidebarsEnabled`) and enumerates the custom-sidebars directory — on every body pass and every `TimelineView` tick. The `SettingCatalog.init → AutomationCatalogSection.init` frame is exactly what the reporter's `sample` fingered. ## Fix - Memoize the composed observation publishers in a non-observed `ExtensionSidebarObservationPublishers` cache, rebuilt only when the workspace identity set changes. `.onReceive` now gets a **stable** instance, subscribes once, and the chain's `removeDuplicates()` suppresses no-op replays → render once, then idle. - `isEnabled` / `customSidebarsEnabled` read only `BetaFeaturesCatalogSection()` instead of the whole `SettingCatalog`. - New cheap `resolvesToDefaultSidebar(effectiveProviderId:)` predicate replaces the body's `descriptor(for:)` routing — no `descriptors` rebuild, no directory scan, at most two `fileExists` probes. The render-model path looks the provider up directly by the effective id. ## Tests Adds routing-equivalence regression tests (`SidebarProviderMenuRegressionTests`) pinning that the cheap predicate routes identically to the old descriptor lookup across built-ins, the hosted extension, unknown ids, and missing custom sidebars. ## Tradeoff / verification note The CPU loop itself isn't cleanly unit-testable without driving SwiftUI rendering; the added tests guard the cheap-routing refactor's behavioral equivalence. Per repo policy this was **not built locally** — CI is the verification gate. --- Need help on this PR? Tag /codesmith with what you need. Autofix is disabled. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes a sustained ~100% CPU SwiftUI re-render loop when selecting bundled extension sidebars, so the app no longer pegs CPU or bricks on restart. Fixes #5970 - **Bug Fixes** - Memoized merged sidebar observation publishers in view `@State` and moved refresh out of the body; rebuild on workspace changes via `.onAppear`/`.onChange` and clear on `.onDisappear`, so `.onReceive` stays stable and idles. - Replaced `descriptor(for:)` checks with a cheap `resolvesToDefaultSidebar(effectiveProviderId:)` and looked up providers directly by id to avoid `SettingCatalog` rebuilds and directory scans on each render. - Read beta flags from `BetaFeaturesCatalogSection` instead of constructing `SettingCatalog` on the body path. - Added regression tests for routing across built-ins, the hosted extension, unknown ids, and missing/invalid custom sidebars (blocks path traversal). Written for commit c4f039bee14a911ce3cb8e64d6ece4f19ec763d8. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Updated beta-controlled behavior for the Extensions sidebar using the active beta flags. * Improved sidebar routing logic to more efficiently determine when the default workspaces view should be shown. * **Bug Fixes** * Fixed a performance issue that caused repeated reactive updates in the Extensions sidebar. * Reduced unnecessary publisher rebuilds and refresh work to improve responsiveness. * **Tests** * Added regression tests covering routing for built-in, hosted, and fallback provider selections in the Extensions sidebar.

body:
Advances **THS-110 (HP-1 Phase 1)** from "DB stood up" to "engine runs end-to-end into `hp1.*`." Builds on the standalone topology (HP-1 owns its own data on `uetclnhbubmkwbherwkw`; no v2 `public.*` reads). Two commits.

## 1. HP-1 engine + loader + Action (`c5fc139`)

The factor math stays in `hp1_engine.py` (also the backtest's source — imported, never rewritten); everything new just fetches data, shapes rows, and writes.

- **`hp1_daily_run.py`** — pure `compute_run()` ranks the 50-name universe **per view × per sleeve** and emits one `hp1.engine_runs` row + ~200 `hp1.engine_ranks` rows.
  - Views (§2): `combined` / `pure_play` (L1+L3+L4) / `megacap` (L2+L5); z-scores recomputed **within each view**. Each name → `combined` + its category view → 4 rows/name.
  - Sleeves: `tactical` (.45zM+.35zRAM+.20zDD, gate >100dMA) and `core` (gate >200dMA).
  - `pct` = percentile within the view's *scored* set; `breadth_pct`/`gate_gross` per §4 (≥40→1.0, 25–40→0.5, <25→0.25).
- **`hp1_db.py`** — psycopg **direct-Postgres** I/O. `hp1` isn't exposed over PostgREST, and an engine/ETL job is naturally a direct-DB client; the owner/service role bypasses RLS (the documented loader/engine write path). Connection from `HP1_DB_URL`.
- **`hp1_price_loader.py`** — **yfinance** bootstrap → `hp1.prices` (idempotent upsert on `(ticker,date)`). Source-swappable to FMP/Polygon at `fetch_yf()` only.
- **`hp1_engine.factors()`** also emits `dist100`/`dist200` (additive; backtest/sim unaffected; `ddraw` already = `dd_from_high`).
- **CI/automation**: `.github/workflows/hp1-engine.yml` (post-close daily load→run + manual backfill); `ci.yml` gains a Python engine-test job; `engine/requirements.txt` pinned; `engine/README.md`.
- **Tests**: 15 new (engine-run shaping + gate/regime/tag helpers). **19 engine + 335 v2 edge-function tests pass.**

### Documented deviation — Core overlay
Spec §3 Core = price-only core ×0.75 + §5 fundamental overlay (Q/G/V/AIQ) ×0.25. The §5 overlay is live-only/unbacktested and its Tier-A inputs aren't in `hp1.*` yet, so Phase 1 writes the **price-only core** (`engine_version = v1.2-priceonly-core`). The blend lands when the overlay data does; the version string bumps so records stay distinguishable.

### Write path verified against the live standalone DB
`information_schema` column/type/nullability match for both tables, **plus** a `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` dry-run insert (1 run + 5 ranks, exercising the view/sleeve/`driver_tag` enums incl. hyphenated `broken-trend`) — **0 residue** after rollback.

## 2. Revert moot ingestion extension — #23 part b (`2651462`)

Under standalone, extending v2's FMP ingestion to the 19 hp1-only names is dead code. Restores `ingest-fundamentals/consensus/form4/short-interest` + `_shared/supabase.ts` (drops `INGEST_KINDS` + the `activeTickers` `kinds` option) to pre-#23. The #23 RLS-harden migration (part a) is untouched. 335 v2 tests pass.

## Remaining on THS-110 (gated on Terry)
- **`HP1_DB_URL`** repo secret = the standalone project's pooler connection string. Then trigger the Action once with `period=3y` to **backfill** (engine needs ≥253 trading days) before the daily `5d` appends.
- Optional: switch the price source from yfinance → FMP (drop-in at `fetch_yf`).
- Frontend fork (`terry-zero-in/hp1`) — separate phase.

Refs: `docs/hp1/HP1_SPEC_v1.1.md` §2–§4, `docs/handoffs/2026-06-17-S35-hp1-standalone-db-live.md`

body:
## Summary

Adds `GET /v1/hyperliquid/outcomes/users/positions` — current open share balance per (user, outcome leg). Backed by `state_user_outcome_position`, the substreams-hypercore v0.5.0 MV that computes the running share-flow sum across BUY / SELL / SETTLEMENT / SPLIT / MERGE / NEGATE events.

Three filter axes, additively composed (at least one required):
- `?user=0x...` — single-user position list
- `?outcome_id=357` — holder list for one outcome leg (top holders sorted by share_balance desc)
- `?question_id=32` — holder list across every outcome in the question

Every row carries an `OutcomeLegContext` matching `/outcomes/trades` and `/outcomes/ohlc`.

## Why

Third leg of the user-shape trio (`/outcomes/users` rolled-up trading stats, this endpoint for current holdings, `/outcomes/users/activity` for the composition event feed). Covers the canonical "what does this user currently hold?" query without falling back to HL `spotClearinghouseState`.

## Coverage caveat (documented inline)

When the sink has not been backfilled to a block predating the user's earliest activity, the running share-flow sum under-reports by exactly the shares acquired before the backfill horizon. Verified empirically against HL `spotClearinghouseState` — 100% of any gap maps to pre-cutoff events, zero in-window misses. Once dev1 / stage / prod sinks are fully backfilled, this MV is authoritative.

## Code references

- `src/routes/hyperliquid/outcomes_users_positions.ts` — route + Zod schemas
- `src/routes/hyperliquid/outcomes_users_positions.sql` — SQL reading `state_user_outcome_position FINAL` with scoped meta CTEs
- `src/routes/index.ts` — route registration at `/v1/hyperliquid/outcomes/users/positions`

## Depends on

#571 (OutcomeContext refactor — provides `OutcomeLegContext` schema). Already on this branch.

author: atlas-from-plumb
body:
Fixes #30.

## Problem

The gotreesitter topology extractors are syntactic — they have no type information — so they resolve a `calls` edge by callee **name** alone, and `funcIdx` keeps only one index per name. When more than one function/method in a file shares that name (the issue's example: a type with its own `deinit` while a call targets a stdlib `ArenaAllocator.deinit`), a receiver-blind `recv.name()` match resolves to an arbitrary same-named target and the spurious edge was recorded at the full `0.8` heuristic confidence. That inflates the call graph for affected names and can mislead `topology_explore`, `topology_impact`, `topology_affected`, and the reconstructed `call_hierarchy` callees.

## Fix (option 2 from the issue — down-weight ambiguous, no type resolution)

- New shared helpers in `internal/topology/extractors/treesitter/common.go`:
  - `callableNameCounts(nodes)` — counts function/method nodes per `Name` (built once per file, after node collection).
  - `heuristicCallEdge(from, to, nodes, nameCounts)` — builds the `EdgeCalls`; when the target's name is shared by more than one callable, it emits `Confidence: 0.5, Source: "heuristic-ambiguous"` instead of `0.8 / "heuristic"`.
- All eight name-keyed extractors — Zig, Python, Rust, Swift, Java, JavaScript, Kotlin, Bash — now route their call-edge emission through the helper (each gained a `nameCounts` field populated at the top of `callEdges`).
- `KindTest` names are **excluded** from the count: in describe/it/test-style suites a test node's `Name` is its description string (`describe('greet', …)`), not a callable identifier, so counting it would falsely mark a real same-named function ambiguous (this surfaced as a JS test fixture).

`source` is a free-form `TEXT` column and `confidence` a `REAL` (no CHECK constraints), so the new value/weight persist and round-trip safely. Uniquely-named calls are unchanged (`0.8`).

## Scope

Per the issue, **receiver-type-aware resolution** (the full fix) and the **Go `go/ast` extractor** (which has type info) are out of scope. The canonical-grammar **wasmts** TS/TSX/Swift extractor shares the same name-only limitation but lives in a separate package; it is left as a follow-up rather than expanding this PR beyond the issue's stated `treesitter/` scope.

## Tests

- New `TestZig_AmbiguousCallEdgeDownWeighted`: two `deinit` methods + a uniquely-named `cleanup` in one file — the `→deinit` edge is `0.5/heuristic-ambiguous`, the `→cleanup` edge stays `0.8/heuristic`.
- Every existing `Test*_CallEdgeIntraFile` (all eight languages) passes unchanged.

`make build`, full `go test ./...`, and `golangci-lint run ./...` all clean.

body:
Adds `@since X.Y.Z` Doxygen tags to every documented public symbol in `include/jwt.h`, recording the LibJWT version that introduced it. The API has been purely additive since the v3.0.0 reset, so v3.0.0 symbols are `@since 3.0.0` and later additions carry their introducing tag.

Versions were derived by diffing `include/jwt.h` across **every** 3.x tag (v3.0.0–v3.5.0, patch releases included) and cross-checked against the git tag boundaries (present at its tag, absent at the prior tag):

| Category | Count | Versions |
|---|---|---|
| `JWT_EXPORT` functions | 117 | 74 @3.0.0, 2 @3.1.0, 3 @3.2.0, 38 @3.4.0 |
| typedef/enum/struct blocks | 27 | 18 @3.0.0, 9 @3.4.0 |
| `static inline` `*_freep` helpers | 5 | builder/checker/jwks @3.0.0, jwe @3.4.0 |
| `jwt_set_GET/SET_*` macros | 8 | all @3.0.0 |
| late enum members (inline) | 4 | `JWT_ALG_ML_DSA_44/65/87`, `JWK_KEY_TYPE_AKP` @3.5.0 |
| `jwt_long_t` | 1 | @3.2.2 (was undocumented; minimal doc block added) |

Notable: `jwt_long_t` first appeared in the **v3.2.2 patch** release (caught only by scanning every tag, not just minors); `jwt_alg_t`/`jwk_key_type_t` are `@since 3.0.0` while their ML-DSA/AKP members carry inline `@since 3.5.0`.

author: matthieugouel
body:
## What

Removes the PAT (`github_token` + checkout `token:`) from `claude-review.yml` so the auto-review uses the official Claude GitHub App's built-in auth and posts as **`claude[bot]`** instead of under a human avatar.

## Why this is safe here (but not in claude.yml)

The official Claude app uses the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which GitHub blocks from triggering downstream workflows (anti-recursion — see [claude-code-action#319](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/issues/319)). That limitation only matters when Claude *pushes commits / opens PRs*.

- **`claude-review.yml` is comment-only** → never commits → the limitation doesn't apply → dropping the PAT is a free win (`claude[bot]` attribution, no CI tradeoff).
- **`claude.yml` (tag mode) keeps the PAT** → `@claude` can be asked to push code, and those commits must still trigger CI.

Result: auto-reviews post as `claude[bot]`; on-demand `@claude` replies remain under the PAT owner. Intentional split.

`id-token` stays off — the official app path doesn't use OIDC (that's Bedrock/Vertex only).

Closes #55.

## Problem

A reset or app restart could leave a run persisted as `builder_running` while the builder PTY — held only in main's process memory — was gone. No process was building, there was no recovery path, and the handoff pane labeled the sent-but-stale handoff a generic `blocked`.

## What changed

- **Detection (pure + tested):** `evaluateBuilderRecovery(run, hasLiveBuilderSession)` in `run.ts` flags a `builder_running` run with no live builder PTY as stale, with a recovery message that adapts to whether a PR is already bound. Mirrors `evaluateClearRun` — Electron/PTY-free and unit-testable.
- **Visibility:** new IPC `runBuilderRecoveryGet` + pushed `runBuilderRecoveryChanged`, so the cockpit tells a stale builder apart from an actively-running one. Main re-emits when the builder PTY starts/dies and when a `builder_running` run is resumed (#40).
- **Recovery — relaunch & re-deliver:** new `runBuilderRelaunch` is an explicit operator action that relaunches the builder and re-delivers the *existing* pointer-first handoff. It reuses the **same worktree cwd safety gate** as the original send (an isolated run's worktree is re-validated and the PTY launches inside it before any prompt is written) and records the re-delivery on the run's prompt log for audit. The run stays `builder_running`; nothing is auto-relaunched or silently re-sent.
- **Recovery — mark failed:** surfaced via the existing `report_agent_failed` interrupt edge with a recorded reason.
- **UI:** a recovery banner in Run Control ("Relaunch builder & re-send handoff" / "Mark agent failed"); PR discovery stays available and read-only; the Handoff pane no longer shows a bare `blocked` for a sent-but-stale handoff and points at the recovery path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A `builder_running` run whose builder PTY is gone is visibly distinguishable from an actively running builder.
- [x] The UI no longer labels a sent-but-stale handoff only as generic `blocked` without explaining the recovery path.
- [x] The operator can explicitly recover by relaunching/re-sending the handoff or by marking the agent failed.
- [x] Recovery records auditable run/prompt history (prompt-log re-send entry; `report_agent_failed` transition with reason).
- [x] Recovery does not bypass the existing worktree cwd safety gate (relaunch re-validates the worktree and launches the PTY inside it).
- [x] PR discovery remains read-only and available.
- [x] Tests cover resumed/persisted `builder_running` runs with no live PTY.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm test` — 207/207 pass (incl. new `evaluateBuilderRecovery` coverage and the resumed-`builder_running`-with-no-PTY case)
- `npm run build` — clean

author: devantler
body:
## Problem

The `🛡️ Scan for known vulnerabilities` gate is **red on every consumer PR** — including all of `devantler-tech/ksail`'s open PRs. It is **not a finding**; govulncheck itself crashes:

```
panic: ForEachElement called on type containing *types.TypeParam
golang.org/x/vuln/scan.(*Cmd).Wait → internal/scan.RunGovulncheck
##[error]govulncheck failed to run (exit 2) - operational error, not a scan result.
```

`devantler/govulncheck-action` (pinned at `a7e51f7`) installs `govulncheck@latest`, which now resolves to **v1.4.0**. v1.4.0 panics on modules using **generics** under **Go 1.26**. Reproduced locally: v1.4.0 panics (exit 2) on such a module while v1.3.0 completes under the same Go 1.26.4 toolchain — a **v1.4.0 regression**.

## Fix

Bump the `devantler/govulncheck-action` pin `a7e51f7` → **`e92df19`**, which pins the install to `govulncheck@v1.3.0` (last known-good). Updated in lockstep:

- `validate-go-project.yaml` — the real gate.
- `ci.yaml` — the two allowlist self-test scan jobs (`test-govulncheck-allowlist-honored` / `-strict-blocks`) and the `EXPECTED` lockstep guard.

Pairs with **devantler/govulncheck-action#1**. `e92df19` currently lives on that PR's branch (descendant of `feat/allow-file`); it resolves immediately as an immutable commit. After #1 merges into `feat/allow-file`, re-pin to the merged tip if you prefer the SHA to sit on `feat/allow-file` (or merge #1 with rebase/merge-commit to preserve `e92df19`).

## Validation

- Local: `govulncheck@v1.3.0 ./...` runs to completion; `govulncheck@v1.4.0 -format json ./...` panics (exit 2).
- The lockstep self-test (`🔒 Assert the gate pins the self-tested action SHA`) is updated to the new SHA, so the allowlist suite keeps exercising the real gate.

author: bowlesb
body:
## What
The peer-GRAPH relational feature, designed against the v2-gate wall (peer_relative's forward-IC is mostly demean MECHANICS, near-insensitive to clusters). New feature = a graph-WEIGHTED demean: `peerrel_graph(i) = ret_i − Σ_j W(i,j)·ret_j`, W = softmax over top-K embedding-similar peers — strictly richer than the uniform hard-cluster demean. Pre-registered bar (forward-IC, not cohesion; shuffle canary) in `prereg.md`.

## Result — DECISIVE NULL (9.6M rows, 18 OOS days)
| ret/fwd | uniform IC | graph IC | shuffle IC | graph beats uniform? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5m/5m | **−0.01986** | −0.01503 | −0.01567 | NO |
| 5m/30m | **−0.00992** | −0.00721 | −0.00680 | NO |
| 30m/5m | **−0.00853** | −0.00571 | −0.00511 | NO |
| 30m/30m | **−0.00672** | −0.00378 | −0.00136 | NO |

**Graph loses to uniform 4/4 cells** (beats only its shuffle 3/4). Concentrating the demean on similar peers REMOVES forward signal vs flat broad neutralization. Confirms at the deepest level: `peer_relative`'s forward value IS the demean mechanics (neutralization breadth), not relational structure.

## 5-cycle synthesis — GPU-embedding-as-feature hunt EXHAUSTED
repr-2 (cohesion ↑, IC flat) · day-ahead (predictable but already captured by `daily_vol_*d`) · D3 + lead-lag (minute returns null both ways) · peer-graph (relational demean loses to uniform). Across direct prediction AND relational representation, **no GPU embedding beats simple features on forward-IC.** No shippable GPU feature in this space — but the priors are banked and tell the platform where not to look.

## Strategic pivot
Per the Lead: speculative feature-embedding exploration is PAUSED. The 3090's near-term value is the eventual MODEL (lightGBM/NN on the full trusted feature set, cohort grading imminent). `GPU_QUEUE.md` re-ranked: the model is the primary (blocked) job; speculative embeddings retired.

## Artifacts (`experiments/gpu_peergraph/`)
`prereg.md`, `build_graph.py`, `gate.py`, `out/gate_result.json` (load-bearing), `results.md`, graph parquet/npz. Lane never touched the live tree.

author: igorboss
body:
Two FHIR `$expand` conformance bugs found by triaging the tx-ecosystem suite against a running termx (the first (2) findings from the conformance harness).

## 1. POST `$expand` with `url` as `valueUri` → 400
The handler read `url` only as `valueUrl`/`valueString`, so a POSTed `Parameters` carrying `url` as **`valueUri`** (what the FHIR spec & the tx-ecosystem tests send) returned `400 "parameter 'url' or 'valueSet' required"`. Now also accepts `valueUri`/`valueCanonical`. ([ValueSetExpandOperation](terminology/src/main/java/org/termx/terminology/fhir/valueset/operations/ValueSetExpandOperation.java))

## 2. Valueless `expansion.parameter` crashes strict clients
`$expand` echoes request params into `expansion.parameter`, but `expansion.parameter.value` is a **`uri`** — a `url`/`canonical` request param was copied to none of the `value[x]` fields, producing a parameter with a name and **no value**. That's invalid FHIR; the validator NPEs on it. Now folds `url`/`canonical` into `valueUri` and drops any still-valueless parameter. ([ValueSetFhirMapper.toValueSetParameter](terminology/src/main/java/org/termx/terminology/fhir/valueset/ValueSetFhirMapper.java))

## Verified
Re-ran `txTests -suite simple-cases` against a local termx (with fixtures loaded) before/after: requests went **400 → executing → producing correct expansion content** (code1/Display1, total 6). Existing `ValueSetExpandOperationTest` + mapper specs still green.

## Remaining (catalogued, follow-up)
Now that requests execute, the residual diffs are cosmetic/completeness gaps — `$expand` adds a top-level `effectivePeriod` the suite doesn't expect; `$expand` emits an extra `compose.include[].valueSet`; `$lookup` returns fewer parameters than expected. Tractable next steps for the conformance push.

author: zaknafeyn
body:
## Summary

- `await showErrorMessage(...)` was suspending the extension host until the user clicked OK, preventing VS Code from flushing the queued `FETCH_PR_ERROR` webview message
- The button stayed locked while the notification was visible; it only unlocked after the user dismissed the notification
- Replaced `await` with `void` on all three `showErrorMessage` calls in `handleFetchPR` — the catch block now exits immediately after `postFetchPRError`, so VS Code can deliver the webview message before the user interacts with the notification
- `handleInvalidDefaultBranch` is unchanged — it still awaits to detect the "Open Settings" click

## Root cause

VS Code's `webview.postMessage` resolves when the IPC message is *queued*, not when the webview JS has *processed* it. While the extension was suspended waiting for the user to click OK, the pending `FETCH_PR_ERROR` message was not flushed to the webview. Switching to fire-and-forget lets the extension host exit the catch block immediately, unblocking message delivery.

- [x] All 357 unit/integration tests pass (`yarn test`)
- [ ] Manual smoke: fetch a non-existent PR number — button should unlock as soon as the error notification appears, before clicking OK

author: p-l-
body:
Two related result-limit robustness fixes.

1. (backend): WEB_MAXRESULTS could be bypassed by q=limit:0. On the list / distinct routes (view, scans, passive, flow), limit:0 is the 'no client-imposed limit' sentinel -- applied via a streaming 'if flt_params.limit and ...: break' or 'or subdb.no_limit'. get_base did 'min(limit, WEB_MAXRESULTS)', but min(0, MAXRESULTS) == 0, so limit:0 streamed the entire collection past the operator's documented hard cap. Factor _resolve_limit(): None -> WEB_LIMIT; when WEB_MAXRESULTS is set it bounds every request, including limit:0 and any value above it; when unset, limit:0 stays unlimited. (The audit / rir routes already clamp non-positive limits, and dns slices to empty, so they were unaffected -- the fix is in the single shared get_base path.) Documented the cap semantics in config.py.

2. (web-ui): host-list.tsx parsed limit ('rawLimit > 0 ? ...') and skip ('Math.max(0, ... || 0)') with two different ad-hoc idioms. Factor parseUrlInt(params, key, {min, fallback}) in lib/paging.ts and use it for both (limit: min 1; skip: min 0). Behaviour-preserving; unit-tested.

Tests: ResolveLimitTests (no-backend) and parseUrlInt unit tests. Bundle regenerated via pkg/buildwebui.

author: connorshea
body:
This changeset was generated using Claude Code w/ Opus 4.8, but informed by usage in a production Rails app and tested and reviewed by me manually.

There are two changes here.

**collapsing `@value_hash` building**: 

Collapse the `@value_hash` double-build (`Hash[map]` + `merge!(Hash[map])`) into two direct passes over `@values`, preserving the name key collision logic while removing some unnecessary allocation of throwaway intermediate arrays/hashes. 

**string freezing**:

For plain-symbol enums, `value` was a fresh String duplicating the `Value`'s own content, one per value per class. Using `-name.to_s` returns a frozen, deduplicated String, so every value named `active` across the entire app can share a single object. It remains a plain String (not the Value subclass), so it is still safe to feed `write_attribute`. Custom values (e.g. in: `{ admin: 1 }`) are unchanged.

Retained memory drops ~40 B/value with this, and more where value names repeat across models (this should be common in large rails apps especially).

----

### Benchmarking

<details>
<summary>benchmark script</summary>

```rb
# frozen_string_literal: true

# Benchmark for the two "simple" constructor optimizations (the
# value-memory-simple-opts branch), independent of the i18n key caching work:
#
#   * @value_hash built with two direct passes over @values instead of
#     Hash[map] + merge!(Hash[map]) — drops the throwaway intermediate arrays
#     and hash (a construction-time allocation win).
#   * @value deduped via -name.to_s for plain-symbol enums — every value named
#     e.g. "active" across the whole app shares one frozen String instead of a
#     fresh String per value per class (a retained-memory win).
#
# Both changes live in Attribute#initialize / Value#initialize, so there is no
# clean way to A/B them inside one process. Instead, run this SAME script twice
# and compare the printed numbers:
#
#   git checkout master                  && ruby -Ilib benchmark/simple_opts_benchmark.rb
#   git checkout value-memory-simple-opts && ruby -Ilib benchmark/simple_opts_benchmark.rb
#
# #text is never called here, so the i18n path is not exercised — this isolates
# the constructor cost.

$LOAD_PATH.unshift File.expand_path('../lib', __dir__)
require 'enumerize'
require 'objspace'

# Six value names that recur across every class, the realistic case the string
# dedup targets (active/pending/... appear on many models).
NAMES = %i[active inactive pending archived deleted suspended].freeze

def new_attr_class
  Class.new do
    extend Enumerize
    enumerize :status, in: NAMES
  end
end

# 1. Objects allocated to define one attribute (class + enumerize + 6 values),
#    averaged over many reps — the construction cost the @value_hash change cuts.
def construct_allocs(reps)
  GC.start
  GC.disable
  start = GC.stat(:total_allocated_objects)
  reps.times { new_attr_class }
  allocs = GC.stat(:total_allocated_objects) - start
  GC.enable
  allocs.to_f / reps
end

# 2. Retained memory for many classes that share the same value names — what the
#    string dedup shrinks.
def retained_bytes(count)
  GC.start
  before = ObjectSpace.memsize_of_all
  store = Array.new(count) { new_attr_class }
  GC.start
  after = ObjectSpace.memsize_of_all
  store.clear
  after - before
end

REPS  = 2_000
COUNT = 5_000

allocs       = construct_allocs(REPS)
mem          = retained_bytes(COUNT)
values_total = COUNT * NAMES.size

puts "Ruby #{RUBY_VERSION}"
puts "Objects allocated defining one attribute : #{format('%.1f', allocs)}"
puts "Retained memory, #{values_total} values (KB)  : #{format('%.1f', mem / 1024.0)}"
puts "Retained memory per value (B)            : #{format('%.1f', mem.to_f / values_total)}"
```

</details>

`@value_hash` two-pass build + `-name.to_s` string dedup, measured by defining 5,000 classes whose six enum value names recur across all of them (the realistic case dedup targets). Whole-class construction, `#text` never called.

| Metric | Master (before) | Simple opts (after) | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Objects allocated defining one attribute | 233.4 | 218.4 | **−15 objects (−6.4%)** |
| Retained memory, 30k values (shared names) | 21,876 KB | 20,705 KB | **−5.4%** |
| Retained memory per value | 746.7 B | 706.7 B | **−40.0 B/value** |

This isn't a massive win, but it does optimize things with no real downside that I can see.

First of the EverArcade prover additions. The other 3 they need already ship — this is the genuine new one.

**`prove_resource_conservation`**: accept ⟹ persisted `resource' <= resource_old + MINT` (HookState resource counter; MINT = a declared per-tx mint cap, 0 if no MINT param = pure conservation). The **dual of `prove_monotonic`** (never moves *down*) — this proves an in-world resource never moves *up* beyond a declared mint (no infinite-inflation / dupe). Distinct from `prove_conservation` (emitted XRP ≤ incoming; here the conserved thing is *state*).

Fail-closed on unconditional-write / width-mismatch / unsupported / unknown. 143 tests pass.

author: jbailes
body:
First webchat-git **route** WP. `POST /v1/workspace/clone {url, name?}` — a webchat user clones a repo as a project under their **own** isolated workspace.

## Security
- Caller identity = the attested **`server.token`-gated `X-Aimee-Webuser`** principal (new `server_http_identity_principal()` accessor), **not** the body → a user can only clone into their own `webusers/<name>/` tree.
- Dest resolved + validated by `workspace_scope` (cross-tenant escape + existing-project rejected).
- Git creds injected from the user's **sealed vault** (WP-C) into the git child env only — never accepted in the body.
- `git clone -- url dest` via `safe_exec_capture_env` (**no shell** → no command injection; `--` → no flag injection); URL rejected if empty/flag-like/control-char.

## Surface
- `git_project` core module (name derivation + clone) — unit-tested independently.
- `rh_workspace_clone` route (`CAP_TOOL_EXECUTE`); cloned project `index_scan_project`'d (agent-searchable).
- openapi `/workspace/clone` documented (`server-api-conformance-check` green).

## Test
`unit-test-git-project` uses a real **`file://`** clone (no network/creds): name derivation + `.git` stripping, files land in the user's scope, re-clone refused (exists), **cross-principal** scoping, and refusals (non-webuser, empty URL, **flag-like URL `--upload-pack=…`**, escaping name). Passes locally.

Builds on WP-A/B/L/C (merged). Default-safe (new route gated on a webuser principal).

author: jung-thomas
body:
Hotfix to PR #387 — caught on first DEV deploy.

```
SQL Error 259: Could not find table/view com_sap_developers_ims_Advocates
Query: SELECT "ID" FROM "com_sap_developers_ims_Advocates" WHERE LOWER("slug") = ?
```

HDI deploys tables and columns with HANA's default UPPERCASE folding. Quoted lowercase identifiers in raw SQL fail because HANA preserves the literal case. The unit suite uses CDS QL on SQLite (which CAP rewrites correctly), so the bug was invisible until the deployed CF instance hit `/api/advocates/:slug/photo`.

Verified actual HANA shape via `SELECT TABLE_NAME FROM TABLES`:
- `COM_SAP_DEVELOPERS_IMS_ADVOCATES`
- `COM_SAP_DEVELOPERS_IMS_ADVOCATEPHOTOS`
- Columns: `PHOTO256`, `PHOTO64`, `PHOTOMIMETYPE`, `SHA256`, `ADVOCATE_ID` (all UPPERCASE)

**Fix**: switch the two raw-SQL queries in `fetchPhoto()` to unquoted UPPERCASE identifiers (HANA's native form). Same pattern as the existing `srv/lib/content-store.js` workaround.

**Hybrid test** (test/hybrid/advocates-photo-hana.test.js) is gated on `ALLOW_HYBRID_WRITES=true` + `cf login` so it never runs in CI. That's the gap that let this through. Worth a follow-up to either run hybrid in CI or to wire a unit-level mock that exercises the HANA branch.

38/38 unit tests still green.

## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

I've seen people asking from time to time why EditorUndoRedoManager does not support Callables, like UndoRedo. The answer is always that live editing expects a regular callables, hence the API does not allow anything fancy.
However there are some use-cases where you don't really care about live editing, or just using a custom callable is easier.

This PR adds a new method to EditorUndoRedoManager that allows adding operations which are explicitly excluded from all UndoRedo hooks. Meaning the editor will not try to send the Callable to running project, so you can use any Callable, even ones that aren't supported.

author: eman-cickusic
body:
## Summary

Add the project's first CI: a GitHub Actions workflow that validates every PR description against a required structure, plus a matching PR template.

## Motivation

PRs are frequently opened with vague or missing descriptions, which makes review and history hard to follow. This enforces a minimum quality bar automatically so reviewers always get the context they need.

## Changes

- `.github/scripts/validate-pr-body.py` — stdlib-only validator. Reads the PR body from `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` and requires six `##` sections (Summary, Motivation, Changes, Validation, Risk, Rollout and Recovery) with real content. Rejects placeholders (TBD/TODO/N/A/None/bare dashes) and requires at least one checked command checkbox in Validation. Prints an itemized list of every problem on failure.
- `.github/workflows/pr-description-check.yml` — runs on `pull_request` (opened, edited, synchronize) on Python 3.11.
- `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` — scaffold with the six sections so contributors pass on the first try.

## Validation

- [x] `python -m py_compile .github/scripts/validate-pr-body.py`
- [x] `python test_validate_pr.py` (8 fixtures: valid, missing sections, placeholders-only, unchecked validation, no-backtick command, blank template, empty body, any-order with `&` — all pass)

## Risk

Low. Touches CI only; no application or runtime code changes. Worst case the check is misconfigured and reports incorrectly — it never blocks merges unless branch protection is set to require it.

## Rollout and Recovery

Merges to `main` and applies to all subsequent PRs. To make it blocking, mark the "Validate PR description" check as required in branch protection. To roll back, revert this PR or delete `.github/workflows/pr-description-check.yml`.
